What happened. 4 rewrites measured (Pass 1, Pass 2, Pass 3, Pass 4); kept: Pass 3 (the lowest area x delay, a later rewrite having to beat it by more than 9.41%). Loop stopped by: no gain beyond noise (gain -115.48% against Pass 3, min-gain 0.0941 (baseline adw_reg_seed_spread_frac)).

Result. Area x delay -76.30% against the unmodified design on the same layout (koios_small, 140 x 140): 2.67744e+08 vs 1.12977e+09 (baseline: median per term over the entry's seed runs (its seed_medians; seeds lists them)); verification: not recorded in the run record.

Mode contract

recorded (outcome.json contract field)

Verbatim, as recorded with the run and sent to the agents.

- primitive to instantiate: `int_sop_4` (precision INT9)
- computes: out = ax*ay + bx*by + cx*cy + dx*dy + chainin
- input ports: clk[1] (clock), reset[1], mode_sigs[12], ax[9], ay[9], bx[9], by[9], cx[9], cy[9], dx[9], dy[9], chainin[64]
- output ports: result[64], chainout[64]
- arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 64 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 64 bits (modulo 2^64), with no saturation and no flag.
- registers: on `clk`, the block registers its operands (`ax`, `ay`, `bx`, `by`, `cx`, `cy`, `dx`, `dy`) at one clock edge and `result` at the next, with the arithmetic between the two registers: operands applied before clock edge k appear in `result` after edge k+1, 2 cycles later. The block has no clock enable and no path around either register. `chainin` is registered at the block's entry like an operand and reaches `result` 2 cycles after it is applied. `chainout` is combinational from the input registers: it carries the value `result` loads at the next clock edge, one cycle before `result` shows it.
- reset: `reset` is synchronous and active high: at a clock edge that samples it high it clears every register of the block (the operand registers, the chainin register and the result register) to 0, and the block loads again at the next edge that samples it low.
- power-up: every register of the block is unknown until the first clear by `reset`; no register of the block has an initial value, and a rewrite may not rely on one.
- tie-off: `chainin` = 0 when the block is not chained (a dedicated chain input: only another block's `chainout` or a constant may drive it); `mode_sigs` = 0 always (the architecture gives the port no meaning for this mode).
- connections: connect every input port, by the port names above; a product-term port the rewrite does not use is tied to 0. `chainout` reaches only the next block's `chainin`, through a dedicated connection to the block directly below it in the column; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it.

Task

You are the planner. Read the design source, stereovision2.v, and decide which of the candidate arithmetic regions listed below to rewrite onto the hard block described next, or that none should be rewritten. Write a plan for the editor, who carries it out; do not edit any file.

The design

Baseline: the unmodified stereovision2 under this run's VPR settings (channel width 300, median of five seeds, 1 to 5) has a worst register-to-register path of 11.6069 ns on its one clock tm3_clk_v0 (I/O pads not timed) and uses 224 DSP tiles (as packed at seed 1) of the device's 306. Its used logic-block area is 9.73358e+07 minimum-width transistor areas (one DSP tile 253779, one cluster 27905) and its routed wirelength is 436921, so its area x delay x wirelength product, the objective, is 4.93619e+14. Its slowest stage (read off the seed-1 timing report) is in my_fir_f1: one hard multiply on a DSP tile (two_mult_18x19), then six adder levels with their carry chains, then one LUT, into an enabled flip-flop. The next slowest stage (read off the seed-1 timing report), in my_fir_f2 (endpoint group $dffe~642, not path 1's $dffe~456), is the same shape as path 1, one hard multiply on a DSP tile, six adder levels with their carry chains, one LUT, into an enabled flip-flop, 11.293 ns, so shortening the slowest stage past that point buys nothing on its own. Any path your rewrite creates is compared against that critical path.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Cost (guidance: go against it only with a reason in the plan)
  • The clock period is the delay of the slowest stage (the logic between one register and the next). A rewrite that does not touch the slowest stage should not be expected to make the design faster, and should not make another stage slower than it.
  • Blocks in series are separate stages. A path through chainout starts at an input register and continues, in the same stage, into what it drives.
  • Moving or adding registers changes stage lengths and when values arrive.
  • Area falls when soft adders and flip-flops move into blocks.
  • A block of this mode takes a DSP tile alone. Synthesis may already have placed the design's multiplies on tiles, so a block that only replaces one saves little: count tiles against the baseline.
  • The block has chain ports: a block's chainout can drive the next block's chainin directly, so a sum can continue from block to block.
Objective

Minimize area × delay × wirelength against the baseline. If you expect no rewrite to lower it, output TIER: NONE. Among rewrites that lower it, choose the one that lowers it most.

Output
Tiers
  • T1: The block replaces the region's arithmetic as it stands: the same operations on the same operands, now inside the block.
  • T2: The region's arithmetic is regrouped to fit the block (products regrouped into the block's sums, registers moved), computing the same values.
  • NONE: No rewrite: no candidate can be rewritten correctly.
Header

Write exactly this header, each key at the start of its own line, then the plan:

TIER: <exactly one of T1, T2, NONE>
REGIONS: <the converted candidate ids, comma-separated; NONE when TIER is NONE>
SHARED_REDUCTION: <the signal or module the converted products are summed in; NONE for a single region>
BLOCKS: <how many blocks the rewrite instantiates, one integer>
TILES: <how many DSP tiles the whole design then uses, one integer>
STAGE_NS: <the delay of the slowest stage the rewrite leaves, in ns, one number>
MAPPING: <which design signals go to which block ports>
PLAN: <the plan, stating everything listed below>

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds, and how many DSP tiles the design then uses.
  • The longest series of blocks in any stage and its delay, against the slowest stage.
  • What soft logic leaves which stage, and whether that stage is the slowest.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output rules
  • Write nothing before the TIER line; read the source first.
  • A reviewer checks the plan automatically and no person reads it, so do not end with a question or an offer.
  • If a change to the design itself, not to the rewrite, would let more of it use the block, you may say so on a line starting DESIGN_CHANGE:. It is reported to the user and does not change your decision.
Reference simulation

After the edit, the framework simulates the edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output on every cycle. A candidate that does not match is not measured. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (int_sop_4.v) are in sim_reference/.

PLAN:

What is converted. All 46 fltr_compute candidate ids (every product of fltr_compute_f1, f2, f3, h1, h2, h3, h4), each id with its 6 instances — 42 module instances in total, one int_sop_4 each, 42 blocks.

What is left, and why. All 45 my_fir candidate ids (my_fir_f1, f2, f3, h1, h2, h3, h4 — the modules that hold the design's two slowest stages) are left, for three reasons that apply to every one of them:

  • Operand width: din is 16 bits (WIDTH_5B, line 1460) and the coefficients are up to 255, so a product does not fit the 9-bit ports. Each product would need two slots (low byte, high byte) plus an external <<8 add, i.e. 4 blocks per my_fir instance, 168 blocks — past the 306-tile device once the rest of the design is counted, and the shift-add would sit on the critical stage.
  • Registers: the sum is loaded into dout by a clock-enabled register (if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1), lines 1476/1486 and the same in the other six) with 0 register stages between the products and the sum, and din (a fltr_compute output) changes on every cycle, not only on enabled cycles. The block has a fixed 2-cycle latency and no clock enable, so its result for din(k) is available one cycle after dout must take it; the only ways out delay dout (and hence my_fir_rdy/vidin_out_reg_*/the bus words) by whole cycles, which the cycle-by-cycle testbench would reject.
  • Those two together mean no correct rewrite of my_fir exists here, so the design's 11.6069 ns stage stays as it is and the rewrite is an area/wirelength rewrite.

Why T2. Each fltr_compute sum is symmetric: c1=c7, c2=c6, c3=c5 in all seven modules. The seven (or six) products are regrouped by the distributive law into four: (d1+d7)*c1 + (d2+d6)*c2 + (d3+d5)*c3 + d4*c4, which is one block instead of two. The regrouping is exact, not approximate: each operand byte is ≤255, so each pre-add is ≤510 and passes through a 9-bit port without truncation; every original product is below 2^17 (largest: 255*364 = 92820 in f3, 255*324 = 82620 in h4, 255*277 = 70635 in f1), so the original 17-bit q registers never truncate and Σq is unchanged by the folding; the folded products are ≤510*364 = 185640 < 2^18 and the whole sum is ≤255*1126 = 287130 < 2^19, so nothing wraps in the block either.

Reproducing the design's sign extension. The design adds {q[16],q[16],q[16],q}, i.e. it reads each 17-bit product as signed, so d_out_tmp = (Σq + 917504·C) mod 2^20 where C counts the products with bit 16 set. For f2, h1, h2, h3 no product can reach 2^16 (largest 255*255 = 65025, 255*193 = 49215, 255*147 = 37485), so C = 0 and dout <= result[18:3] is exact. For f1, f3, h4 exactly one coefficient can push a product past 2^16, so the editor adds a comparator and two 1-bit (f3: 2-bit) pipeline registers and corrects the block's result:

  • f1: C = (din[31:24] >= 8'd237) (277*236 = 65372, 277*237 = 65649)
  • h4: C = (din[31:24] >= 8'd203) (324*202 = 65448, 324*203 = 65772)
  • f3: C = (din[39:32] >= 8'd181) + (din[23:16] >= 8'd181) (364*180 = 65520, 364*181 = 65884), C in 0..2
    and d_out_tmp = result[19:0] + (C==0 ? 20'd0 : C==1 ? 20'd917504 : 20'd786432); dout <= d_out_tmp[18:3]; (786432 = 2*917504 mod 2^20). The correction logic sits between the block's result register and the existing dout register, a stage with about 9 ns of slack; nothing is added after dout, so the my_fir stages that read dout are untouched. No ASSUMES: line is needed — every bound above follows from the 8-bit slices and the literal coefficients.

Reset. reset is tied to 1'b0 on every block. The design's own reset (active low, line 203) clears only video_state, tm3_sram_adsp, horiz and vert; q, d_out_tmp and dout in fltr_compute have no reset and keep running through a reset pulse. Driving the block's reset from the design's reset would zero the filter pipeline on every mid-run reset pulse while the reference keeps computing, and the difference reaches bus_word_3..6_2to1 through h_fltr and port_bus_2to1 — so the block must never be cleared. With reset low the block's registers load every cycle, so their power-up X flushes in two cycles exactly as the reference's own unreset q/d_out_tmp X flushes in three; both sides are X on the same cycles (the fifos hold X far into the lead-in anyway) and the testbench's !== compare accepts X against X. No added register is relied on for an initial value: the pre-adds are combinational and the two correction registers load unconditionally every cycle.

Register stages, per converted region (all 46 ids behave alike). Before: operand byte -> q register (stage 1, the "products registered 1 stage before the sum" of the table) -> d_out_tmp register after the 6-level (5-level where c4 = 0) adder chain (stage 2) -> dout (stage 3). After: operand byte -> soft pre-add (combinational) -> block input registers (stage 1) -> block result register (stage 2) -> dout (stage 3). Three stages before and after, so dout changes on exactly the same cycle as in the baseline; the only register that moves is q, which becomes the block's input register, and d_out_tmp, which becomes the block's result register.

Soft logic removed, and from which stage. The 20-bit adder chain (6 levels in f1/f2/h2/h4, 5 in f3/h1/h3, about 120 and 100 BLEs) and the 20-bit d_out_tmp register leave the stage from the q registers to d_out_tmp. That stage is not the design's slowest: its delay is roughly 0.060 + 0.96 + 6*1.069 ≈ 7.5 ns against the 11.6069 ns my_fir_f1 stage, so removing it buys no clock period, only area and wirelength — this rewrite is taken for the area×wirelength factors, with the period held fixed. Added back per instance: three 9-bit pre-adders (~27 BLEs) in the stage from the buff_out registers to the block, plus at most 4 BLEs of comparator/correction. Net about -90 BLEs per instance, ~-3500 BLEs ≈ -350 clusters ≈ -9.7e6 area, on top of the DSP change.

Blocks and tiles. 42 blocks added (one per fltr_compute instance), each alone on a DSP tile. They replace 276 mult_9x9_fixed_pt multiplies that sit four to a tile, including the 57 tiles that hold only these; 224 - 57 + 42 = 209 tiles, and as low as about 197 if the packer also consolidates the tiles these products shared. DSP tile count therefore falls against the 224-tile baseline rather than rising, which is why folding to one block per sum is preferred over the straightforward two-block (4+3) split: that split would need 84 blocks (251 tiles), 42 extra chain pairs or a kept soft adder, and one-cycle operand-skew registers.

Longest series of blocks in any stage. One. No block drives another: chainin is tied to 0 and chainout is left unconnected on all 42 blocks, because a folded sum needs only four products. The rewrite's own stages are: buff_out register -> pre-adder -> block input register, ≈0.060 + 0.960 + 1.069 + 1.419 + 0.019 = 3.53 ns on medians (≈5.34 ns on the slowest samples); inside the block, 0.060 + 2.140 + 0.019 = 2.219 ns; block result register -> (correction LUT) -> dout, ≈1.1 ns, ≈2.2 ns with the correction. All far below the 11.6069 ns my_fir_f1 stage and below the 11.293 ns my_fir_f2 stage, so the slowest stage the rewrite leaves is the untouched 11.6069 ns one. dout stays a soft flip-flop with the same fanout, so the stage that starts at it (the critical one) keeps its shape exactly.

Editor notes. Edit only the seven fltr_compute_* module bodies (lines 841-1076); the 6 v_fltr instances pick the change up through the instantiations at lines 706-712, 765-771 and 824-830, and nothing else in the design is touched. Instantiate int_sop_4 by name with named port connections and do not add a definition for it (the model in sim_reference/int_sop_4.v is supplied). Keep the module port list, dout's reg [15:0] declaration and the always @(posedge clk) block; delete q1..q7 and d_out_tmp's register declaration. Pattern (f1 shown; the other six differ only in the coefficients, in the tie-off of dx/dy where c4 = 0, and in the presence/width of the correction):

wire [8:0] s1 = din[55:48] + din[7:0];
wire [8:0] s2 = din[47:40] + din[15:8];
wire [8:0] s3 = din[39:32] + din[23:16];

DESIGN_CHANGE: fltr_compute_f2 (lines 889-898) and fltr_compute_h2 (lines 992-1001) are the same filter on the same din in every v_fltr instance, so vidin_out_f2 and vidin_out_h2 are always equal; computing one of them once per v_fltr would drop 6 of the 42 blocks and 6 sets of pre-adders. 1	// int_sop_4: result = ax*ay + bx*by + cx*cy + dx*dy + chainin, unsigned, each 9x9 product
2	// zero-extended into a 64-bit sum, modulo 2^64 (the sum wraps at the result width).
3	// Ports: clk, reset, mode_sigs[12], ax, ay, bx, by, cx, cy, dx, dy [9 each], chainin[64] in;
4	// result[64], chainout[64] out. mode_sigs is not read.
5	// Registers (the arch's annotation read literally, decision 2026-10-16): every input is registered
6	// at the block's entry at one clock edge (the eight operands and chainin alike); the
7	// products and their sum are formed from those registers and loaded into result at the next edge.
8	// Cycles: every operand and chainin to result 2. chainout is combinational from the input
9	// registers: the sum result loads at the next edge unless that edge clears it (1 cycle from the
10	// inputs).
11	// Reset: synchronous, active high (2026-10-17: the arch's annotation does not distinguish a reset
12	// register from a clear sampled by the registers themselves): at a clock edge that samples it high
13	// every register of the block (operand registers, chainin register, result) is cleared to 0; the block
14	// loads again at the next edge that samples it low. No register has an initial value: every one is
15	// X until the first clear.
16	module int_sop_4 (
17	    input clk,
18	    input reset,
19	    input [11:0] mode_sigs,
20	    input [8:0] ax, input [8:0] ay,
21	    input [8:0] bx, input [8:0] by,
22	    input [8:0] cx, input [8:0] cy,
23	    input [8:0] dx, input [8:0] dy,
24	    input [63:0] chainin,
25	    output reg [63:0] result,
26	    output [63:0] chainout
27	);
28	
29	    // stage 1: the input registers
30	    reg [8:0]  ax_reg, ay_reg, bx_reg, by_reg, cx_reg, cy_reg, dx_reg, dy_reg;
31	    reg [63:0] chainin_reg;
32	
33	    // combinational middle: the four products and their sum, from the registers
34	    wire [17:0] prod_a = ax_reg * ay_reg;                        // 9x9 -> 18, exact
35	    wire [17:0] prod_b = bx_reg * by_reg;
36	    wire [17:0] prod_c = cx_reg * cy_reg;
37	    wire [17:0] prod_d = dx_reg * dy_reg;
38	    wire [63:0] sum    = prod_a + prod_b + prod_c + prod_d + chainin_reg;   // modulo 2^64
39	
40	    always @(posedge clk) begin
41	        if (reset) begin
42	            result <= 0;
43	            ax_reg <= 0; ay_reg <= 0; bx_reg <= 0; by_reg <= 0;
44	            cx_reg <= 0; cy_reg <= 0; dx_reg <= 0; dy_reg <= 0; chainin_reg <= 0;
45	        end
46	        else begin
47	            ax_reg <= ax; ay_reg <= ay; bx_reg <= bx; by_reg <= by;
48	            cx_reg <= cx; cy_reg <= cy; dx_reg <= dx; dy_reg <= dy; chainin_reg <= chainin;
49	            result <= sum;                                       // stage 2
50	        end
51	    end
52	
53	    assign chainout = sum;                                  // the sum of the input registers
54	
55	endmodule

  • input ports: clk[1] (clock), reset[1], mode_sigs[12], ax[9], ay[9], bx[9], by[9], cx[9], cy[9], dx[9], dy[9], chainin[64]
  • output ports: result[64], chainout[64]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 64 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 64 bits (modulo 2^64), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: on clk, the block registers its operands (ax, ay, bx, by, cx, cy, dx, dy) at one clock edge and result at the next, with the arithmetic between the two registers: operands applied before clock edge k appear in result after edge k+1, 2 cycles later. The block has no clock enable and no path around either register. chainin is registered at the block's entry like an operand and reaches result 2 cycles after it is applied. chainout is combinational from the input registers: it carries the value result loads at the next clock edge, one cycle before result shows it.
  • reset: reset is synchronous and active high: at a clock edge that samples it high it clears every register of the block (the operand registers, the chainin register and the result register) to 0, and the block loads again at the next edge that samples it low.
  • power-up: every register of the block is unknown until the first clear by reset; no register of the block has an initial value, and a rewrite may not rely on one.
  • tie-off: chainin = 0 when the block is not chained (a dedicated chain input: only another block's chainout or a constant may drive it); mode_sigs = 0 always (the architecture gives the port no meaning for this mode).
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above; a product-term port the rewrite does not use is tied to 0. chainout reaches only the next block's chainin, through a dedicated connection to the block directly below it in the column; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it.
The design

The design source is stereovision2.v. The candidate regions the planner was offered:

An id names a product by its module and its multiply. One that ends in (sum_in=<module>) is a product whose sum sits in that other module: the product leaves its own module through a port and is added there, so the arithmetic to convert spans both. A #1, #2 after an id separates instances of the same product that sit in sums of different shapes.

In every row, operation: sop.
In every row, instances: 6.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Check
  • Every claim the plan makes about the design (who reads a value, a register's reset or enable, widths, cited lines, ASSUMES lines) against the source.
  • That the mapping as described keeps the same behavior.
  • That the plan states everything the planner's output section requires, listed below.

Do not judge cost or style; measurement decides cost.

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds, and how many DSP tiles the design then uses.
  • The longest series of blocks in any stage and its delay, against the slowest stage.
  • What soft logic leaves which stage, and whether that stage is the slowest.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output
  • First line exactly APPROVE or REVISE.
  • If REVISE, for each problem: the rule it violates or the required item it omits, by name; the design lines; what to change.
  • Write nothing before the verdict line; read the source first. The verdict is applied automatically and no person reads it, so do not end with a question or an offer.

SHARED_REDUCTION: d_out_tmp of each fltr_compute_{f1,f2,f3,h1,h2,h3,h4} instance (seven reductions per v_fltr, 42 reductions over the 6 v_fltr instances; one block per reduction)
BLOCKS: 42
TILES: 209
STAGE_NS: 11.6069
MAPPING: per fltr_compute instance, with din = {buff_out1..buff_out7} so d1=din[55:48], d2=din[47:40], d3=din[39:32], d4=din[31:24], d5=din[23:16], d6=din[15:8], d7=din[7:0], and the three 9-bit soft pre-adds s1=d1+d7, s2=d2+d6, s3=d3+d5: ax=s1, ay=c1, bx=s2, by=c2, cx=s3, cy=c3, dx={1'b0,d4}, dy=c4; clk=clk (tm3_clk_v0), reset=1'b0, mode_sigs=12'd0, chainin=64'd0, chainout left unconnected; dout is loaded from result (see PLAN). Coefficients (c1,c2,c3,c4): f1 = (29,101,17,277); f2 = (4,42,163,255); f3 = (20,179,364, dx=9'd0/dy=9'd0); h1 = (17,25,193, dx=9'd0/dy=9'd0); h2 = (4,42,163,255); h3 = (23,72,147, dx=9'd0/dy=9'd0); h4 = (14,43,80,324).

PLAN:

What is converted. All 46 fltr_compute candidate ids (every product of fltr_compute_f1, f2, f3, h1, h2, h3, h4), each id with its 6 instances — 42 module instances in total, one int_sop_4 each, 42 blocks.

What is left, and why. All 45 my_fir candidate ids (my_fir_f1, f2, f3, h1, h2, h3, h4 — the modules that hold the design's two slowest stages) are left, for three reasons that apply to every one of them:

  • Operand width: din is 16 bits (WIDTH_5B, line 1460) and the coefficients are up to 255, so a product does not fit the 9-bit ports. Each product would need two slots (low byte, high byte) plus an external <<8 add, i.e. 4 blocks per my_fir instance, 168 blocks — past the 306-tile device once the rest of the design is counted, and the shift-add would sit on the critical stage.
  • Registers: the sum is loaded into dout by a clock-enabled register (if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1), lines 1476/1486 and the same in the other six) with 0 register stages between the products and the sum, and din (a fltr_compute output) changes on every cycle, not only on enabled cycles. The block has a fixed 2-cycle latency and no clock enable, so its result for din(k) is available one cycle after dout must take it; the only ways out delay dout (and hence my_fir_rdy/vidin_out_reg_*/the bus words) by whole cycles, which the cycle-by-cycle testbench would reject.
  • Those two together mean no correct rewrite of my_fir exists here, so the design's 11.6069 ns stage stays as it is and the rewrite is an area/wirelength rewrite.

Why T2. Each fltr_compute sum is symmetric: c1=c7, c2=c6, c3=c5 in all seven modules. The seven (or six) products are regrouped by the distributive law into four: (d1+d7)*c1 + (d2+d6)*c2 + (d3+d5)*c3 + d4*c4, which is one block instead of two. The regrouping is exact, not approximate: each operand byte is ≤255, so each pre-add is ≤510 and passes through a 9-bit port without truncation; every original product is below 2^17 (largest: 255*364 = 92820 in f3, 255*324 = 82620 in h4, 255*277 = 70635 in f1), so the original 17-bit q registers never truncate and Σq is unchanged by the folding; the folded products are ≤510*364 = 185640 < 2^18 and the whole sum is ≤255*1126 = 287130 < 2^19, so nothing wraps in the block either.

Reproducing the design's sign extension. The design adds {q[16],q[16],q[16],q}, i.e. it reads each 17-bit product as signed, so d_out_tmp = (Σq + 917504·C) mod 2^20 where C counts the products with bit 16 set. For f2, h1, h2, h3 no product can reach 2^16 (largest 255*255 = 65025, 255*193 = 49215, 255*147 = 37485), so C = 0 and dout <= result[18:3] is exact. For f1, f3, h4 exactly one coefficient can push a product past 2^16, so the editor adds a comparator and two 1-bit (f3: 2-bit) pipeline registers and corrects the block's result:

  • f1: C = (din[31:24] >= 8'd237) (277*236 = 65372, 277*237 = 65649)
  • h4: C = (din[31:24] >= 8'd203) (324*202 = 65448, 324*203 = 65772)
  • f3: C = (din[39:32] >= 8'd181) + (din[23:16] >= 8'd181) (364*180 = 65520, 364*181 = 65884), C in 0..2
    and d_out_tmp = result[19:0] + (C==0 ? 20'd0 : C==1 ? 20'd917504 : 20'd786432); dout <= d_out_tmp[18:3]; (786432 = 2*917504 mod 2^20). The correction logic sits between the block's result register and the existing dout register, a stage with about 9 ns of slack; nothing is added after dout, so the my_fir stages that read dout are untouched. No ASSUMES: line is needed — every bound above follows from the 8-bit slices and the literal coefficients.

Reset. reset is tied to 1'b0 on every block. The design's own reset (active low, line 203) clears only video_state, tm3_sram_adsp, horiz and vert; q, d_out_tmp and dout in fltr_compute have no reset and keep running through a reset pulse. Driving the block's reset from the design's reset would zero the filter pipeline on every mid-run reset pulse while the reference keeps computing, and the difference reaches bus_word_3..6_2to1 through h_fltr and port_bus_2to1 — so the block must never be cleared. With reset low the block's registers load every cycle, so their power-up X flushes in two cycles exactly as the reference's own unreset q/d_out_tmp X flushes in three; both sides are X on the same cycles (the fifos hold X far into the lead-in anyway) and the testbench's !== compare accepts X against X. No added register is relied on for an initial value: the pre-adds are combinational and the two correction registers load unconditionally every cycle.

Register stages, per converted region (all 46 ids behave alike). Before: operand byte -> q register (stage 1, the "products registered 1 stage before the sum" of the table) -> d_out_tmp register after the 6-level (5-level where c4 = 0) adder chain (stage 2) -> dout (stage 3). After: operand byte -> soft pre-add (combinational) -> block input registers (stage 1) -> block result register (stage 2) -> dout (stage 3). Three stages before and after, so dout changes on exactly the same cycle as in the baseline; the only register that moves is q, which becomes the block's input register, and d_out_tmp, which becomes the block's result register.

Soft logic removed, and from which stage. The 20-bit adder chain (6 levels in f1/f2/h2/h4, 5 in f3/h1/h3, about 120 and 100 BLEs) and the 20-bit d_out_tmp register leave the stage from the q registers to d_out_tmp. That stage is not the design's slowest: its delay is roughly 0.060 + 0.96 + 6*1.069 ≈ 7.5 ns against the 11.6069 ns my_fir_f1 stage, so removing it buys no clock period, only area and wirelength — this rewrite is taken for the area×wirelength factors, with the period held fixed. Added back per instance: three 9-bit pre-adders (~27 BLEs) in the stage from the buff_out registers to the block, plus at most 4 BLEs of comparator/correction. Net about -90 BLEs per instance, ~-3500 BLEs ≈ -350 clusters ≈ -9.7e6 area, on top of the DSP change.

Blocks and tiles. 42 blocks added (one per fltr_compute instance), each alone on a DSP tile. They replace 276 mult_9x9_fixed_pt multiplies that sit four to a tile, including the 57 tiles that hold only these; 224 - 57 + 42 = 209 tiles, and as low as about 197 if the packer also consolidates the tiles these products shared. DSP tile count therefore falls against the 224-tile baseline rather than rising, which is why folding to one block per sum is preferred over the straightforward two-block (4+3) split: that split would need 84 blocks (251 tiles), 42 extra chain pairs or a kept soft adder, and one-cycle operand-skew registers.

Longest series of blocks in any stage. One. No block drives another: chainin is tied to 0 and chainout is left unconnected on all 42 blocks, because a folded sum needs only four products. The rewrite's own stages are: buff_out register -> pre-adder -> block input register, ≈0.060 + 0.960 + 1.069 + 1.419 + 0.019 = 3.53 ns on medians (≈5.34 ns on the slowest samples); inside the block, 0.060 + 2.140 + 0.019 = 2.219 ns; block result register -> (correction LUT) -> dout, ≈1.1 ns, ≈2.2 ns with the correction. All far below the 11.6069 ns my_fir_f1 stage and below the 11.293 ns my_fir_f2 stage, so the slowest stage the rewrite leaves is the untouched 11.6069 ns one. dout stays a soft flip-flop with the same fanout, so the stage that starts at it (the critical one) keeps its shape exactly.

Editor notes. Edit only the seven fltr_compute_* module bodies (lines 841-1076); the 6 v_fltr instances pick the change up through the instantiations at lines 706-712, 765-771 and 824-830, and nothing else in the design is touched. Instantiate int_sop_4 by name with named port connections and do not add a definition for it (the model in sim_reference/int_sop_4.v is supplied). Keep the module port list, dout's reg [15:0] declaration and the always @(posedge clk) block; delete q1..q7 and d_out_tmp's register declaration. Pattern (f1 shown; the other six differ only in the coefficients, in the tie-off of dx/dy where c4 = 0, and in the presence/width of the correction):

wire [8:0] s1 = din[55:48] + din[7:0];
wire [8:0] s2 = din[47:40] + din[15:8];
wire [8:0] s3 = din[39:32] + din[23:16];
wire [63:0] sop;
reg ext4_d1, ext4_d2;
int_sop_4 isop (.clk(clk), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0),
.ax(s1), .ay(9'd29), .bx(s2), .by(9'd101),
.cx(s3), .cy(9'd17), .dx({1'b0, din[31:24]}), .dy(9'd277),
.chainin(64'b0), .result(sop), .chainout());
wire [19:0] d_out_tmp = sop[19:0] + (ext4_d2 ? 20'h E0000 : 20'h00000);
always @(posedge clk)
begin
ext4_d1 <= (din[31:24] >= 8'd237);
ext4_d2 <= ext4_d1;
dout <= d_out_tmp[18:3];
end

f2/h2, h1 and h3 need no ext registers and use dout <= sop[18:3];. f3 uses a 2-bit ext_d1/ext_d2 loaded with {1'b0,(din[39:32] >= 8'd181)} + {1'b0,(din[23:16] >= 8'd181)} and the three-way correction constant.

DESIGN_CHANGE: fltr_compute_f2 (lines 889-898) and fltr_compute_h2 (lines 992-1001) are the same filter on the same din in every v_fltr instance, so vidin_out_f2 and vidin_out_h2 are always equal; computing one of them once per v_fltr would drop 6 of the 42 blocks and 6 sets of pre-adders. Separately, the my_fir family — which holds both of the design's slowest stages — would become convertible if its din were narrowed to 9 bits (it is driven by a 16-bit filter output) and its products were registered one stage before the sum instead of feeding a clock-enabled output register directly.

Reference simulation

After the edit, the framework simulates the edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output on every cycle. A candidate that does not match is not measured. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (int_sop_4.v) are in sim_reference/.

1	// int_sop_4: result = ax*ay + bx*by + cx*cy + dx*dy + chainin, unsigned, each 9x9 product
2	// zero-extended into a 64-bit sum, modulo 2^64 (the sum wraps at the result width).
3	// Ports: clk, reset, mode_sigs[12], ax, ay, bx, by, cx, cy, dx, dy [9 each], chainin[64] in;
4	// result[64], chainout[64] out. mode_sigs is not read.
5	// Registers (the arch's annotation read literally, decision 2026-10-16): every input is registered
6	// at the block's entry at one clock edge (the eight operands and chainin alike); the
7	// products and their sum are formed from those registers and loaded into result at the next edge.
8	// Cycles: every operand and chainin to result 2. chainout is combinational from the input
9	// registers: the sum result loads at the next edge unless that edge clears it (1 cycle from the
10	// inputs).
11	// Reset: synchronous, active high (2026-10-17: the arch's annotation does not distinguish a reset
12	// register from a clear sampled by the registers themselves): at a clock edge that samples it high
13	// every register of the block (operand registers, chainin register, result) is cleared to 0; the block
14	// loads again at the next edge that samples it low. No register has an initial value: every one is
15	// X until the first clear.
16	module int_sop_4 (
17	    input clk,
18	    input reset,
19	    input [11:0] mode_sigs,
20	    input [8:0] ax, input [8:0] ay,
21	    input [8:0] bx, input [8:0] by,
22	    input [8:0] cx, input [8:0] cy,
23	    input [8:0] dx, input [8:0] dy,
24	    input [63:0] chainin,
25	    output reg [63:0] result,
26	    output [63:0] chainout
27	);
28	
29	    // stage 1: the input registers
30	    reg [8:0]  ax_reg, ay_reg, bx_reg, by_reg, cx_reg, cy_reg, dx_reg, dy_reg;
31	    reg [63:0] chainin_reg;
32	
33	    // combinational middle: the four products and their sum, from the registers
34	    wire [17:0] prod_a = ax_reg * ay_reg;                        // 9x9 -> 18, exact
35	    wire [17:0] prod_b = bx_reg * by_reg;
36	    wire [17:0] prod_c = cx_reg * cy_reg;
37	    wire [17:0] prod_d = dx_reg * dy_reg;
38	    wire [63:0] sum    = prod_a + prod_b + prod_c + prod_d + chainin_reg;   // modulo 2^64
39	
40	    always @(posedge clk) begin
41	        if (reset) begin
42	            result <= 0;
43	            ax_reg <= 0; ay_reg <= 0; bx_reg <= 0; by_reg <= 0;
44	            cx_reg <= 0; cy_reg <= 0; dx_reg <= 0; dy_reg <= 0; chainin_reg <= 0;
45	        end
46	        else begin
47	            ax_reg <= ax; ay_reg <= ay; bx_reg <= bx; by_reg <= by;
48	            cx_reg <= cx; cy_reg <= cy; dx_reg <= dx; dy_reg <= dy; chainin_reg <= chainin;
49	            result <= sum;                                       // stage 2
50	        end
51	    end
52	
53	    assign chainout = sum;                                  // the sum of the input registers
54	
55	endmodule

Task

Edit stereovision2.v in this directory to carry out the approved plan below: rewrite the regions it names onto the hard block described next. If a step cannot be done as the plan says, stop and say which step and why; do not improvise a different rewrite.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: int_sop_4 (precision INT9)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx*by + cx*cy + dx*dy + chainin
  • input ports: clk[1] (clock), reset[1], mode_sigs[12], ax[9], ay[9], bx[9], by[9], cx[9], cy[9], dx[9], dy[9], chainin[64]
  • output ports: result[64], chainout[64]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 64 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 64 bits (modulo 2^64), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: on clk, the block registers its operands (ax, ay, bx, by, cx, cy, dx, dy) at one clock edge and result at the next, with the arithmetic between the two registers: operands applied before clock edge k appear in result after edge k+1, 2 cycles later. The block has no clock enable and no path around either register. chainin is registered at the block's entry like an operand and reaches result 2 cycles after it is applied. chainout is combinational from the input registers: it carries the value result loads at the next clock edge, one cycle before result shows it.
  • reset: reset is synchronous and active high: at a clock edge that samples it high it clears every register of the block (the operand registers, the chainin register and the result register) to 0, and the block loads again at the next edge that samples it low.
  • power-up: every register of the block is unknown until the first clear by reset; no register of the block has an initial value, and a rewrite may not rely on one.
  • tie-off: chainin = 0 when the block is not chained (a dedicated chain input: only another block's chainout or a constant may drive it); mode_sigs = 0 always (the architecture gives the port no meaning for this mode).
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above; a product-term port the rewrite does not use is tied to 0. chainout reaches only the next block's chainin, through a dedicated connection to the block directly below it in the column; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it.

  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.

PLAN:

What is converted. All 46 fltr_compute candidate ids (every product of fltr_compute_f1, f2, f3, h1, h2, h3, h4), each id with its 6 instances — 42 module instances in total, one int_sop_4 each, 42 blocks.

What is left, and why. All 45 my_fir candidate ids (my_fir_f1, f2, f3, h1, h2, h3, h4 — the modules that hold the design's two slowest stages) are left, for three reasons that apply to every one of them:

  • Operand width: din is 16 bits (WIDTH_5B, line 1460) and the coefficients are up to 255, so a product does not fit the 9-bit ports. Each product would need two slots (low byte, high byte) plus an external <<8 add, i.e. 4 blocks per my_fir instance, 168 blocks — past the 306-tile device once the rest of the design is counted, and the shift-add would sit on the critical stage.
  • Registers: the sum is loaded into dout by a clock-enabled register (if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1), lines 1476/1486 and the same in the other six) with 0 register stages between the products and the sum, and din (a fltr_compute output) changes on every cycle, not only on enabled cycles. The block has a fixed 2-cycle latency and no clock enable, so its result for din(k) is available one cycle after dout must take it; the only ways out delay dout (and hence my_fir_rdy/vidin_out_reg_*/the bus words) by whole cycles, which the cycle-by-cycle testbench would reject.
  • Those two together mean no correct rewrite of my_fir exists here, so the design's 11.6069 ns stage stays as it is and the rewrite is an area/wirelength rewrite.

Why T2. Each fltr_compute sum is symmetric: c1=c7, c2=c6, c3=c5 in all seven modules. The seven (or six) products are regrouped by the distributive law into four: (d1+d7)*c1 + (d2+d6)*c2 + (d3+d5)*c3 + d4*c4, which is one block instead of two. The regrouping is exact, not approximate: each operand byte is ≤255, so each pre-add is ≤510 and passes through a 9-bit port without truncation; every original product is below 2^17 (largest: 255*364 = 92820 in f3, 255*324 = 82620 in h4, 255*277 = 70635 in f1), so the original 17-bit q registers never truncate and Σq is unchanged by the folding; the folded products are ≤510*364 = 185640 < 2^18 and the whole sum is ≤255*1126 = 287130 < 2^19, so nothing wraps in the block either.

Reproducing the design's sign extension. The design adds {q[16],q[16],q[16],q}, i.e. it reads each 17-bit product as signed, so d_out_tmp = (Σq + 917504·C) mod 2^20 where C counts the products with bit 16 set. For f2, h1, h2, h3 no product can reach 2^16 (largest 255*255 = 65025, 255*193 = 49215, 255*147 = 37485), so C = 0 and dout <= result[18:3] is exact. For f1, f3, h4 exactly one coefficient can push a product past 2^16, so the editor adds a comparator and two 1-bit (f3: 2-bit) pipeline registers and corrects the block's result:

  • f1: C = (din[31:24] >= 8'd237) (277*236 = 65372, 277*237 = 65649)
  • h4: C = (din[31:24] >= 8'd203) (324*202 = 65448, 324*203 = 65772)
  • f3: C = (din[39:32] >= 8'd181) + (din[23:16] >= 8'd181) (364*180 = 65520, 364*181 = 65884), C in 0..2
    and d_out_tmp = result[19:0] + (C==0 ? 20'd0 : C==1 ? 20'd917504 : 20'd786432); dout <= d_out_tmp[18:3]; (786432 = 2*917504 mod 2^20). The correction logic sits between the block's result register and the existing dout register, a stage with about 9 ns of slack; nothing is added after dout, so the my_fir stages that read dout are untouched. No ASSUMES: line is needed — every bound above follows from the 8-bit slices and the literal coefficients.

Reset. reset is tied to 1'b0 on every block. The design's own reset (active low, line 203) clears only video_state, tm3_sram_adsp, horiz and vert; q, d_out_tmp and dout in fltr_compute have no reset and keep running through a reset pulse. Driving the block's reset from the design's reset would zero the filter pipeline on every mid-run reset pulse while the reference keeps computing, and the difference reaches bus_word_3..6_2to1 through h_fltr and port_bus_2to1 — so the block must never be cleared. With reset low the block's registers load every cycle, so their power-up X flushes in two cycles exactly as the reference's own unreset q/d_out_tmp X flushes in three; both sides are X on the same cycles (the fifos hold X far into the lead-in anyway) and the testbench's !== compare accepts X against X. No added register is relied on for an initial value: the pre-adds are combinational and the two correction registers load unconditionally every cycle.

Register stages, per converted region (all 46 ids behave alike). Before: operand byte -> q register (stage 1, the "products registered 1 stage before the sum" of the table) -> d_out_tmp register after the 6-level (5-level where c4 = 0) adder chain (stage 2) -> dout (stage 3). After: operand byte -> soft pre-add (combinational) -> block input registers (stage 1) -> block result register (stage 2) -> dout (stage 3). Three stages before and after, so dout changes on exactly the same cycle as in the baseline; the only register that moves is q, which becomes the block's input register, and d_out_tmp, which becomes the block's result register.

Soft logic removed, and from which stage. The 20-bit adder chain (6 levels in f1/f2/h2/h4, 5 in f3/h1/h3, about 120 and 100 BLEs) and the 20-bit d_out_tmp register leave the stage from the q registers to d_out_tmp. That stage is not the design's slowest: its delay is roughly 0.060 + 0.96 + 6*1.069 ≈ 7.5 ns against the 11.6069 ns my_fir_f1 stage, so removing it buys no clock period, only area and wirelength — this rewrite is taken for the area×wirelength factors, with the period held fixed. Added back per instance: three 9-bit pre-adders (~27 BLEs) in the stage from the buff_out registers to the block, plus at most 4 BLEs of comparator/correction. Net about -90 BLEs per instance, ~-3500 BLEs ≈ -350 clusters ≈ -9.7e6 area, on top of the DSP change.

Blocks and tiles. 42 blocks added (one per fltr_compute instance), each alone on a DSP tile. They replace 276 mult_9x9_fixed_pt multiplies that sit four to a tile, including the 57 tiles that hold only these; 224 - 57 + 42 = 209 tiles, and as low as about 197 if the packer also consolidates the tiles these products shared. DSP tile count therefore falls against the 224-tile baseline rather than rising, which is why folding to one block per sum is preferred over the straightforward two-block (4+3) split: that split would need 84 blocks (251 tiles), 42 extra chain pairs or a kept soft adder, and one-cycle operand-skew registers.

Longest series of blocks in any stage. One. No block drives another: chainin is tied to 0 and chainout is left unconnected on all 42 blocks, because a folded sum needs only four products. The rewrite's own stages are: buff_out register -> pre-adder -> block input register, ≈0.060 + 0.960 + 1.069 + 1.419 + 0.019 = 3.53 ns on medians (≈5.34 ns on the slowest samples); inside the block, 0.060 + 2.140 + 0.019 = 2.219 ns; block result register -> (correction LUT) -> dout, ≈1.1 ns, ≈2.2 ns with the correction. All far below the 11.6069 ns my_fir_f1 stage and below the 11.293 ns my_fir_f2 stage, so the slowest stage the rewrite leaves is the untouched 11.6069 ns one. dout stays a soft flip-flop with the same fanout, so the stage that starts at it (the critical one) keeps its shape exactly.

Editor notes. Edit only the seven fltr_compute_* module bodies (lines 841-1076); the 6 v_fltr instances pick the change up through the instantiations at lines 706-712, 765-771 and 824-830, and nothing else in the design is touched. Instantiate int_sop_4 by name with named port connections and do not add a definition for it (the model in sim_reference/int_sop_4.v is supplied). Keep the module port list, dout's reg [15:0] declaration and the always @(posedge clk) block; delete q1..q7 and d_out_tmp's register declaration. Pattern (f1 shown; the other six differ only in the coefficients, in the tie-off of dx/dy where c4 = 0, and in the presence/width of the correction):

wire [8:0] s1 = din[55:48] + din[7:0];
wire [8:0] s2 = din[47:40] + din[15:8];
wire [8:0] s3 = din[39:32] + din[23:16];
wire [63:0] sop;
reg ext4_d1, ext4_d2;
int_sop_4 isop (.clk(clk), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0),
.ax(s1), .ay(9'd29), .bx(s2), .by(9'd101),
.cx(s3), .cy(9'd17), .dx({1'b0, din[31:24]}), .dy(9'd277),
.chainin(64'b0), .result(sop), .chainout());
wire [19:0] d_out_tmp = sop[19:0] + (ext4_d2 ? 20'h E0000 : 20'h00000);
always @(posedge clk)
begin
ext4_d1 <= (din[31:24] >= 8'd237);
ext4_d2 <= ext4_d1;
dout <= d_out_tmp[18:3];
end

f2/h2, h1 and h3 need no ext registers and use dout <= sop[18:3];. f3 uses a 2-bit ext_d1/ext_d2 loaded with {1'b0,(din[39:32] >= 8'd181)} + {1'b0,(din[23:16] >= 8'd181)} and the three-way correction constant.

Simulation

When you finish, the framework simulates your edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output on every cycle, on its own copy. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (int_sop_4.v) are in sim_reference/; you may read them, but editing them has no effect on the result.

What I changed

Only the seven fltr_compute_* module bodies (the file's lines 841–1076). The 6 v_fltr instances pick the change up through their existing instantiations; nothing else in the design was touched. All 46 named regions (every $mul of the seven modules) are gone from soft logic.

In every module the seven taps are symmetric (c1=c7, c2=c6, c3=c5), so the seven products fold by the distributive law into the four of one int_sop_4: three 9-bit soft pre-adds s1=d1+d7, s2=d2+d6, s3=d3+d5 feed ax/bx/cx, the coefficients feed ay/by/cy, and {1'b0,d4}/c4 feed dx/dy. Region by region:

  • f1 (:859$44–:865$50) — coefficients 29, 101, 17, 277. Only q4 can reach bit 16 (277·237 = 65649), so the original's sign extension of the 17-bit products contributes one term: two added 1-bit pipeline registers carry din[31:24] >= 8'd237 alongside the block, and d_out_tmp = sop[19:0] + (ext4_d2 ? 20'hE0000 : 0) before the kept dout <= d_out_tmp[18:3].
  • f2 (:889$58–:895$64) — 4, 42, 163, 255. No product reaches bit 16 (max 65025), so no correction: dout <= sop[18:3].

Nothing wraps: the largest folded sum is f3's 510·563 = 287130 < 2^20, so sop[19:0] equals the untruncated Σq and the 20-bit modulo of the original is reproduced exactly by the correction constants.

1	// int_sop_4: result = ax*ay + bx*by + cx*cy + dx*dy + chainin, unsigned, each 9x9 product
2	// zero-extended into a 64-bit sum, modulo 2^64 (the sum wraps at the result width).
3	// Ports: clk, reset, mode_sigs[12], ax, ay, bx, by, cx, cy, dx, dy [9 each], chainin[64] in;
4	// result[64], chainout[64] out. mode_sigs is not read.
5	// Registers (the arch's annotation read literally, decision 2026-10-16): every input is registered
6	// at the block's entry at one clock edge (the eight operands and chainin alike); the
7	// products and their sum are formed from those registers and loaded into result at the next edge.
8	// Cycles: every operand and chainin to result 2. chainout is combinational from the input
9	// registers: the sum result loads at the next edge unless that edge clears it (1 cycle from the
10	// inputs).
11	// Reset: synchronous, active high (2026-10-17: the arch's annotation does not distinguish a reset
12	// register from a clear sampled by the registers themselves): at a clock edge that samples it high
13	// every register of the block (operand registers, chainin register, result) is cleared to 0; the block
14	// loads again at the next edge that samples it low. No register has an initial value: every one is
15	// X until the first clear.
16	module int_sop_4 (
17	    input clk,
18	    input reset,
19	    input [11:0] mode_sigs,
20	    input [8:0] ax, input [8:0] ay,
21	    input [8:0] bx, input [8:0] by,
22	    input [8:0] cx, input [8:0] cy,
23	    input [8:0] dx, input [8:0] dy,
24	    input [63:0] chainin,
25	    output reg [63:0] result,
26	    output [63:0] chainout
27	);
28	
29	    // stage 1: the input registers
30	    reg [8:0]  ax_reg, ay_reg, bx_reg, by_reg, cx_reg, cy_reg, dx_reg, dy_reg;
31	    reg [63:0] chainin_reg;
32	
33	    // combinational middle: the four products and their sum, from the registers
34	    wire [17:0] prod_a = ax_reg * ay_reg;                        // 9x9 -> 18, exact
35	    wire [17:0] prod_b = bx_reg * by_reg;
36	    wire [17:0] prod_c = cx_reg * cy_reg;
37	    wire [17:0] prod_d = dx_reg * dy_reg;
38	    wire [63:0] sum    = prod_a + prod_b + prod_c + prod_d + chainin_reg;   // modulo 2^64
39	
40	    always @(posedge clk) begin
41	        if (reset) begin
42	            result <= 0;
43	            ax_reg <= 0; ay_reg <= 0; bx_reg <= 0; by_reg <= 0;
44	            cx_reg <= 0; cy_reg <= 0; dx_reg <= 0; dy_reg <= 0; chainin_reg <= 0;
45	        end
46	        else begin
47	            ax_reg <= ax; ay_reg <= ay; bx_reg <= bx; by_reg <= by;
48	            cx_reg <= cx; cy_reg <= cy; dx_reg <= dx; dy_reg <= dy; chainin_reg <= chainin;
49	            result <= sum;                                       // stage 2
50	        end
51	    end
52	
53	    assign chainout = sum;                                  // the sum of the input registers
54	
55	endmodule

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Inner-loop check: the front end of the real flow, then a cell census. NOT place-and-route.
3	# usage: bash check.sh <file.v>
4	# Reads, in the flow's order: blocks.vlib (every hard block of the architecture, declared from its
5	# models), primitives.vlib (the flow's library of memories, adders and multipliers), then the design;
6	# then elaborates with the flow's hierarchy check. A module that is not defined, a port name the
7	# block does not have, or a misspelled block name fails here as it would in the flow. Do not
8	# declare the target block in the design: blocks.vlib declares it, and a design that defines a module
9	# of the target block's name fails this check.
10	# Prints one pass/fail line, then the cell census of the whole design (the last "Number of cells"
11	# table yosys prints): soft arithmetic as $mul/$add/$sub, registers as $dff*/$sdff*, memories as
12	# $mem*, muxes as $mux/$pmux, and every instantiated module by name, which is where a hard-block
13	# instantiation shows up with its instance count.
14	set -u
15	f="${1:?usage: check.sh <file.v>}"
16	here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
17	lib=""
18	[ -f "$here/blocks.vlib" ] && lib="read_verilog -lib $here/blocks.vlib; "
19	[ -f "$here/primitives.vlib" ] && lib="${lib}read_verilog -nomem2reg $here/primitives.vlib; "
20	target="$(sed -n 's|^// target block: *\([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*\).*|\1|p' "$here/blocks.vlib" 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
21	if [ -n "$target" ] && grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*module[[:space:]]+$target([^A-Za-z0-9_$]|$)" "$f"; then
22	  echo "FAIL: $f defines module $target; blocks.vlib declares it. Remove the module definition and keep the instances."
23	  exit 1
24	fi
25	out="$(yosys -p "${lib}read_verilog -sv -nolatches $f; hierarchy -check -auto-top -purge_lib; proc; opt; stat" 2>&1)"
26	rc=$?
27	if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
28	  echo "FAIL: does not synthesize (yosys exit $rc)"
29	  echo "$out" | grep -iE 'error|warning' | tail -15
30	  echo "$out" | tail -10
31	  exit 1
32	fi
33	echo "OK: synthesizes cleanly"
34	echo "Cell census (yosys stat, whole design):"
35	echo "$out" | awk '/Number of cells:/{buf=$0 "\n"; on=1; next}
36	                   on && /^[[:space:]]+[$A-Za-z_][^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+[0-9]+[[:space:]]*$/ {buf=buf $0 "\n"; next}
37	                   on {on=0}
38	                   END{printf "%s", buf}' \
39	  | grep -E 'Number of cells|^[[:space:]]+(\$(mul|add|sub|mem|memrd|memwr|dff|dffe|sdff|sdffe|adff|adffe|mux|pmux)|[A-Za-z_])' || true

Task

You are the acceptance reviewer. You did not plan or write this edit. Check the edit against the approved plan, the block's contract and the correctness rules.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: int_sop_4 (precision INT9)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx*by + cx*cy + dx*dy + chainin
  • input ports: clk[1] (clock), reset[1], mode_sigs[12], ax[9], ay[9], bx[9], by[9], cx[9], cy[9], dx[9], dy[9], chainin[64]
  • output ports: result[64], chainout[64]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 64 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 64 bits (modulo 2^64), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: on clk, the block registers its operands (ax, ay, bx, by, cx, cy, dx, dy) at one clock edge and result at the next, with the arithmetic between the two registers: operands applied before clock edge k appear in result after edge k+1, 2 cycles later. The block has no clock enable and no path around either register. chainin is registered at the block's entry like an operand and reaches result 2 cycles after it is applied. chainout is combinational from the input registers: it carries the value result loads at the next clock edge, one cycle before result shows it.
  • reset: reset is synchronous and active high: at a clock edge that samples it high it clears every register of the block (the operand registers, the chainin register and the result register) to 0, and the block loads again at the next edge that samples it low.
  • power-up: every register of the block is unknown until the first clear by reset; no register of the block has an initial value, and a rewrite may not rely on one.
  • tie-off: chainin = 0 when the block is not chained (a dedicated chain input: only another block's chainout or a constant may drive it); mode_sigs = 0 always (the architecture gives the port no meaning for this mode).
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above; a product-term port the rewrite does not use is tied to 0. chainout reaches only the next block's chainin, through a dedicated connection to the block directly below it in the column; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it.
The design

The file stereovision2.v is the edited design. The edit is the diff below, taken against the original source.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.

PLAN:

What is converted. All 46 fltr_compute candidate ids (every product of fltr_compute_f1, f2, f3, h1, h2, h3, h4), each id with its 6 instances — 42 module instances in total, one int_sop_4 each, 42 blocks.

What is left, and why. All 45 my_fir candidate ids (my_fir_f1, f2, f3, h1, h2, h3, h4 — the modules that hold the design's two slowest stages) are left, for three reasons that apply to every one of them:

  • Operand width: din is 16 bits (WIDTH_5B, line 1460) and the coefficients are up to 255, so a product does not fit the 9-bit ports. Each product would need two slots (low byte, high byte) plus an external <<8 add, i.e. 4 blocks per my_fir instance, 168 blocks — past the 306-tile device once the rest of the design is counted, and the shift-add would sit on the critical stage.
  • Registers: the sum is loaded into dout by a clock-enabled register (if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1), lines 1476/1486 and the same in the other six) with 0 register stages between the products and the sum, and din (a fltr_compute output) changes on every cycle, not only on enabled cycles. The block has a fixed 2-cycle latency and no clock enable, so its result for din(k) is available one cycle after dout must take it; the only ways out delay dout (and hence my_fir_rdy/vidin_out_reg_*/the bus words) by whole cycles, which the cycle-by-cycle testbench would reject.
  • Those two together mean no correct rewrite of my_fir exists here, so the design's 11.6069 ns stage stays as it is and the rewrite is an area/wirelength rewrite.

Why T2. Each fltr_compute sum is symmetric: c1=c7, c2=c6, c3=c5 in all seven modules. The seven (or six) products are regrouped by the distributive law into four: (d1+d7)*c1 + (d2+d6)*c2 + (d3+d5)*c3 + d4*c4, which is one block instead of two. The regrouping is exact, not approximate: each operand byte is ≤255, so each pre-add is ≤510 and passes through a 9-bit port without truncation; every original product is below 2^17 (largest: 255*364 = 92820 in f3, 255*324 = 82620 in h4, 255*277 = 70635 in f1), so the original 17-bit q registers never truncate and Σq is unchanged by the folding; the folded products are ≤510*364 = 185640 < 2^18 and the whole sum is ≤255*1126 = 287130 < 2^19, so nothing wraps in the block either.

Reproducing the design's sign extension. The design adds {q[16],q[16],q[16],q}, i.e. it reads each 17-bit product as signed, so d_out_tmp = (Σq + 917504·C) mod 2^20 where C counts the products with bit 16 set. For f2, h1, h2, h3 no product can reach 2^16 (largest 255*255 = 65025, 255*193 = 49215, 255*147 = 37485), so C = 0 and dout <= result[18:3] is exact. For f1, f3, h4 exactly one coefficient can push a product past 2^16, so the editor adds a comparator and two 1-bit (f3: 2-bit) pipeline registers and corrects the block's result:

  • f1: C = (din[31:24] >= 8'd237) (277*236 = 65372, 277*237 = 65649)
  • h4: C = (din[31:24] >= 8'd203) (324*202 = 65448, 324*203 = 65772)
  • f3: C = (din[39:32] >= 8'd181) + (din[23:16] >= 8'd181) (364*180 = 65520, 364*181 = 65884), C in 0..2
    and d_out_tmp = result[19:0] + (C==0 ? 20'd0 : C==1 ? 20'd917504 : 20'd786432); dout <= d_out_tmp[18:3]; (786432 = 2*917504 mod 2^20). The correction logic sits between the block's result register and the existing dout register, a stage with about 9 ns of slack; nothing is added after dout, so the my_fir stages that read dout are untouched. No ASSUMES: line is needed — every bound above follows from the 8-bit slices and the literal coefficients.

Reset. reset is tied to 1'b0 on every block. The design's own reset (active low, line 203) clears only video_state, tm3_sram_adsp, horiz and vert; q, d_out_tmp and dout in fltr_compute have no reset and keep running through a reset pulse. Driving the block's reset from the design's reset would zero the filter pipeline on every mid-run reset pulse while the reference keeps computing, and the difference reaches bus_word_3..6_2to1 through h_fltr and port_bus_2to1 — so the block must never be cleared. With reset low the block's registers load every cycle, so their power-up X flushes in two cycles exactly as the reference's own unreset q/d_out_tmp X flushes in three; both sides are X on the same cycles (the fifos hold X far into the lead-in anyway) and the testbench's !== compare accepts X against X. No added register is relied on for an initial value: the pre-adds are combinational and the two correction registers load unconditionally every cycle.

Register stages, per converted region (all 46 ids behave alike). Before: operand byte -> q register (stage 1, the "products registered 1 stage before the sum" of the table) -> d_out_tmp register after the 6-level (5-level where c4 = 0) adder chain (stage 2) -> dout (stage 3). After: operand byte -> soft pre-add (combinational) -> block input registers (stage 1) -> block result register (stage 2) -> dout (stage 3). Three stages before and after, so dout changes on exactly the same cycle as in the baseline; the only register that moves is q, which becomes the block's input register, and d_out_tmp, which becomes the block's result register.

Soft logic removed, and from which stage. The 20-bit adder chain (6 levels in f1/f2/h2/h4, 5 in f3/h1/h3, about 120 and 100 BLEs) and the 20-bit d_out_tmp register leave the stage from the q registers to d_out_tmp. That stage is not the design's slowest: its delay is roughly 0.060 + 0.96 + 6*1.069 ≈ 7.5 ns against the 11.6069 ns my_fir_f1 stage, so removing it buys no clock period, only area and wirelength — this rewrite is taken for the area×wirelength factors, with the period held fixed. Added back per instance: three 9-bit pre-adders (~27 BLEs) in the stage from the buff_out registers to the block, plus at most 4 BLEs of comparator/correction. Net about -90 BLEs per instance, ~-3500 BLEs ≈ -350 clusters ≈ -9.7e6 area, on top of the DSP change.

Blocks and tiles. 42 blocks added (one per fltr_compute instance), each alone on a DSP tile. They replace 276 mult_9x9_fixed_pt multiplies that sit four to a tile, including the 57 tiles that hold only these; 224 - 57 + 42 = 209 tiles, and as low as about 197 if the packer also consolidates the tiles these products shared. DSP tile count therefore falls against the 224-tile baseline rather than rising, which is why folding to one block per sum is preferred over the straightforward two-block (4+3) split: that split would need 84 blocks (251 tiles), 42 extra chain pairs or a kept soft adder, and one-cycle operand-skew registers.

Longest series of blocks in any stage. One. No block drives another: chainin is tied to 0 and chainout is left unconnected on all 42 blocks, because a folded sum needs only four products. The rewrite's own stages are: buff_out register -> pre-adder -> block input register, ≈0.060 + 0.960 + 1.069 + 1.419 + 0.019 = 3.53 ns on medians (≈5.34 ns on the slowest samples); inside the block, 0.060 + 2.140 + 0.019 = 2.219 ns; block result register -> (correction LUT) -> dout, ≈1.1 ns, ≈2.2 ns with the correction. All far below the 11.6069 ns my_fir_f1 stage and below the 11.293 ns my_fir_f2 stage, so the slowest stage the rewrite leaves is the untouched 11.6069 ns one. dout stays a soft flip-flop with the same fanout, so the stage that starts at it (the critical one) keeps its shape exactly.

Editor notes. Edit only the seven fltr_compute_* module bodies (lines 841-1076); the 6 v_fltr instances pick the change up through the instantiations at lines 706-712, 765-771 and 824-830, and nothing else in the design is touched. Instantiate int_sop_4 by name with named port connections and do not add a definition for it (the model in sim_reference/int_sop_4.v is supplied). Keep the module port list, dout's reg [15:0] declaration and the always @(posedge clk) block; delete q1..q7 and d_out_tmp's register declaration. Pattern (f1 shown; the other six differ only in the coefficients, in the tie-off of dx/dy where c4 = 0, and in the presence/width of the correction):

wire [8:0] s1 = din[55:48] + din[7:0];
wire [8:0] s2 = din[47:40] + din[15:8];
wire [8:0] s3 = din[39:32] + din[23:16];
wire [63:0] sop;
reg ext4_d1, ext4_d2;
int_sop_4 isop (.clk(clk), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0),
.ax(s1), .ay(9'd29), .bx(s2), .by(9'd101),
.cx(s3), .cy(9'd17), .dx({1'b0, din[31:24]}), .dy(9'd277),
.chainin(64'b0), .result(sop), .chainout());
wire [19:0] d_out_tmp = sop[19:0] + (ext4_d2 ? 20'h E0000 : 20'h00000);
always @(posedge clk)
begin
ext4_d1 <= (din[31:24] >= 8'd237);
ext4_d2 <= ext4_d1;
dout <= d_out_tmp[18:3];
end

f2/h2, h1 and h3 need no ext registers and use dout <= sop[18:3];. f3 uses a 2-bit ext_d1/ext_d2 loaded with {1'b0,(din[39:32] >= 8'd181)} + {1'b0,(din[23:16] >= 8'd181)} and the three-way correction constant.

DESIGN_CHANGE: fltr_compute_f2 (lines 889-898) and fltr_compute_h2 (lines 992-1001) are the same filter on the same din in every v_fltr instance, so vidin_out_f2 and vidin_out_h2 are always equal; computing one of them once per v_fltr would drop 6 of the 42 blocks and 6 sets of pre-adders. Separately, the my_fir family — which holds both of the design's slowest stages — would become convertible if its din were narrowed to 9 bits (it is driven by a 16-bit filter output) and its products were registered one stage before the sum instead of feeding a clock-enabled output register directly.

1	// int_sop_4: result = ax*ay + bx*by + cx*cy + dx*dy + chainin, unsigned, each 9x9 product
2	// zero-extended into a 64-bit sum, modulo 2^64 (the sum wraps at the result width).
3	// Ports: clk, reset, mode_sigs[12], ax, ay, bx, by, cx, cy, dx, dy [9 each], chainin[64] in;
4	// result[64], chainout[64] out. mode_sigs is not read.
5	// Registers (the arch's annotation read literally, decision 2026-10-16): every input is registered
6	// at the block's entry at one clock edge (the eight operands and chainin alike); the
7	// products and their sum are formed from those registers and loaded into result at the next edge.
8	// Cycles: every operand and chainin to result 2. chainout is combinational from the input
9	// registers: the sum result loads at the next edge unless that edge clears it (1 cycle from the
10	// inputs).
11	// Reset: synchronous, active high (2026-10-17: the arch's annotation does not distinguish a reset
12	// register from a clear sampled by the registers themselves): at a clock edge that samples it high
13	// every register of the block (operand registers, chainin register, result) is cleared to 0; the block
14	// loads again at the next edge that samples it low. No register has an initial value: every one is
15	// X until the first clear.
16	module int_sop_4 (
17	    input clk,
18	    input reset,
19	    input [11:0] mode_sigs,
20	    input [8:0] ax, input [8:0] ay,
21	    input [8:0] bx, input [8:0] by,
22	    input [8:0] cx, input [8:0] cy,
23	    input [8:0] dx, input [8:0] dy,
24	    input [63:0] chainin,
25	    output reg [63:0] result,
26	    output [63:0] chainout
27	);
28	
29	    // stage 1: the input registers
30	    reg [8:0]  ax_reg, ay_reg, bx_reg, by_reg, cx_reg, cy_reg, dx_reg, dy_reg;
31	    reg [63:0] chainin_reg;
32	
33	    // combinational middle: the four products and their sum, from the registers
34	    wire [17:0] prod_a = ax_reg * ay_reg;                        // 9x9 -> 18, exact
35	    wire [17:0] prod_b = bx_reg * by_reg;
36	    wire [17:0] prod_c = cx_reg * cy_reg;
37	    wire [17:0] prod_d = dx_reg * dy_reg;
38	    wire [63:0] sum    = prod_a + prod_b + prod_c + prod_d + chainin_reg;   // modulo 2^64
39	
40	    always @(posedge clk) begin
41	        if (reset) begin
42	            result <= 0;
43	            ax_reg <= 0; ay_reg <= 0; bx_reg <= 0; by_reg <= 0;
44	            cx_reg <= 0; cy_reg <= 0; dx_reg <= 0; dy_reg <= 0; chainin_reg <= 0;
45	        end
46	        else begin
47	            ax_reg <= ax; ay_reg <= ay; bx_reg <= bx; by_reg <= by;
48	            cx_reg <= cx; cy_reg <= cy; dx_reg <= dx; dy_reg <= dy; chainin_reg <= chainin;
49	            result <= sum;                                       // stage 2
50	        end
51	    end
52	
53	    assign chainout = sum;                                  // the sum of the input registers
54	
55	endmodule

prompt

Task

You are the planner. Read the design source, stereovision2.v, and decide which of the candidate arithmetic regions listed below to rewrite onto the hard block described next, or that none should be rewritten. Write a plan for the editor, who carries it out; do not edit any file.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: int_sop_4 (precision INT9)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx*by + cx*cy + dx*dy + chainin
  • input ports: clk[1] (clock), reset[1], mode_sigs[12], ax[9], ay[9], bx[9], by[9], cx[9], cy[9], dx[9], dy[9], chainin[64]
  • output ports: result[64], chainout[64]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 64 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 64 bits (modulo 2^64), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: on clk, the block registers its operands (ax, ay, bx, by, cx, cy, dx, dy) at one clock edge and result at the next, with the arithmetic between the two registers: operands applied before clock edge k appear in result after edge k+1, 2 cycles later. The block has no clock enable and no path around either register. chainin is registered at the block's entry like an operand and reaches result 2 cycles after it is applied. chainout is combinational from the input registers: it carries the value result loads at the next clock edge, one cycle before result shows it.
  • reset: reset is synchronous and active high: at a clock edge that samples it high it clears every register of the block (the operand registers, the chainin register and the result register) to 0, and the block loads again at the next edge that samples it low.
  • power-up: every register of the block is unknown until the first clear by reset; no register of the block has an initial value, and a rewrite may not rely on one.
  • tie-off: chainin = 0 when the block is not chained (a dedicated chain input: only another block's chainout or a constant may drive it); mode_sigs = 0 always (the architecture gives the port no meaning for this mode).
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above; a product-term port the rewrite does not use is tied to 0. chainout reaches only the next block's chainin, through a dedicated connection to the block directly below it in the column; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it.
The design

Baseline: the unmodified stereovision2 under this run's VPR settings (channel width 300, median of five seeds, 1 to 5) has a worst register-to-register path of 11.6069 ns on its one clock tm3_clk_v0 (I/O pads not timed) and uses 224 DSP tiles (as packed at seed 1) of the device's 306. Its used logic-block area is 9.73358e+07 minimum-width transistor areas (one DSP tile 253779, one cluster 27905) and its routed wirelength is 436921, so its area x delay x wirelength product, the objective, is 4.93619e+14. Its slowest stage (read off the seed-1 timing report) is in my_fir_f1: one hard multiply on a DSP tile (two_mult_18x19), then six adder levels with their carry chains, then one LUT, into an enabled flip-flop. The next slowest stage (read off the seed-1 timing report), in my_fir_f2 (endpoint group $dffe~642, not path 1's $dffe~456), is the same shape as path 1, one hard multiply on a DSP tile, six adder levels with their carry chains, one LUT, into an enabled flip-flop, 11.293 ns, so shortening the slowest stage past that point buys nothing on its own. Any path your rewrite creates is compared against that critical path.

An id names a product by its module and its multiply. One that ends in (sum_in=<module>) is a product whose sum sits in that other module: the product leaves its own module through a port and is added there, so the arithmetic to convert spans both. A #1, #2 after an id separates instances of the same product that sit in sums of different shapes.
