Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Cost (guidance: go against it only with a reason in the plan)
  • The clock period is the delay of the slowest stage (the logic between one register and the next). A rewrite that does not touch the slowest stage should not be expected to make the design faster, and should not make another stage slower than it.
  • Blocks in series are separate stages. A path through chainout starts at an input register and continues, in the same stage, into what it drives.
  • Moving or adding registers changes stage lengths and when values arrive.
  • Area falls when soft adders and flip-flops move into blocks.
  • A block of this mode takes a DSP tile alone. Synthesis may already have placed the design's multiplies on tiles, so a block that only replaces one saves little: count tiles against the baseline.
  • The block has chain ports: a block's chainout can drive the next block's chainin directly, so a sum can continue from block to block.
Objective

Minimize area × delay × wirelength against the baseline. If you expect no rewrite to lower it, output TIER: NONE. Among rewrites that lower it, choose the one that lowers it most.

Output
Tiers
  • T1: The block replaces the region's arithmetic as it stands: the same operations on the same operands, now inside the block.
  • T2: The region's arithmetic is regrouped to fit the block (products regrouped into the block's sums, registers moved), computing the same values.
  • NONE: No rewrite: no candidate can be rewritten correctly.
Header

Write exactly this header, each key at the start of its own line, then the plan:

TIER: <exactly one of T1, T2, NONE>
REGIONS: <the converted candidate ids, comma-separated; NONE when TIER is NONE>
SHARED_REDUCTION: <the signal or module the converted products are summed in; NONE for a single region>
BLOCKS: <how many blocks the rewrite instantiates, one integer>
TILES: <how many DSP tiles the whole design then uses, one integer>
STAGE_NS: <the delay of the slowest stage the rewrite leaves, in ns, one number>
MAPPING: <which design signals go to which block ports>
PLAN: <the plan, stating everything listed below>

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds, and how many DSP tiles the design then uses.
  • The longest series of blocks in any stage and its delay, against the slowest stage.
  • What soft logic leaves which stage, and whether that stage is the slowest.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output rules
  • Write nothing before the TIER line; read the source first.
  • A reviewer checks the plan automatically and no person reads it, so do not end with a question or an offer.
  • If a change to the design itself, not to the rewrite, would let more of it use the block, you may say so on a line starting DESIGN_CHANGE:. It is reported to the user and does not change your decision.

The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (int_sop_4.v) are in sim_reference/.

PLAN:

What is converted, and what is left

  1. All 46 fltr_compute candidates (f1,f2,f3,h1,h2,h3,h4) are converted exactly as in the kept candidate: keep that edit verbatim (the seven folded sums, the three 9-bit pre-adds, the ext*_d1/ext*_d2 sign-extension corrections for f1, f3 and h4, reset tied to 1'b0). It already measured -39% on the product and is not touched by this revision.
  2. 31 of the 45 my_fir candidates are converted: in every my_fir module the products of n_delay_reg2, n_delay_reg3 (where present), n_delay_reg4, n_delay_reg5 and n_delay_reg6 move onto blocks. Because the taps are symmetric (c4=c2, c5=c1, c6=c0, cited at lines 1440-1449, 1500-1506, 1561-1567, 1616-1625, 1675-1681, 1734-1740, 1792-1798), those five products fold into four: c2*(n2+n4) + c3*n3 + c5*n5 + c6*n6. The taps are 16 bits and the block's ports are 9, so each tap is split into bytes and the four products are formed once over the high bytes and once over the low bytes: sum = 256*HI + LO, exactly. Operands stay inside 9 bits: a byte pair sums to at most 510, a single byte to 255, and every coefficient is at most 255. The whole sum is at most 673*65535 = 44.1e6 < 2^28, so neither the original nor the rewrite truncates and the unsigned block arithmetic matches the unsigned source arithmetic bit for bit.
  3. 14 my_fir candidates are left, all for one reason: they are the two newest samples of the window (din * c0 at lines 1486, 1542, 1602, 1661, 1716, 1775, 1833 and n_delay_reg1 * c1 at lines 1487, 1543, 1603, 1662, 1717, 1776, 1834). A readable block result costs 2 cycles (chainout is 1 cycle but reaches only another block's chainin, so soft logic cannot read it), while dout loads one cycle after din is presented. din's value is produced by the upstream fltr_compute dout register and does not exist two cycles early inside h_fltr, so c0*din must stay a soft/DSP multiply feeding the last adder of the dout stage. The c1 term does not need the block either: since n_delay_reg1 is the enabled register of din, the enabled register q1_reg <= din*c1 holds exactly c1*n_delay_reg1 at every cycle, so that product moves one cycle earlier into its own short stage and leaves the dout stage as a register input.

Why the operands are the advanced taps, and why this is exact

The block answers two cycles after its operands are applied, so at cycle c it must be given the tap values that will stand at cycle c+2. The delay line advances by sh = e(c) + e(c+1) steps over those two cycles, with e the enable new_data_rdy. e(c) is the module's own input; e(c+1) is available at cycle c because v_nd_s1_left and its five siblings are plain unconditional registers of the top-level inputs v_nd_s*_*_2to0 (lines 430-438, 188-197), so the unregistered strobe is the next cycle's enable. Hence new_data_rdy_nxt. Expanding the delay line twice gives n_k(c+2) = n_{k-sh}(c) for k >= 2 (with n_0 = din), in all four (e(c),e(c+1)) cases; k=1 would need n_{-1}, which is why tap 1 is left out of the block. Those are the p2..p6 of the MAPPING. Every p is a value already held in a register of the module, so the rewrite is defined exactly when the original is: for a given load edge the block sees the identical sample values, only read earlier out of earlier registers, so the X behaviour at start-up is unchanged as well. reset is tied to 0 on every block: the design never clears these pipelines, and the testbench pulses reset mid-run, so clearing the block there would diverge. No block register is relied on for an initial value; each is reloaded every cycle and washes out within two cycles, inside the hundreds of cycles the 226/316/496-deep fifos take to flush.

Blocks and tiles

126 blocks: 42 for the fltr_compute reductions (one per instance, 7 modules x 6 v_fltr instances) and 84 for the my_fir reductions (two per instance, 7 modules x 6 h_fltr instances). Each takes its DSP tile alone. The remaining multiplies in the design are the two per my_fir instance (din*c0 and din*c1), 84 of them, which pack about two to a two_mult_18x19 tile, ~45 tiles. Total ~171 tiles, against 224 in the baseline and 187 measured for the kept candidate; the device has 306.

Stages and delay

No stage holds two blocks in series: every block is fed from design registers and read from its own result register, so the longest series of blocks in any stage is one, 2.219 ns inside the block, well under the slowest stage. No chainout is used.

The slowest stage of the kept candidate, 11.4491 ns, is the my_fir stage: one 18x19 multiply, six adder levels with their carry chains, one LUT, into the enabled flip-flop. That stage is what this rewrite empties. What leaves it: all six adder levels and five of the seven multiplies. What is left in it: the single multiply din*c0 and three adders, written so the multiply feeds only the final adder — 0.060 (din clock-to-Q) + ~1.0 wire + 2.140 multiply + 0.544 wire + one ~28-bit carry chain + 0.019 setup, about 4.7 ns; the q1_reg/sop_lo path through the three adders is about 4.9 ns. The new stages the rewrite creates are both shorter: tap register to block input is 0.060 + 0.960 + one mux LUT + one 8-bit carry chain + 1.419 + 0.019, about 3.7 ns, and din to q1_reg is 0.060 + ~1.0 + 2.140 + 0.019, about 3.2 ns. The fltr_compute stages are unchanged from the kept candidate and are shorter still.

With the my_fir stage down to ~4.9 ns, the slowest stage left in the design is in steer_fltr (lines 640-643): three levels of 31-bit add/subtract from im_p_tmp_1..4 into im_p_tmp, roughly 0.060 + 0.960 + three carry-chain levels with their wires + 0.019, about 5.9 ns. That stage is untouched by the rewrite and sets STAGE_NS. It is an estimate off the sampled wire and adder figures, not a measured path; the period should land near it, between about 5.5 and 7 ns, against 11.4491.

Register stages, before and after

  • fltr_compute (all 46 regions): before, din -> q1..q7 (1 stage) -> d_out_tmp (2nd) -> dout (3rd). After, din -> block input register (1st) -> block result register (2nd) -> dout (3rd). Three stages before and after, same values at the same edges; the sign-extension correction is delayed two cycles by ext*_d1/ext*_d2 to land with the block result.
  • my_fir (all 31 converted regions): before, the taps are registers and the products and their six-level sum are combinational into the enabled dout, one register stage from tap to dout. After, the same tap values are presented to the block two cycles before that edge, pass the block's input register and result register, and are added into the same dout register at the same edge with the same value — the sample-to-dout latency is unchanged, no register is added on the din-to-dout path, and the new q1_reg holds c1*n_delay_reg1, the value the original computed combinationally at that edge.

Edit notes for the editor

Keep the kept candidate's fltr_compute edit exactly as it stands. In each my_fir module: add the new_data_rdy_nxt input at the end of the port list, add reg[23:0] q1_reg;, the sh/p2..p6 wires, the two 9-bit pre-adds, the two int_sop_4 instances, keep n_delay_reg1..6 and output_data_ready as they are, add q1_reg <= din * c1; inside the if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1) branch, and replace the seven-term dout <= ... with the parenthesised form of the MAPPING (the parenthesisation matters: it keeps the multiply one adder level from the register). In h_fltr add the input vidin_new_data_nxt at the end of its port list and pass it as the last argument of all seven my_fir instantiations (lines 514-520). At the top, add the matching last argument to the six h_fltr instantiations (lines 188-190, 195-197). The top's own port list does not change.

DESIGN_CHANGE: if fltr_compute exposed its pre-register sum (d_out_tmp[18:3], the value dout takes next cycle) as an output, routed through v_fltr into h_fltr, then my_fir's din would be known one cycle early; the c0 product could then be registered like the c1 one, which would empty the my_fir dout stage of its last multiply (about 1.2 ns off that stage) and would also let the c0 and c1 terms fold back into the blocks' fourth products, removing both remaining soft multiplies per filter, about 45 more DSP tiles.

1	        // stereovision2's top (from the generated testbench of 2026-10-16). The six filter streams are
2	        // v_nd_s*_*_2to0 (strobe) and v_d_reg_s*_*_2to0 (byte); reset is active low. Under START_ONLY
3	        // the mid-run reset pulses are left out.
4	        phase = "rst-pattern";   // a reset pattern while data flows: one-cycle, three-cycle and back-to-back pulses
5	        for (i = 0; i < 120; i = i + 1) begin
6	            tick;
7	            vidin_new_data = i[0]; vidin_rgb_reg = i * 7; vidin_addr_reg = i * 131; svid_comp_switch = i[2]; offchip_sram_data_in = {i, ~i};
8	            reset = (`MIDRUN_RESETS && (i == 10 || (i >= 30 && i < 33) || i == 50 || i == 51 || i == 70 || (i >= 90 && i < 98))) ? 1'b0 : 1'b1;
9	            {v_nd_s1_left_2to0, v_nd_s2_left_2to0, v_nd_s4_left_2to0, v_nd_s1_right_2to0, v_nd_s2_right_2to0, v_nd_s4_right_2to0} = (i % 3 == 0) ? 6'h3F : {i[0], i[1], i[2], i[0], i[1], i[2]};
10	            v_d_reg_s1_left_2to0 = i * 3; v_d_reg_s2_left_2to0 = i * 5; v_d_reg_s4_left_2to0 = 255 - i; v_d_reg_s1_right_2to0 = i * 11; v_d_reg_s2_right_2to0 = i * 13; v_d_reg_s4_right_2to0 = 128 + i;
11	        end
12	        phase = "max";
13	        for (i = 0; i < 40; i = i + 1) begin tick; set_zero; reset = 1; {v_d_reg_s1_left_2to0, v_d_reg_s2_left_2to0, v_d_reg_s4_left_2to0, v_d_reg_s1_right_2to0, v_d_reg_s2_right_2to0, v_d_reg_s4_right_2to0} = {6{8'd255}}; end
14	        phase = "alt";
15	        for (i = 0; i < 40; i = i + 1) begin tick; set_zero; reset = 1; {v_d_reg_s1_left_2to0, v_d_reg_s2_left_2to0, v_d_reg_s4_left_2to0, v_d_reg_s1_right_2to0, v_d_reg_s2_right_2to0, v_d_reg_s4_right_2to0} = i[0] ? {6{8'd255}} : 48'd0; end
16	        phase = "ramp";
17	        for (i = 0; i < 64; i = i + 1) begin tick; set_zero; reset = 1; {v_d_reg_s1_left_2to0, v_d_reg_s2_left_2to0, v_d_reg_s4_left_2to0, v_d_reg_s1_right_2to0, v_d_reg_s2_right_2to0, v_d_reg_s4_right_2to0} = {6{i[7:0] * 8'd4}}; end
18	        zero_cycles(8);
19	        // the long random stretch: every data input random, the s1_left strobe every 8 to 12 cycles
20	        // (port_bus_2to1 shows all six streams only when its counter runs a full round between s1_left
21	        // strobes), the other five strobes random with probability 1/2, reset 1 in 128
22	        phase = "random"; gap = 0;
23	        for (i = 0; i < `RANDOM_CYCLES; i = i + 1) begin
24	            tick; set_data;
25	            if (gap == 0) begin draw; gap = 8 + (r32 % 5); end
26	            gap = gap - 1;
27	            v_nd_s1_left_2to0 = (gap == 0);
28	            draw; reset = (`MIDRUN_RESETS && (r32 % 128) == 0) ? 1'b0 : 1'b1;
29	        end

1	// int_sop_4: result = ax*ay + bx*by + cx*cy + dx*dy + chainin, unsigned, each 9x9 product
2	// zero-extended into a 64-bit sum, modulo 2^64 (the sum wraps at the result width).
3	// Ports: clk, reset, mode_sigs[12], ax, ay, bx, by, cx, cy, dx, dy [9 each], chainin[64] in;
4	// result[64], chainout[64] out. mode_sigs is not read.
5	// Registers (the arch's annotation read literally, decision 2026-10-16): every input is registered
6	// at the block's entry at one clock edge (the eight operands and chainin alike); the
7	// products and their sum are formed from those registers and loaded into result at the next edge.
8	// Cycles: every operand and chainin to result 2. chainout is combinational from the input
9	// registers: the sum result loads at the next edge unless that edge clears it (1 cycle from the
10	// inputs).
11	// Reset: synchronous, active high (2026-10-17: the arch's annotation does not distinguish a reset
12	// register from a clear sampled by the registers themselves): at a clock edge that samples it high
13	// every register of the block (operand registers, chainin register, result) is cleared to 0; the block
14	// loads again at the next edge that samples it low. No register has an initial value: every one is
15	// X until the first clear.
16	module int_sop_4 (
17	    input clk,
18	    input reset,
19	    input [11:0] mode_sigs,
20	    input [8:0] ax, input [8:0] ay,
21	    input [8:0] bx, input [8:0] by,
22	    input [8:0] cx, input [8:0] cy,
23	    input [8:0] dx, input [8:0] dy,
24	    input [63:0] chainin,
25	    output reg [63:0] result,
26	    output [63:0] chainout
27	);
28	
29	    // stage 1: the input registers
30	    reg [8:0]  ax_reg, ay_reg, bx_reg, by_reg, cx_reg, cy_reg, dx_reg, dy_reg;
31	    reg [63:0] chainin_reg;
32	
33	    // combinational middle: the four products and their sum, from the registers
34	    wire [17:0] prod_a = ax_reg * ay_reg;                        // 9x9 -> 18, exact
35	    wire [17:0] prod_b = bx_reg * by_reg;
36	    wire [17:0] prod_c = cx_reg * cy_reg;
37	    wire [17:0] prod_d = dx_reg * dy_reg;
38	    wire [63:0] sum    = prod_a + prod_b + prod_c + prod_d + chainin_reg;   // modulo 2^64
39	
40	    always @(posedge clk) begin
41	        if (reset) begin
42	            result <= 0;
43	            ax_reg <= 0; ay_reg <= 0; bx_reg <= 0; by_reg <= 0;
44	            cx_reg <= 0; cy_reg <= 0; dx_reg <= 0; dy_reg <= 0; chainin_reg <= 0;
45	        end
46	        else begin
47	            ax_reg <= ax; ay_reg <= ay; bx_reg <= bx; by_reg <= by;
48	            cx_reg <= cx; cy_reg <= cy; dx_reg <= dx; dy_reg <= dy; chainin_reg <= chainin;
49	            result <= sum;                                       // stage 2
50	        end
51	    end
52	
53	    assign chainout = sum;                                  // the sum of the input registers
54	
55	endmodule

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: int_sop_4 (precision INT9)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx*by + cx*cy + dx*dy + chainin
  • input ports: clk[1] (clock), reset[1], mode_sigs[12], ax[9], ay[9], bx[9], by[9], cx[9], cy[9], dx[9], dy[9], chainin[64]
  • output ports: result[64], chainout[64]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 64 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 64 bits (modulo 2^64), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: on clk, the block registers its operands (ax, ay, bx, by, cx, cy, dx, dy) at one clock edge and result at the next, with the arithmetic between the two registers: operands applied before clock edge k appear in result after edge k+1, 2 cycles later. The block has no clock enable and no path around either register. chainin is registered at the block's entry like an operand and reaches result 2 cycles after it is applied. chainout is combinational from the input registers: it carries the value result loads at the next clock edge, one cycle before result shows it.
  • reset: reset is synchronous and active high: at a clock edge that samples it high it clears every register of the block (the operand registers, the chainin register and the result register) to 0, and the block loads again at the next edge that samples it low.
  • power-up: every register of the block is unknown until the first clear by reset; no register of the block has an initial value, and a rewrite may not rely on one.
  • tie-off: chainin = 0 when the block is not chained (a dedicated chain input: only another block's chainout or a constant may drive it); mode_sigs = 0 always (the architecture gives the port no meaning for this mode).
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above; a product-term port the rewrite does not use is tied to 0. chainout reaches only the next block's chainin, through a dedicated connection to the block directly below it in the column; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Check
  • Every claim the plan makes about the design (who reads a value, a register's reset or enable, widths, cited lines, ASSUMES lines) against the source.
  • That the mapping as described keeps the same behavior.
  • That the plan states everything the planner's output section requires, listed below.

Do not judge cost or style; measurement decides cost.

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds, and how many DSP tiles the design then uses.
  • The longest series of blocks in any stage and its delay, against the slowest stage.
  • What soft logic leaves which stage, and whether that stage is the slowest.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output
  • First line exactly APPROVE or REVISE.
  • If REVISE, for each problem: the rule it violates or the required item it omits, by name; the design lines; what to change.
  • Write nothing before the verdict line; read the source first. The verdict is applied automatically and no person reads it, so do not end with a question or an offer.
What is currently built and measured

PLAN:

What is converted, and what is left

  1. All 46 fltr_compute candidates (f1,f2,f3,h1,h2,h3,h4) are converted exactly as in the kept candidate: keep that edit verbatim (the seven folded sums, the three 9-bit pre-adds, the ext*_d1/ext*_d2 sign-extension corrections for f1, f3 and h4, reset tied to 1'b0). It already measured -39% on the product and is not touched by this revision.
  2. 31 of the 45 my_fir candidates are converted: in every my_fir module the products of n_delay_reg2, n_delay_reg3 (where present), n_delay_reg4, n_delay_reg5 and n_delay_reg6 move onto blocks. Because the taps are symmetric (c4=c2, c5=c1, c6=c0, cited at lines 1440-1449, 1500-1506, 1561-1567, 1616-1625, 1675-1681, 1734-1740, 1792-1798), those five products fold into four: c2*(n2+n4) + c3*n3 + c5*n5 + c6*n6. The taps are 16 bits and the block's ports are 9, so each tap is split into bytes and the four products are formed once over the high bytes and once over the low bytes: sum = 256*HI + LO, exactly. Operands stay inside 9 bits: a byte pair sums to at most 510, a single byte to 255, and every coefficient is at most 255. The whole sum is at most 673*65535 = 44.1e6 < 2^28, so neither the original nor the rewrite truncates and the unsigned block arithmetic matches the unsigned source arithmetic bit for bit.
  3. 14 my_fir candidates are left, all for one reason: they are the two newest samples of the window (din * c0 at lines 1486, 1542, 1602, 1661, 1716, 1775, 1833 and n_delay_reg1 * c1 at lines 1487, 1543, 1603, 1662, 1717, 1776, 1834). A readable block result costs 2 cycles (chainout is 1 cycle but reaches only another block's chainin, so soft logic cannot read it), while dout loads one cycle after din is presented. din's value is produced by the upstream fltr_compute dout register and does not exist two cycles early inside h_fltr, so c0*din must stay a soft/DSP multiply feeding the last adder of the dout stage. The c1 term does not need the block either: since n_delay_reg1 is the enabled register of din, the enabled register q1_reg <= din*c1 holds exactly c1*n_delay_reg1 at every cycle, so that product moves one cycle earlier into its own short stage and leaves the dout stage as a register input.

Why the operands are the advanced taps, and why this is exact

The block answers two cycles after its operands are applied, so at cycle c it must be given the tap values that will stand at cycle c+2. The delay line advances by sh = e(c) + e(c+1) steps over those two cycles, with e the enable new_data_rdy. e(c) is the module's own input; e(c+1) is available at cycle c because v_nd_s1_left and its five siblings are plain unconditional registers of the top-level inputs v_nd_s*_*_2to0 (lines 430-438, 188-197), so the unregistered strobe is the next cycle's enable. Hence new_data_rdy_nxt. Expanding the delay line twice gives n_k(c+2) = n_{k-sh}(c) for k >= 2 (with n_0 = din), in all four (e(c),e(c+1)) cases; k=1 would need n_{-1}, which is why tap 1 is left out of the block. Those are the p2..p6 of the MAPPING. Every p is a value already held in a register of the module, so the rewrite is defined exactly when the original is: for a given load edge the block sees the identical sample values, only read earlier out of earlier registers, so the X behaviour at start-up is unchanged as well. reset is tied to 0 on every block: the design never clears these pipelines, and the testbench pulses reset mid-run, so clearing the block there would diverge. No block register is relied on for an initial value; each is reloaded every cycle and washes out within two cycles, inside the hundreds of cycles the 226/316/496-deep fifos take to flush.

Blocks and tiles

126 blocks: 42 for the fltr_compute reductions (one per instance, 7 modules x 6 v_fltr instances) and 84 for the my_fir reductions (two per instance, 7 modules x 6 h_fltr instances). Each takes its DSP tile alone. The remaining multiplies in the design are the two per my_fir instance (din*c0 and din*c1), 84 of them, which pack about two to a two_mult_18x19 tile, ~45 tiles. Total ~171 tiles, against 224 in the baseline and 187 measured for the kept candidate; the device has 306.

Stages and delay

No stage holds two blocks in series: every block is fed from design registers and read from its own result register, so the longest series of blocks in any stage is one, 2.219 ns inside the block, well under the slowest stage. No chainout is used.

The slowest stage of the kept candidate, 11.4491 ns, is the my_fir stage: one 18x19 multiply, six adder levels with their carry chains, one LUT, into the enabled flip-flop. That stage is what this rewrite empties. What leaves it: all six adder levels and five of the seven multiplies. What is left in it: the single multiply din*c0 and three adders, written so the multiply feeds only the final adder — 0.060 (din clock-to-Q) + ~1.0 wire + 2.140 multiply + 0.544 wire + one ~28-bit carry chain + 0.019 setup, about 4.7 ns; the q1_reg/sop_lo path through the three adders is about 4.9 ns. The new stages the rewrite creates are both shorter: tap register to block input is 0.060 + 0.960 + one mux LUT + one 8-bit carry chain + 1.419 + 0.019, about 3.7 ns, and din to q1_reg is 0.060 + ~1.0 + 2.140 + 0.019, about 3.2 ns. The fltr_compute stages are unchanged from the kept candidate and are shorter still.

With the my_fir stage down to ~4.9 ns, the slowest stage left in the design is in steer_fltr (lines 640-643): three levels of 31-bit add/subtract from im_p_tmp_1..4 into im_p_tmp, roughly 0.060 + 0.960 + three carry-chain levels with their wires + 0.019, about 5.9 ns. That stage is untouched by the rewrite and sets STAGE_NS. It is an estimate off the sampled wire and adder figures, not a measured path; the period should land near it, between about 5.5 and 7 ns, against 11.4491.

Register stages, before and after

  • fltr_compute (all 46 regions): before, din -> q1..q7 (1 stage) -> d_out_tmp (2nd) -> dout (3rd). After, din -> block input register (1st) -> block result register (2nd) -> dout (3rd). Three stages before and after, same values at the same edges; the sign-extension correction is delayed two cycles by ext*_d1/ext*_d2 to land with the block result.
  • my_fir (all 31 converted regions): before, the taps are registers and the products and their six-level sum are combinational into the enabled dout, one register stage from tap to dout. After, the same tap values are presented to the block two cycles before that edge, pass the block's input register and result register, and are added into the same dout register at the same edge with the same value — the sample-to-dout latency is unchanged, no register is added on the din-to-dout path, and the new q1_reg holds c1*n_delay_reg1, the value the original computed combinationally at that edge.

Edit notes for the editor

Keep the kept candidate's fltr_compute edit exactly as it stands. In each my_fir module: add the new_data_rdy_nxt input at the end of the port list, add reg[23:0] q1_reg;, the sh/p2..p6 wires, the two 9-bit pre-adds, the two int_sop_4 instances, keep n_delay_reg1..6 and output_data_ready as they are, add q1_reg <= din * c1; inside the if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1) branch, and replace the seven-term dout <= ... with the parenthesised form of the MAPPING (the parenthesisation matters: it keeps the multiply one adder level from the register). In h_fltr add the input vidin_new_data_nxt at the end of its port list and pass it as the last argument of all seven my_fir instantiations (lines 514-520). At the top, add the matching last argument to the six h_fltr instantiations (lines 188-190, 195-197). The top's own port list does not change.

1	// int_sop_4: result = ax*ay + bx*by + cx*cy + dx*dy + chainin, unsigned, each 9x9 product
2	// zero-extended into a 64-bit sum, modulo 2^64 (the sum wraps at the result width).
3	// Ports: clk, reset, mode_sigs[12], ax, ay, bx, by, cx, cy, dx, dy [9 each], chainin[64] in;
4	// result[64], chainout[64] out. mode_sigs is not read.
5	// Registers (the arch's annotation read literally, decision 2026-10-16): every input is registered
6	// at the block's entry at one clock edge (the eight operands and chainin alike); the
7	// products and their sum are formed from those registers and loaded into result at the next edge.
8	// Cycles: every operand and chainin to result 2. chainout is combinational from the input
9	// registers: the sum result loads at the next edge unless that edge clears it (1 cycle from the
10	// inputs).
11	// Reset: synchronous, active high (2026-10-17: the arch's annotation does not distinguish a reset
12	// register from a clear sampled by the registers themselves): at a clock edge that samples it high
13	// every register of the block (operand registers, chainin register, result) is cleared to 0; the block
14	// loads again at the next edge that samples it low. No register has an initial value: every one is
15	// X until the first clear.
16	module int_sop_4 (
17	    input clk,
18	    input reset,
19	    input [11:0] mode_sigs,
20	    input [8:0] ax, input [8:0] ay,
21	    input [8:0] bx, input [8:0] by,
22	    input [8:0] cx, input [8:0] cy,
23	    input [8:0] dx, input [8:0] dy,
24	    input [63:0] chainin,
25	    output reg [63:0] result,
26	    output [63:0] chainout
27	);
28	
29	    // stage 1: the input registers
30	    reg [8:0]  ax_reg, ay_reg, bx_reg, by_reg, cx_reg, cy_reg, dx_reg, dy_reg;
31	    reg [63:0] chainin_reg;
32	
33	    // combinational middle: the four products and their sum, from the registers
34	    wire [17:0] prod_a = ax_reg * ay_reg;                        // 9x9 -> 18, exact
35	    wire [17:0] prod_b = bx_reg * by_reg;
36	    wire [17:0] prod_c = cx_reg * cy_reg;
37	    wire [17:0] prod_d = dx_reg * dy_reg;
38	    wire [63:0] sum    = prod_a + prod_b + prod_c + prod_d + chainin_reg;   // modulo 2^64
39	
40	    always @(posedge clk) begin
41	        if (reset) begin
42	            result <= 0;
43	            ax_reg <= 0; ay_reg <= 0; bx_reg <= 0; by_reg <= 0;
44	            cx_reg <= 0; cy_reg <= 0; dx_reg <= 0; dy_reg <= 0; chainin_reg <= 0;
45	        end
46	        else begin
47	            ax_reg <= ax; ay_reg <= ay; bx_reg <= bx; by_reg <= by;
48	            cx_reg <= cx; cy_reg <= cy; dx_reg <= dx; dy_reg <= dy; chainin_reg <= chainin;
49	            result <= sum;                                       // stage 2
50	        end
51	    end
52	
53	    assign chainout = sum;                                  // the sum of the input registers
54	
55	endmodule

Task

Edit stereovision2.v in this directory to carry out the approved plan below: rewrite the regions it names onto the hard block described next. If a step cannot be done as the plan says, stop and say which step and why; do not improvise a different rewrite.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: int_sop_4 (precision INT9)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx*by + cx*cy + dx*dy + chainin
  • input ports: clk[1] (clock), reset[1], mode_sigs[12], ax[9], ay[9], bx[9], by[9], cx[9], cy[9], dx[9], dy[9], chainin[64]
  • output ports: result[64], chainout[64]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 64 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 64 bits (modulo 2^64), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: on clk, the block registers its operands (ax, ay, bx, by, cx, cy, dx, dy) at one clock edge and result at the next, with the arithmetic between the two registers: operands applied before clock edge k appear in result after edge k+1, 2 cycles later. The block has no clock enable and no path around either register. chainin is registered at the block's entry like an operand and reaches result 2 cycles after it is applied. chainout is combinational from the input registers: it carries the value result loads at the next clock edge, one cycle before result shows it.
  • reset: reset is synchronous and active high: at a clock edge that samples it high it clears every register of the block (the operand registers, the chainin register and the result register) to 0, and the block loads again at the next edge that samples it low.
  • power-up: every register of the block is unknown until the first clear by reset; no register of the block has an initial value, and a rewrite may not rely on one.
  • tie-off: chainin = 0 when the block is not chained (a dedicated chain input: only another block's chainout or a constant may drive it); mode_sigs = 0 always (the architecture gives the port no meaning for this mode).
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above; a product-term port the rewrite does not use is tied to 0. chainout reaches only the next block's chainin, through a dedicated connection to the block directly below it in the column; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it.

  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.

What is converted, and what is left

  1. All 46 fltr_compute candidates (f1,f2,f3,h1,h2,h3,h4) are converted exactly as in the kept candidate: keep that edit verbatim (the seven folded sums, the three 9-bit pre-adds, the ext*_d1/ext*_d2 sign-extension corrections for f1, f3 and h4, reset tied to 1'b0). It already measured -39% on the product and is not touched by this revision.
  2. 31 of the 45 my_fir candidates are converted: in every my_fir module the products of n_delay_reg2, n_delay_reg3 (where present), n_delay_reg4, n_delay_reg5 and n_delay_reg6 move onto blocks. Because the taps are symmetric (c4=c2, c5=c1, c6=c0, cited at lines 1440-1449, 1500-1506, 1561-1567, 1616-1625, 1675-1681, 1734-1740, 1792-1798), those five products fold into four: c2*(n2+n4) + c3*n3 + c5*n5 + c6*n6. The taps are 16 bits and the block's ports are 9, so each tap is split into bytes and the four products are formed once over the high bytes and once over the low bytes: sum = 256*HI + LO, exactly. Operands stay inside 9 bits: a byte pair sums to at most 510, a single byte to 255, and every coefficient is at most 255. The whole sum is at most 673*65535 = 44.1e6 < 2^28, so neither the original nor the rewrite truncates and the unsigned block arithmetic matches the unsigned source arithmetic bit for bit.
  3. 14 my_fir candidates are left, all for one reason: they are the two newest samples of the window (din * c0 at lines 1486, 1542, 1602, 1661, 1716, 1775, 1833 and n_delay_reg1 * c1 at lines 1487, 1543, 1603, 1662, 1717, 1776, 1834). A readable block result costs 2 cycles (chainout is 1 cycle but reaches only another block's chainin, so soft logic cannot read it), while dout loads one cycle after din is presented. din's value is produced by the upstream fltr_compute dout register and does not exist two cycles early inside h_fltr, so c0*din must stay a soft/DSP multiply feeding the last adder of the dout stage. The c1 term does not need the block either: since n_delay_reg1 is the enabled register of din, the enabled register q1_reg <= din*c1 holds exactly c1*n_delay_reg1 at every cycle, so that product moves one cycle earlier into its own short stage and leaves the dout stage as a register input.

Why the operands are the advanced taps, and why this is exact

The block answers two cycles after its operands are applied, so at cycle c it must be given the tap values that will stand at cycle c+2. The delay line advances by sh = e(c) + e(c+1) steps over those two cycles, with e the enable new_data_rdy. e(c) is the module's own input; e(c+1) is available at cycle c because v_nd_s1_left and its five siblings are plain unconditional registers of the top-level inputs v_nd_s*_*_2to0 (lines 430-438, 188-197), so the unregistered strobe is the next cycle's enable. Hence new_data_rdy_nxt. Expanding the delay line twice gives n_k(c+2) = n_{k-sh}(c) for k >= 2 (with n_0 = din), in all four (e(c),e(c+1)) cases; k=1 would need n_{-1}, which is why tap 1 is left out of the block. Those are the p2..p6 of the MAPPING. Every p is a value already held in a register of the module, so the rewrite is defined exactly when the original is: for a given load edge the block sees the identical sample values, only read earlier out of earlier registers, so the X behaviour at start-up is unchanged as well. reset is tied to 0 on every block: the design never clears these pipelines, and the testbench pulses reset mid-run, so clearing the block there would diverge. No block register is relied on for an initial value; each is reloaded every cycle and washes out within two cycles, inside the hundreds of cycles the 226/316/496-deep fifos take to flush.

Blocks and tiles

126 blocks: 42 for the fltr_compute reductions (one per instance, 7 modules x 6 v_fltr instances) and 84 for the my_fir reductions (two per instance, 7 modules x 6 h_fltr instances). Each takes its DSP tile alone. The remaining multiplies in the design are the two per my_fir instance (din*c0 and din*c1), 84 of them, which pack about two to a two_mult_18x19 tile, ~45 tiles. Total ~171 tiles, against 224 in the baseline and 187 measured for the kept candidate; the device has 306.

Stages and delay

No stage holds two blocks in series: every block is fed from design registers and read from its own result register, so the longest series of blocks in any stage is one, 2.219 ns inside the block, well under the slowest stage. No chainout is used.

The slowest stage of the kept candidate, 11.4491 ns, is the my_fir stage: one 18x19 multiply, six adder levels with their carry chains, one LUT, into the enabled flip-flop. That stage is what this rewrite empties. What leaves it: all six adder levels and five of the seven multiplies. What is left in it: the single multiply din*c0 and three adders, written so the multiply feeds only the final adder — 0.060 (din clock-to-Q) + ~1.0 wire + 2.140 multiply + 0.544 wire + one ~28-bit carry chain + 0.019 setup, about 4.7 ns; the q1_reg/sop_lo path through the three adders is about 4.9 ns. The new stages the rewrite creates are both shorter: tap register to block input is 0.060 + 0.960 + one mux LUT + one 8-bit carry chain + 1.419 + 0.019, about 3.7 ns, and din to q1_reg is 0.060 + ~1.0 + 2.140 + 0.019, about 3.2 ns. The fltr_compute stages are unchanged from the kept candidate and are shorter still.

With the my_fir stage down to ~4.9 ns, the slowest stage left in the design is in steer_fltr (lines 640-643): three levels of 31-bit add/subtract from im_p_tmp_1..4 into im_p_tmp, roughly 0.060 + 0.960 + three carry-chain levels with their wires + 0.019, about 5.9 ns. That stage is untouched by the rewrite and sets STAGE_NS. It is an estimate off the sampled wire and adder figures, not a measured path; the period should land near it, between about 5.5 and 7 ns, against 11.4491.

Register stages, before and after

  • fltr_compute (all 46 regions): before, din -> q1..q7 (1 stage) -> d_out_tmp (2nd) -> dout (3rd). After, din -> block input register (1st) -> block result register (2nd) -> dout (3rd). Three stages before and after, same values at the same edges; the sign-extension correction is delayed two cycles by ext*_d1/ext*_d2 to land with the block result.
  • my_fir (all 31 converted regions): before, the taps are registers and the products and their six-level sum are combinational into the enabled dout, one register stage from tap to dout. After, the same tap values are presented to the block two cycles before that edge, pass the block's input register and result register, and are added into the same dout register at the same edge with the same value — the sample-to-dout latency is unchanged, no register is added on the din-to-dout path, and the new q1_reg holds c1*n_delay_reg1, the value the original computed combinationally at that edge.

Edit notes for the editor

Keep the kept candidate's fltr_compute edit exactly as it stands. In each my_fir module: add the new_data_rdy_nxt input at the end of the port list, add reg[23:0] q1_reg;, the sh/p2..p6 wires, the two 9-bit pre-adds, the two int_sop_4 instances, keep n_delay_reg1..6 and output_data_ready as they are, add q1_reg <= din * c1; inside the if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1) branch, and replace the seven-term dout <= ... with the parenthesised form of the MAPPING (the parenthesisation matters: it keeps the multiply one adder level from the register). In h_fltr add the input vidin_new_data_nxt at the end of its port list and pass it as the last argument of all seven my_fir instantiations (lines 514-520). At the top, add the matching last argument to the six h_fltr instantiations (lines 188-190, 195-197). The top's own port list does not change.

Simulation

When you finish, the framework simulates your edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output on every cycle, on its own copy. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (int_sop_4.v) are in sim_reference/; you may read them, but editing them has no effect on the result.

What changed, region by region

fltr_compute_{f1,f2,f3,h1,h2,h3,h4} — all 46 regions (42 block instances, one per instance of each module)

Each module's seven q1..q7 multiplies and the d_out_tmp sum became one int_sop_4. The symmetric tap pairs are folded into 9-bit pre-adds ahead of the block: s1 = din[55:48]+din[7:0], s2 = din[47:40]+din[15:8], s3 = din[39:32]+din[23:16], with dx = {1'b0,din[31:24]} (tied to 9'd0 in f3/h1/h3, whose centre coefficient is 0). Coefficients as in the plan: f1 (29,101,17,277), f2/h2 (4,42,163,255), f3 (20,179,364,0), h1 (17,25,193,0), h3 (23,72,147,0), h4 (14,43,80,324). reset = 1'b0, mode_sigs = 12'd0, chainin = 64'd0, chainout unconnected.

The original summed 17-bit products sign-extended into bits 19:17, so where a product can reach 2^16 the extension is reproduced outside the block as +20'hE0000 per set sign bit, derived by a comparator on the input byte (no multiplier) and held back two cycles (ext_d1/ext_d2) to land with result: f1 din[31:24]>=237 (q4), f3 din[39:32]>=181 and din[23:16]>=181 (q3,q5), h4 din[31:24]>=203 (q4). f2, h1, h2, h3 cannot set bit 16 and need no correction. dout <= (result[19:0] + ext)[18:3] keeps the original's three register stages and its mod-2^20 wrap.

my_fir_{f1,f2,f3,h1,h2,h3,h4} — 31 of the 45 regions (84 block instances, two per instance)

The n_delay_reg2..6 products became two blocks per instance, split by tap byte: 256*sop_hi + sop_lo, with ax = p2[hi/lo]+p4[hi/lo] against c2 (the c4=c2 fold), bx = p3 against c3, cx = p5 against c5, dx = p6 against c6. f3, h1, h3 and h4 have no n_delay_reg3 term, so their bx/by are tied to 9'd0 and p3 is dropped. Because the block answers two cycles later, the operands are the advanced taps p2..p6, selected by sh = new_data_rdy + new_data_rdy_nxt. reset = 1'b0, mode_sigs = 12'd0, chainin = 64'd0, chainout unconnected.

The 14 regions for din*COEF0 and n_delay_reg1*COEF1 stay in soft logic, as the plan specifies: the c1 product moved one cycle earlier into the new enabled register q1_reg <= din * COEF1 (equal to COEF1*n_delay_reg1 at every cycle, since both load from din on the same enable), and dout <= ((q1_reg + sop_lo[19:0]) + {sop_hi[19:0],8'd0}) + (din * COEF0).

Wiring (plan item C): new input new_data_rdy_nxt at the end of each my_fir port list, fed from a new vidin_new_data_nxt input at the end of h_fltr's port list, driven at the top by the unregistered strobe of each stream (v_nd_s{1,2,4}_{left,right}_2to0) on the six h_fltr instances. v_nd_s*_* are plain unconditional registers of those strobes (lines 430-441), so this is next cycle's enable. The top module's own port list is unchanged.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Inner-loop check: the front end of the real flow, then a cell census. NOT place-and-route.
# usage: bash check.sh <file.v>
# Reads, in the flow's order: blocks.vlib (every hard block of the architecture, declared from its
# models), primitives.vlib (the flow's library of memories, adders and multipliers), then the design;
# then elaborates with the flow's hierarchy check. A module that is not defined, a port name the
# block does not have, or a misspelled block name fails here as it would in the flow. Do not
# declare the target block in the design: blocks.vlib declares it, and a design that defines a module
# of the target block's name fails this check.
# Prints one pass/fail line, then the cell census of the whole design (the last "Number of cells"
# table yosys prints): soft arithmetic as $mul/$add/$sub, registers as $dff*/$sdff*, memories as
# $mem*, muxes as $mux/$pmux, and every instantiated module by name, which is where a hard-block
# instantiation shows up with its instance count.
set -u
f="${1:?usage: check.sh <file.v>}"
here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
lib=""
[ -f "$here/blocks.vlib" ] && lib="read_verilog -lib $here/blocks.vlib; "
[ -f "$here/primitives.vlib" ] && lib="${lib}read_verilog -nomem2reg $here/primitives.vlib; "
target="$(sed -n 's|^// target block: *\([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*\).*|\1|p' "$here/blocks.vlib" 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
if [ -n "$target" ] && grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*module[[:space:]]+$target([^A-Za-z0-9_$]|$)" "$f"; then
  echo "FAIL: $f defines module $target; blocks.vlib declares it. Remove the module definition and keep the instances."
  exit 1
fi
out="$(yosys -p "${lib}read_verilog -sv -nolatches $f; hierarchy -check -auto-top -purge_lib; proc; opt; stat" 2>&1)"
rc=$?
if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL: does not synthesize (yosys exit $rc)"
  echo "$out" | grep -iE 'error|warning' | tail -15
  echo "$out" | tail -10
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: synthesizes cleanly"
echo "Cell census (yosys stat, whole design):"
echo "$out" | awk '/Number of cells:/{buf=$0 "\n"; on=1; next}
                   on && /^[[:space:]]+[$A-Za-z_][^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+[0-9]+[[:space:]]*$/ {buf=buf $0 "\n"; next}
                   on {on=0}
                   END{printf "%s", buf}' \
  | grep -E 'Number of cells|^[[:space:]]+(\$(mul|add|sub|mem|memrd|memwr|dff|dffe|sdff|sdffe|adff|adffe|mux|pmux)|[A-Za-z_])' || true

 "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n# Rewrites the seven fltr_compute modules and the seven my_fir modules of\n# stereovision2.v onto int_sop_4 blocks, as the approved plan describes.\nimport sys\n\npath = sys.argv[1]\nsrc = open(path).read()\n\n\ndef replace_module(src, name, new_text):\n    start = src.index(\"module %s (\" % name)\n    end = src.index(\"endmodule\", start) + len(\"endmodule\")\n    return src[:start] + new_text + src[end:]\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------- fltr_compute\n# (c1, c2, c3, c4): c1 on din[55:48] and din[7:0], c2 on din[47:40] and din[15:8],\n# c3 on din[39:32] and din[23:16], c4 on din[31:24].\n# ext: the (slice, threshold) of every product whose 17-bit result can set bit 16,\n# which the original sum sign-extends into bits 19:17.\nFLTR = {\n    \"f1\": ((29, 101, 17, 277), [(\"31:24\", 237)]),\n    \"f2\": ((4, 42, 163, 255), []),\n    \"f3\": ((20, 179, 364, 0), [(\"39:32\", 181), (\"23:16\", 181)]),\n    \"h1\": ((17, 25, 193, 0), []),\n    \"h2\": ((4, 42, 163, 255), []),\n    \"h3\": ((23, 72, 147, 0), []),\n    \"h4\": ((14, 43, 80, 324), [(\"31:24\", 203)]),\n}\n\nFLTR_TMPL = \"\"\"module fltr_compute_%(n)s (clk, din, dout);\n\n    input clk;\n    input[55:0] din;\n    output[15:0] dout;\n    reg[15:0] dout;\n    wire[63:0] sop_res;\n    // the pairs of taps that share a coefficient, folded before the block\n    wire[8:0] s1 = din[55:48] + din[7:0];\n    wire[8:0] s2 = din[47:40] + din[15:8];\n    wire[8:0] s3 = din[39:32] + din[23:16];\n%(extdecl)s\n    int_sop_4 inst_sop (.clk(clk), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0),\n                        .ax(s1), .ay(9'd%(c1)d),\n                        .bx(s2), .by(9'd%(c2)d),\n                        .cx(s3), .cy(9'd%(c3)d),\n                        .dx(%(dx)s), .dy(9'd%(c4)d),\n                        .chainin(64'b0), .result(sop_res), .chainout());\n\n    always @(posedge clk)\n    begin\n%(extseq)s          dout <= %(dsum)s;\n    end\n endmodule\"\"\"\n\n\ndef fltr_module(n):\n    (c1, c2, c3, c4), ext = FLTR[n]\n    dx = \"9'd0\" if c4 == 0 else \"{1'b0, din[31:24]}\"\n    if not ext:\n        extdecl, extseq, dsum = \"\", \"\", \"sop_res[18:3]\"\n    else:\n        # the sign bit of each product that can set it, held back the two cycles\n        # the block takes, then added back where the original sign extension put it\n        conds = \"\".join(\n            \"    wire ext%d = (din[%s] >= 8'd%d); \\n\" % (i, sl, th)\n            for i, (sl, th) in enumerate(ext)\n        )\n        w = len(ext)\n        bits = \"{%s}\" % \", \".join(\"ext%d\" % i for i in reversed(range(w))) if w > 1 else \"ext0\"\n        reg = \"    reg[%d:0] ext_d1; \\n    reg[%d:0] ext_d2; \\n\" % (w - 1, w - 1)\n        terms = \" + \".join(\n            \"(ext_d2%s ? 20'hE0000 : 20'h00000)\" % (\"[%d]\" % i if w > 1 else \"\")\n            for i in range(w)\n        )\n        extdecl = conds + reg + \"    wire[19:0] d_out_sum = sop_res[19:0] + %s; \\n\" % terms\n        extseq = \"          ext_d1 <= %s; \\n          ext_d2 <= ext_d1; \\n\" % bits\n        dsum = \"d_out_sum[18:3]\"\n    return FLTR_TMPL % dict(n=n, c1=c1, c2=c2, c3=c3, c4=c4, dx=dx,\n                            extdecl=extdecl, extseq=extseq, dsum=dsum)\n\n\nfor n in FLTR:\n    src = replace_module(src, \"fltr_compute_\" + n, fltr_module(n))\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------- my_fir\n# suffix of the coefficient macros, and (c2, c3, c5, c6); c3 is None where the\n# module has no n_delay_reg3 term.\nFIR = {\n    \"f1\": (\"b\", (15, 235, 101, 29)),\n    \"f2\": (\"c\", (163, 255, 42, 4)),\n    \"f3\": (\"d\", (148, None, 77, 12)),\n    \"h1\": (\"1\", (193, None, 25, 15)),\n    \"h2\": (\"2\", (163, 255, 42, 4)),\n    \"h3\": (\"3\", (109, None, 56, 9)),\n    \"h4\": (\"4\", (109, None, 56, 9)),\n}\n\nFIR_TMPL = \"\"\"module my_fir_%(n)s (clk, new_data_rdy, output_data_ready, din, dout, new_data_rdy_nxt);\n\n//coefdata=%(coefdata)s;\n\n    input clk;\n    input[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] din;\n    output[28 - 1:0] dout;\n    reg[28 - 1:0] dout;\n\tinput new_data_rdy;\n\tinput new_data_rdy_nxt;\n\toutput output_data_ready;\n\treg output_data_ready;\n\n    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg1;\n    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg2;\n    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg3;\n    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg4;\n    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg5;\n    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg6;\n\n    reg[23:0] q1_reg;\n    wire[63:0] sop_hi;\n    wire[63:0] sop_lo;\n    // the blocks answer two cycles from now: give them the taps as they will\n    // stand then, the delay line having advanced by this cycle's enable and the\n    // next one's\n    wire[1:0] sh = new_data_rdy + new_data_rdy_nxt;\n    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p2 = (sh == 2'd0) ? n_delay_reg2 : (sh == 2'd1) ? n_delay_reg1 : din;\n%(p3decl)s    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p4 = (sh == 2'd0) ? n_delay_reg4 : (sh == 2'd1) ? n_delay_reg3 : n_delay_reg2;\n    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p5 = (sh == 2'd0) ? n_delay_reg5 : (sh == 2'd1) ? n_delay_reg4 : n_delay_reg3;\n    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p6 = (sh == 2'd0) ? n_delay_reg6 : (sh == 2'd1) ? n_delay_reg5 : n_delay_reg4;\n    // the taps split by byte: the sum of the products is 256 * sop_hi + sop_lo\n    wire[8:0] ax_hi = p2[15:8] + p4[15:8];\n    wire[8:0] ax_lo = p2[7:0] + p4[7:0];\n\n    int_sop_4 inst_sop_hi (.clk(clk), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0),\n                           .ax(ax_hi), .ay(9'd%(c2)d),\n                           .bx(%(bxhi)s), .by(%(by)s),\n                           .cx({1'b0, p5[15:8]}), .cy(9'd%(c5)d),\n                           .dx({1'b0, p6[15:8]}), .dy(9'd%(c6)d),\n                           .chainin(64'b0), .result(sop_hi), .chainout());\n    int_sop_4 inst_sop_lo (.clk(clk), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0),\n                           .ax(ax_lo), .ay(9'd%(c2)d),\n                           .bx(%(bxlo)s), .by(%(by)s),\n                           .cx({1'b0, p5[7:0]}), .cy(9'd%(c5)d),\n                           .dx({1'b0, p6[7:0]}), .dy(9'd%(c6)d),\n                           .chainin(64'b0), .result(sop_lo), .chainout());\n\n    always @(posedge clk)\n    begin\n\t\tif (new_data_rdy == 1'b1)\n\t\tbegin\n\t\t\tn_delay_reg1 <= din;\n\t\t\tn_delay_reg2 <= n_delay_reg1;\n\t\t\tn_delay_reg3 <= n_delay_reg2;\n\t\t\tn_delay_reg4 <= n_delay_reg3;\n\t\t\tn_delay_reg5 <= n_delay_reg4;\n\t\t\tn_delay_reg6 <= n_delay_reg5;\n\n\t\t\t// q1_reg holds `COEF1_%(s)s * n_delay_reg1: both load from din on the same enable\n\t\t\tq1_reg <= din * `COEF1_%(s)s;\n\n\t\t\toutput_data_ready <= 1'b1;\n\t\t\tdout <= ((q1_reg + sop_lo[19:0]) + {sop_hi[19:0], 8'd0}) + (din * `COEF0_%(s)s);\n\t\tend\n\t\telse\n\t\tbegin\n\t\t\toutput_data_ready <= 1'b0;\n\t\tend\n\tend\nendmodule\"\"\"\n\n\ndef fir_module(n):\n    s, (c2, c3, c5, c6) = FIR[n]\n    coefdata = \",\".join(str(x) for x in\n                        [None, None, c2, c3, c2, c5, c6][2:])  # placeholder, replaced below\n    if c3 is None:\n        p3decl = \"\"\n        bxhi = bxlo = \"9'd0\"\n        by = \"9'd0\"\n        coefs = [c6, c5, c2, 0, c2, c5, c6]\n    else:\n        p3decl = \"    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p3 = (sh == 2'd0) ? n_delay_reg3 : (sh == 2'd1) ? n_delay_reg2 : n_delay_reg1; \\n\"\n        bxhi = \"{1'b0, p3[15:8]}\"\n        bxlo = \"{1'b0, p3[7:0]}\"\n        by = \"9'd%d\" % c3\n        coefs = [c6, c5, c2, c3, c2, c5, c6]\n    coefdata = \",\".join(str(x) for x in coefs)\n    return FIR_TMPL % dict(n=n, s=s, c2=c2, c5=c5, c6=c6, by=by,\n                           bxhi=bxhi, bxlo=bxlo, p3decl=p3decl, coefdata=coefdata)\n\n\nfor n in FIR:\n    src = replace_module(src, \"my_fir_\" + n, fir_module(n))\n\nopen(path, \"w\").write(src)\nprint(\"rewrote %d modules\" % (len(FLTR) + len(FIR)))\n"
}

module fltr_compute_f1 (clk, din, dout);

    input clk;
    input[55:0] din;
    output[15:0] dout;
    reg[15:0] dout;
    wire[63:0] sop_res;
    // the pairs of taps that share a coefficient, folded before the block
    wire[8:0] s1 = din[55:48] + din[7:0];
    wire[8:0] s2 = din[47:40] + din[15:8];
    wire[8:0] s3 = din[39:32] + din[23:16];
    wire ext0 = (din[31:24] >= 8'd237); 
    reg[0:0] ext_d1; 
    reg[0:0] ext_d2; 
    wire[19:0] d_out_sum = sop_res[19:0] + (ext_d2 ? 20'hE0000 : 20'h00000); 

    int_sop_4 inst_sop (.clk(clk), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0),
                        .ax(s1), .ay(9'd29),
                        .bx(s2), .by(9'd101),
                        .cx(s3), .cy(9'd17),
                        .dx({1'b0, din[31:24]}), .dy(9'd277),
                        .chainin(64'b0), .result(sop_res), .chainout());

    always @(posedge clk)
    begin
          ext_d1 <= ext0; 
          ext_d2 <= ext_d1; 
          dout <= d_out_sum[18:3];
    end
 endmodule
=== f3 ===
module fltr_compute_f3 (clk, din, dout);

    input clk;
    input[55:0] din;
    output[15:0] dout;
    reg[15:0] dout;
    wire[63:0] sop_res;
    // the pairs of taps that share a coefficient, folded before the block
    wire[8:0] s1 = din[55:48] + din[7:0];
    wire[8:0] s2 = din[47:40] + din[15:8];
    wire[8:0] s3 = din[39:32] + din[23:16];
    wire ext0 = (din[39:32] >= 8'd181); 
    wire ext1 = (din[23:16] >= 8'd181); 
    reg[1:0] ext_d1; 
    reg[1:0] ext_d2; 
    wire[19:0] d_out_sum = sop_res[19:0] + (ext_d2[0] ? 20'hE0000 : 20'h00000) + (ext_d2[1] ? 20'hE0000 : 20'h00000); 

    int_sop_4 inst_sop (.clk(clk), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0),
                        .ax(s1), .ay(9'd20),
                        .bx(s2), .by(9'd179),
                        .cx(s3), .cy(9'd364),
                        .dx(9'd0), .dy(9'd0),
                        .chainin(64'b0), .result(sop_res), .chainout());

    always @(posedge clk)
    begin
          ext_d1 <= {ext1, ext0}; 
          ext_d2 <= ext_d1; 
          dout <= d_out_sum[18:3];
    end
 endmodule

module my_fir_f1 (clk, new_data_rdy, output_data_ready, din, dout, new_data_rdy_nxt);

//coefdata=29,101,-15,-235,-15,101,29;

    input clk;
    input[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] din;
    output[28 - 1:0] dout;
    reg[28 - 1:0] dout;
	input new_data_rdy;
	input new_data_rdy_nxt;
	output output_data_ready;
	reg output_data_ready;

    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg1;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg2;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg3;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg4;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg5;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg6;

    reg[23:0] q1_reg;
    wire[63:0] sop_hi;
    wire[63:0] sop_lo;
    // the blocks answer two cycles from now: give them the taps as they will
    // stand then, the delay line having advanced by this cycle's enable and the
    // next one's
    wire[1:0] sh = new_data_rdy + new_data_rdy_nxt;
    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p2 = (sh == 2'd0) ? n_delay_reg2 : (sh == 2'd1) ? n_delay_reg1 : din;
    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p3 = (sh == 2'd0) ? n_delay_reg3 : (sh == 2'd1) ? n_delay_reg2 : n_delay_reg1; 
    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p4 = (sh == 2'd0) ? n_delay_reg4 : (sh == 2'd1) ? n_delay_reg3 : n_delay_reg2;
    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p5 = (sh == 2'd0) ? n_delay_reg5 : (sh == 2'd1) ? n_delay_reg4 : n_delay_reg3;
    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p6 = (sh == 2'd0) ? n_delay_reg6 : (sh == 2'd1) ? n_delay_reg5 : n_delay_reg4;
    // the taps split by byte: the sum of the products is 256 * sop_hi + sop_lo
    wire[8:0] ax_hi = p2[15:8] + p4[15:8];
    wire[8:0] ax_lo = p2[7:0] + p4[7:0];

    int_sop_4 inst_sop_hi (.clk(clk), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0),
                           .ax(ax_hi), .ay(9'd15),
                           .bx({1'b0, p3[15:8]}), .by(9'd235),
                           .cx({1'b0, p5[15:8]}), .cy(9'd101),
                           .dx({1'b0, p6[15:8]}), .dy(9'd29),
                           .chainin(64'b0), .result(sop_hi), .chainout());
    int_sop_4 inst_sop_lo (.clk(clk), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0),
                           .ax(ax_lo), .ay(9'd15),
                           .bx({1'b0, p3[7:0]}), .by(9'd235),
                           .cx({1'b0, p5[7:0]}), .cy(9'd101),
                           .dx({1'b0, p6[7:0]}), .dy(9'd29),
                           .chainin(64'b0), .result(sop_lo), .chainout());

    always @(posedge clk)
    begin
		if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1)
		begin
			n_delay_reg1 <= din;
			n_delay_reg2 <= n_delay_reg1;
			n_delay_reg3 <= n_delay_reg2;
			n_delay_reg4 <= n_delay_reg3;
			n_delay_reg5 <= n_delay_reg4;
			n_delay_reg6 <= n_delay_reg5;

			// q1_reg holds `COEF1_b * n_delay_reg1: both load from din on the same enable
			q1_reg <= din * `COEF1_b;

			output_data_ready <= 1'b1;
			dout <= ((q1_reg + sop_lo[19:0]) + {sop_hi[19:0], 8'd0}) + (din * `COEF0_b);
		end
		else
		begin
			output_data_ready <= 1'b0;
		end
	end
endmodule

You are the acceptance reviewer. You did not plan or write this edit. Check the edit against the approved plan, the block's contract and the correctness rules.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: int_sop_4 (precision INT9)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx*by + cx*cy + dx*dy + chainin
  • input ports: clk[1] (clock), reset[1], mode_sigs[12], ax[9], ay[9], bx[9], by[9], cx[9], cy[9], dx[9], dy[9], chainin[64]
  • output ports: result[64], chainout[64]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 64 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 64 bits (modulo 2^64), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: on clk, the block registers its operands (ax, ay, bx, by, cx, cy, dx, dy) at one clock edge and result at the next, with the arithmetic between the two registers: operands applied before clock edge k appear in result after edge k+1, 2 cycles later. The block has no clock enable and no path around either register. chainin is registered at the block's entry like an operand and reaches result 2 cycles after it is applied. chainout is combinational from the input registers: it carries the value result loads at the next clock edge, one cycle before result shows it.
  • reset: reset is synchronous and active high: at a clock edge that samples it high it clears every register of the block (the operand registers, the chainin register and the result register) to 0, and the block loads again at the next edge that samples it low.
  • power-up: every register of the block is unknown until the first clear by reset; no register of the block has an initial value, and a rewrite may not rely on one.
  • tie-off: chainin = 0 when the block is not chained (a dedicated chain input: only another block's chainout or a constant may drive it); mode_sigs = 0 always (the architecture gives the port no meaning for this mode).
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above; a product-term port the rewrite does not use is tied to 0. chainout reaches only the next block's chainin, through a dedicated connection to the block directly below it in the column; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it.

BLOCKS: 126
TILES: 171
STAGE_NS: 5.9
MAPPING:
A. fltr_compute_{f1,f2,f3,h1,h2,h3,h4} (unchanged from the kept candidate), one block per instance, with s1 = din[55:48]+din[7:0], s2 = din[47:40]+din[15:8], s3 = din[39:32]+din[23:16] (9-bit): ax=s1, ay=c1; bx=s2, by=c2; cx=s3, cy=c3; dx={1'b0,din[31:24]}, dy=c4; clk=clk, reset=1'b0, mode_sigs=12'd0, chainin=64'd0, chainout unconnected. (c1,c2,c3,c4): f1=(29,101,17,277), f2=(4,42,163,255), f3=(20,179,364,0 with dx=9'd0), h1=(17,25,193,0 with dx=9'd0), h2=(4,42,163,255), h3=(23,72,147,0 with dx=9'd0), h4=(14,43,80,324).
B. my_fir_{f1,f2,f3,h1,h2,h3,h4}, two blocks per instance (one per byte of the 16-bit taps). With sh = new_data_rdy + new_data_rdy_nxt and the advanced taps p2..p6 (p2 = sh==0 ? n_delay_reg2 : sh==1 ? n_delay_reg1 : din; p3 = sh==0 ? n_delay_reg3 : sh==1 ? n_delay_reg2 : n_delay_reg1; p4 = sh==0 ? n_delay_reg4 : sh==1 ? n_delay_reg3 : n_delay_reg2; p5 = sh==0 ? n_delay_reg5 : sh==1 ? n_delay_reg4 : n_delay_reg3; p6 = sh==0 ? n_delay_reg6 : sh==1 ? n_delay_reg5 : n_delay_reg4):
high block: ax = p2[15:8]+p4[15:8] (9 bits), ay = c2; bx = {1'b0,p3[15:8]}, by = c3; cx = {1'b0,p5[15:8]}, cy = c5; dx = {1'b0,p6[15:8]}, dy = c6
low block: ax = p2[7:0]+p4[7:0] (9 bits), ay = c2; bx = {1'b0,p3[7:0]}, by = c3; cx = {1'b0,p5[7:0]}, cy = c5; dx = {1'b0,p6[7:0]}, dy = c6
both: clk=clk, reset=1'b0, mode_sigs=12'd0, chainin=64'd0, chainout unconnected; results named sop_hi, sop_lo.
(c2,c3,c5,c6) per module: f1=(15,235,101,29); f2=(163,255,42,4); f3=(148,—,77,12); h1=(193,—,25,15); h2=(163,255,42,4); h3=(109,—,56,9); h4=(109,—,56,9). Where c3 is "—" (f3,h1,h3,h4 have no n_delay_reg3 term) tie bx=9'd0, by=9'd0 and drop p3.
dout <= ((q1_reg + sop_lo[19:0]) + {sop_hi[19:0], 8'd0}) + (din * c0), with q1_reg a new 24-bit register loaded in the same enabled always block as q1_reg <= din * c1.
C. new 1-bit port new_data_rdy_nxt on every my_fir module, driven by a new 1-bit input vidin_new_data_nxt on h_fltr, driven at the top (lines 188-197) by the unregistered strobe: h_fltr_1_left←v_nd_s1_left_2to0, h_fltr_2_left←v_nd_s2_left_2to0, h_fltr_4_left←v_nd_s4_left_2to0, h_fltr_1_right←v_nd_s1_right_2to0, h_fltr_2_right←v_nd_s2_right_2to0, h_fltr_4_right←v_nd_s4_right_2to0.
PLAN:

What is converted, and what is left

  1. All 46 fltr_compute candidates (f1,f2,f3,h1,h2,h3,h4) are converted exactly as in the kept candidate: keep that edit verbatim (the seven folded sums, the three 9-bit pre-adds, the ext*_d1/ext*_d2 sign-extension corrections for f1, f3 and h4, reset tied to 1'b0). It already measured -39% on the product and is not touched by this revision.
  2. 31 of the 45 my_fir candidates are converted: in every my_fir module the products of n_delay_reg2, n_delay_reg3 (where present), n_delay_reg4, n_delay_reg5 and n_delay_reg6 move onto blocks. Because the taps are symmetric (c4=c2, c5=c1, c6=c0, cited at lines 1440-1449, 1500-1506, 1561-1567, 1616-1625, 1675-1681, 1734-1740, 1792-1798), those five products fold into four: c2*(n2+n4) + c3*n3 + c5*n5 + c6*n6. The taps are 16 bits and the block's ports are 9, so each tap is split into bytes and the four products are formed once over the high bytes and once over the low bytes: sum = 256*HI + LO, exactly. Operands stay inside 9 bits: a byte pair sums to at most 510, a single byte to 255, and every coefficient is at most 255. The whole sum is at most 673*65535 = 44.1e6 < 2^28, so neither the original nor the rewrite truncates and the unsigned block arithmetic matches the unsigned source arithmetic bit for bit.
  3. 14 my_fir candidates are left, all for one reason: they are the two newest samples of the window (din * c0 at lines 1486, 1542, 1602, 1661, 1716, 1775, 1833 and n_delay_reg1 * c1 at lines 1487, 1543, 1603, 1662, 1717, 1776, 1834). A readable block result costs 2 cycles (chainout is 1 cycle but reaches only another block's chainin, so soft logic cannot read it), while dout loads one cycle after din is presented. din's value is produced by the upstream fltr_compute dout register and does not exist two cycles early inside h_fltr, so c0*din must stay a soft/DSP multiply feeding the last adder of the dout stage. The c1 term does not need the block either: since n_delay_reg1 is the enabled register of din, the enabled register q1_reg <= din*c1 holds exactly c1*n_delay_reg1 at every cycle, so that product moves one cycle earlier into its own short stage and leaves the dout stage as a register input.

Why the operands are the advanced taps, and why this is exact

The block answers two cycles after its operands are applied, so at cycle c it must be given the tap values that will stand at cycle c+2. The delay line advances by sh = e(c) + e(c+1) steps over those two cycles, with e the enable new_data_rdy. e(c) is the module's own input; e(c+1) is available at cycle c because v_nd_s1_left and its five siblings are plain unconditional registers of the top-level inputs v_nd_s*_*_2to0 (lines 430-438, 188-197), so the unregistered strobe is the next cycle's enable. Hence new_data_rdy_nxt. Expanding the delay line twice gives n_k(c+2) = n_{k-sh}(c) for k >= 2 (with n_0 = din), in all four (e(c),e(c+1)) cases; k=1 would need n_{-1}, which is why tap 1 is left out of the block. Those are the p2..p6 of the MAPPING. Every p is a value already held in a register of the module, so the rewrite is defined exactly when the original is: for a given load edge the block sees the identical sample values, only read earlier out of earlier registers, so the X behaviour at start-up is unchanged as well. reset is tied to 0 on every block: the design never clears these pipelines, and the testbench pulses reset mid-run, so clearing the block there would diverge. No block register is relied on for an initial value; each is reloaded every cycle and washes out within two cycles, inside the hundreds of cycles the 226/316/496-deep fifos take to flush.

Blocks and tiles

126 blocks: 42 for the fltr_compute reductions (one per instance, 7 modules x 6 v_fltr instances) and 84 for the my_fir reductions (two per instance, 7 modules x 6 h_fltr instances). Each takes its DSP tile alone. The remaining multiplies in the design are the two per my_fir instance (din*c0 and din*c1), 84 of them, which pack about two to a two_mult_18x19 tile, ~45 tiles. Total ~171 tiles, against 224 in the baseline and 187 measured for the kept candidate; the device has 306.

Stages and delay

No stage holds two blocks in series: every block is fed from design registers and read from its own result register, so the longest series of blocks in any stage is one, 2.219 ns inside the block, well under the slowest stage. No chainout is used.

The slowest stage of the kept candidate, 11.4491 ns, is the my_fir stage: one 18x19 multiply, six adder levels with their carry chains, one LUT, into the enabled flip-flop. That stage is what this rewrite empties. What leaves it: all six adder levels and five of the seven multiplies. What is left in it: the single multiply din*c0 and three adders, written so the multiply feeds only the final adder — 0.060 (din clock-to-Q) + ~1.0 wire + 2.140 multiply + 0.544 wire + one ~28-bit carry chain + 0.019 setup, about 4.7 ns; the q1_reg/sop_lo path through the three adders is about 4.9 ns. The new stages the rewrite creates are both shorter: tap register to block input is 0.060 + 0.960 + one mux LUT + one 8-bit carry chain + 1.419 + 0.019, about 3.7 ns, and din to q1_reg is 0.060 + ~1.0 + 2.140 + 0.019, about 3.2 ns. The fltr_compute stages are unchanged from the kept candidate and are shorter still.

With the my_fir stage down to ~4.9 ns, the slowest stage left in the design is in steer_fltr (lines 640-643): three levels of 31-bit add/subtract from im_p_tmp_1..4 into im_p_tmp, roughly 0.060 + 0.960 + three carry-chain levels with their wires + 0.019, about 5.9 ns. That stage is untouched by the rewrite and sets STAGE_NS. It is an estimate off the sampled wire and adder figures, not a measured path; the period should land near it, between about 5.5 and 7 ns, against 11.4491.

Register stages, before and after

  • fltr_compute (all 46 regions): before, din -> q1..q7 (1 stage) -> d_out_tmp (2nd) -> dout (3rd). After, din -> block input register (1st) -> block result register (2nd) -> dout (3rd). Three stages before and after, same values at the same edges; the sign-extension correction is delayed two cycles by ext*_d1/ext*_d2 to land with the block result.
  • my_fir (all 31 converted regions): before, the taps are registers and the products and their six-level sum are combinational into the enabled dout, one register stage from tap to dout. After, the same tap values are presented to the block two cycles before that edge, pass the block's input register and result register, and are added into the same dout register at the same edge with the same value — the sample-to-dout latency is unchanged, no register is added on the din-to-dout path, and the new q1_reg holds c1*n_delay_reg1, the value the original computed combinationally at that edge.

Edit notes for the editor

Keep the kept candidate's fltr_compute edit exactly as it stands. In each my_fir module: add the new_data_rdy_nxt input at the end of the port list, add reg[23:0] q1_reg;, the sh/p2..p6 wires, the two 9-bit pre-adds, the two int_sop_4 instances, keep n_delay_reg1..6 and output_data_ready as they are, add q1_reg <= din * c1; inside the if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1) branch, and replace the seven-term dout <= ... with the parenthesised form of the MAPPING (the parenthesisation matters: it keeps the multiply one adder level from the register). In h_fltr add the input vidin_new_data_nxt at the end of its port list and pass it as the last argument of all seven my_fir instantiations (lines 514-520). At the top, add the matching last argument to the six h_fltr instantiations (lines 188-190, 195-197). The top's own port list does not change.

DESIGN_CHANGE: if fltr_compute exposed its pre-register sum (d_out_tmp[18:3], the value dout takes next cycle) as an output, routed through v_fltr into h_fltr, then my_fir's din would be known one cycle early; the c0 product could then be registered like the c1 one, which would empty the my_fir dout stage of its last multiply (about 1.2 ns off that stage) and would also let the c0 and c1 terms fold back into the blocks' fourth products, removing both remaining soft multiplies per filter, about 45 more DSP tiles.

Port additions in h_fltr (stereovision2.v:455, 515-521) and the six top-level instantiations (stereovision2.v:188-190, 195-197) are plan item C; no other region differs, and the instance count is 21 = 7 + 7×2.

Byte split is exact (256·hi + lo), all products ≤ 2^18, all partial sums < 2^20, total ≤ 44.1e6 < 2^28, so no truncation anywhere the original had none.
  • Visibility/terms/reset/scope. Only q1..q7/d_out_tmp (module-internal, no other reader) moved inside; all seven taps are still summed; no reset path exists for these pipelines in the original, so tying block reset to 0 preserves behaviour across the mid-run reset; added registers are only relied on after they load, and no ASSUMES is needed since the next-cycle enable is structural.

1	// int_sop_4: result = ax*ay + bx*by + cx*cy + dx*dy + chainin, unsigned, each 9x9 product
2	// zero-extended into a 64-bit sum, modulo 2^64 (the sum wraps at the result width).
3	// Ports: clk, reset, mode_sigs[12], ax, ay, bx, by, cx, cy, dx, dy [9 each], chainin[64] in;
4	// result[64], chainout[64] out. mode_sigs is not read.
5	// Registers (the arch's annotation read literally, decision 2026-10-16): every input is registered
6	// at the block's entry at one clock edge (the eight operands and chainin alike); the
7	// products and their sum are formed from those registers and loaded into result at the next edge.
8	// Cycles: every operand and chainin to result 2. chainout is combinational from the input
9	// registers: the sum result loads at the next edge unless that edge clears it (1 cycle from the
10	// inputs).
11	// Reset: synchronous, active high (2026-10-17: the arch's annotation does not distinguish a reset
12	// register from a clear sampled by the registers themselves): at a clock edge that samples it high
13	// every register of the block (operand registers, chainin register, result) is cleared to 0; the block
14	// loads again at the next edge that samples it low. No register has an initial value: every one is
15	// X until the first clear.
16	module int_sop_4 (
17	    input clk,
18	    input reset,
19	    input [11:0] mode_sigs,
20	    input [8:0] ax, input [8:0] ay,
21	    input [8:0] bx, input [8:0] by,
22	    input [8:0] cx, input [8:0] cy,
23	    input [8:0] dx, input [8:0] dy,
24	    input [63:0] chainin,
25	    output reg [63:0] result,
26	    output [63:0] chainout
27	);
28	
29	    // stage 1: the input registers
30	    reg [8:0]  ax_reg, ay_reg, bx_reg, by_reg, cx_reg, cy_reg, dx_reg, dy_reg;
31	    reg [63:0] chainin_reg;
32	
33	    // combinational middle: the four products and their sum, from the registers
34	    wire [17:0] prod_a = ax_reg * ay_reg;                        // 9x9 -> 18, exact
35	    wire [17:0] prod_b = bx_reg * by_reg;
