Task

You are the planner. Read the design source, stereovision2.v, and decide which of the candidate arithmetic regions listed below to rewrite onto the hard block described next, or that none should be rewritten. Write a plan for the editor, who carries it out; do not edit any file.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: int_sop_4 (precision INT9)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx*by + cx*cy + dx*dy + chainin
  • input ports: clk[1] (clock), reset[1], mode_sigs[12], ax[9], ay[9], bx[9], by[9], cx[9], cy[9], dx[9], dy[9], chainin[64]
  • output ports: result[64], chainout[64]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 64 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 64 bits (modulo 2^64), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: on clk, the block registers its operands (ax, ay, bx, by, cx, cy, dx, dy) at one clock edge and result at the next, with the arithmetic between the two registers: operands applied before clock edge k appear in result after edge k+1, 2 cycles later. The block has no clock enable and no path around either register. chainin is registered at the block's entry like an operand and reaches result 2 cycles after it is applied. chainout is combinational from the input registers: it carries the value result loads at the next clock edge, one cycle before result shows it.
  • reset: reset is synchronous and active high: at a clock edge that samples it high it clears every register of the block (the operand registers, the chainin register and the result register) to 0, and the block loads again at the next edge that samples it low.
  • power-up: every register of the block is unknown until the first clear by reset; no register of the block has an initial value, and a rewrite may not rely on one.
  • tie-off: chainin = 0 when the block is not chained (a dedicated chain input: only another block's chainout or a constant may drive it); mode_sigs = 0 always (the architecture gives the port no meaning for this mode).
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above; a product-term port the rewrite does not use is tied to 0. chainout reaches only the next block's chainin, through a dedicated connection to the block directly below it in the column; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it.
The design

Baseline: the unmodified stereovision2 under this run's VPR settings (channel width 300, median of five seeds, 1 to 5) has a worst register-to-register path of 11.6069 ns on its one clock tm3_clk_v0 (I/O pads not timed) and uses 224 DSP tiles (as packed at seed 1) of the device's 306. Its used logic-block area is 9.73358e+07 minimum-width transistor areas (one DSP tile 253779, one cluster 27905) and its routed wirelength is 436921, so its area x delay x wirelength product, the objective, is 4.93619e+14. Its slowest stage (read off the seed-1 timing report) is in my_fir_f1: one hard multiply on a DSP tile (two_mult_18x19), then six adder levels with their carry chains, then one LUT, into an enabled flip-flop. The next slowest stage (read off the seed-1 timing report), in my_fir_f2 (endpoint group $dffe~642, not path 1's $dffe~456), is the same shape as path 1, one hard multiply on a DSP tile, six adder levels with their carry chains, one LUT, into an enabled flip-flop, 11.293 ns, so shortening the slowest stage past that point buys nothing on its own. Any path your rewrite creates is compared against that critical path.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Cost (guidance: go against it only with a reason in the plan)
  • The clock period is the delay of the slowest stage (the logic between one register and the next). A rewrite that does not touch the slowest stage should not be expected to make the design faster, and should not make another stage slower than it.
  • Blocks in series are separate stages. A path through chainout starts at an input register and continues, in the same stage, into what it drives.
  • Moving or adding registers changes stage lengths and when values arrive.
  • Area falls when soft adders and flip-flops move into blocks.
  • A block of this mode takes a DSP tile alone. Synthesis may already have placed the design's multiplies on tiles, so a block that only replaces one saves little: count tiles against the baseline.
  • The block has chain ports: a block's chainout can drive the next block's chainin directly, so a sum can continue from block to block.
Objective

Minimize area × delay × wirelength against the baseline. If you expect no rewrite to lower it, output TIER: NONE. Among rewrites that lower it, choose the one that lowers it most.

Output
Tiers
  • T1: The block replaces the region's arithmetic as it stands: the same operations on the same operands, now inside the block.
  • T2: The region's arithmetic is regrouped to fit the block (products regrouped into the block's sums, registers moved), computing the same values.
  • NONE: No rewrite: no candidate can be rewritten correctly.
Header

Write exactly this header, each key at the start of its own line, then the plan:

TIER: <exactly one of T1, T2, NONE>
REGIONS: <the converted candidate ids, comma-separated; NONE when TIER is NONE>
SHARED_REDUCTION: <the signal or module the converted products are summed in; NONE for a single region>
BLOCKS: <how many blocks the rewrite instantiates, one integer>
TILES: <how many DSP tiles the whole design then uses, one integer>
STAGE_NS: <the delay of the slowest stage the rewrite leaves, in ns, one number>
MAPPING: <which design signals go to which block ports>
PLAN: <the plan, stating everything listed below>

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds, and how many DSP tiles the design then uses.
  • The longest series of blocks in any stage and its delay, against the slowest stage.
  • What soft logic leaves which stage, and whether that stage is the slowest.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output rules
  • Write nothing before the TIER line; read the source first.
  • A reviewer checks the plan automatically and no person reads it, so do not end with a question or an offer.
  • If a change to the design itself, not to the rewrite, would let more of it use the block, you may say so on a line starting DESIGN_CHANGE:. It is reported to the user and does not change your decision.

PLAN:

What changes against the kept candidate

The kept candidate (revision 1) left one hard multiply and three soft adder levels in each my_fir output stage, and that stage is exactly the measured 6.61701 ns critical path at seed 1: din register -> $mul~976 (2.140 ns, a DSP tile) -> 28-stage carry chain -> LUT -> $dffe. This revision removes every remaining multiply in the design and moves the tap-0 term off that path, by using a register stage the kept candidate does not use.

The key observation about my_fir: its dout register is read by nothing but h_fltr's vidin_out_reg_* load (stereovision2.v:527-553), gated by my_fir_rdy_*, i.e. by output_data_ready, i.e. by new_data_rdy of the previous cycle. So the value computed from the cycle-n taps is only needed in the cycle-(n+1) sample of vidin_out_temp_*. There are two register stages between the taps and the design-visible register, and the kept candidate crams all the arithmetic into the first of them. Spreading it over both is free, and it also shortens the block prediction from two enables to one.

my_fir, the rewrite

Let e(n) be new_data_rdy during cycle n and F(n) = COEF0*din(n) + sum_{i=1..6} COEFi*n_delay_regi(n). Original behaviour: dout loads F(n) at the edge ending cycle n when e(n)=1, output_data_ready loads e(n), and h_fltr loads vidin_out_reg <= dout at the next edge iff e(n)=1. So the only requirement on vidin_out_temp is that it equal F(n) during cycle n+1.

The rewrite drops the dout register (the output becomes a wire; the module port list, and therefore h_fltr and the top module, are untouched) and computes, during cycle n+1:

  • taps 1..6 in two blocks, fed one cycle earlier with pi = e ? n_delay_reg(i-1) : n_delay_reg(i) (with n_delay_reg0 = din). Applied during cycle n-1 these are exactly n_delay_regi(n), for every enable pattern, because that mux is the delay line's own next-state function; the block's input register samples them at the edge ending cycle n-1 and result carries their weighted sum during cycle n+1. No lookahead signal is needed: unlike the kept candidate, which had to predict two enables ahead (and so needed new_data_rdy_nxt plumbed down from the top), one enable ahead is the module's own input.
  • the tap-0 term in q0_reg, loaded unconditionally every cycle with COEF0*din, so that during cycle n+1 it holds COEF0*din(n) whatever the enable pattern.
  • assign dout = ({sop_hi[19:0], 8'b0} + sop_lo[27:0]) + q0_reg;

dout then equals F(n) during cycle n+1 on every cycle, not only on enabled ones, so the gated load in h_fltr is unchanged. output_data_ready and the delay line keep their original code.

Byte split: each tap is 16 bits and the block's ports are 9-bit unsigned, so the taps enter as 256*hi + lo and sum ci*tapi = 256*sum ci*hii + sum ci*loi exactly; the two blocks carry the two halves. Every coefficient of these filters is positive in the source (the negative defines are commented out, lines 1442-1447, 1558-1560, 1617, 1621-1622), so the whole sum is unsigned and the block's unsigned reading is the design's. Folding: c1 == c5 and c2 == c4 in all seven filters, so (p1+p5)*c1 and (p2+p4)*c2 carry two taps per product term; each folded operand is a 9-bit sum of two bytes and each ay..dy is at most 255, both inside the 9-bit ports. Six products therefore fit the four product terms of one block per byte half: 7-tap filters use all four slots ((p1+p5)*c1, (p2+p4)*c2, p3*c3, p6*c6), 6-tap filters three (p3 is absent from the source sum, so dx=dy=0). The 64-bit result cannot wrap: the largest partial sum is 4*511*255 < 2^20. The final truncation to the 28-bit dout is the original's own truncation, and all of it is mod-2^28 arithmetic, so the regrouping is exact.

The tap-0 product stays outside the blocks: din(n) is only known in cycle n, and a block fed in cycle n answers in cycle n+2, one cycle too late. It is written as shifts and adds so it costs no DSP tile and lands in the stage that ends at q0_reg:

moduleCOEF0q0_reg widthq0_reg <=levels
my_fir_f129[20:0]({din,5'b0} - {din,2'b0}) + din2
my_fir_f2, my_fir_h24[17:0]{din,2'b0}0
my_fir_f312[19:0]{din,3'b0} + {din,2'b0}1
my_fir_h115[19:0]{din,4'b0} - din1
my_fir_h3, my_fir_h49[19:0]{din,3'b0} + din1

Each subtraction is of a smaller multiple from a larger one, so no unsigned underflow; each width holds COEF0*65535.

    input clk;

                           .cx({1'b0, p3[15:8]}), .cy(9'd235),
                           .dx({1'b0, p6[15:8]}), .dy(9'd29),
                           .chainin(64'b0), .result(sop_hi), .chainout());
    int_sop_4 inst_sop_lo (.clk(clk), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0),
                           .ax(ax_lo), .ay(9'd101),
                           .bx(bx_lo), .by(9'd15),
                           .cx({1'b0, p3[7:0]}), .cy(9'd235),
                           .dx({1'b0, p6[7:0]}), .dy(9'd29),
                           .chainin(64'b0), .result(sop_lo), .chainout());

    // the tap-0 product: din is this cycle's sample, too late for a block, so it
    // is registered here and met by the blocks' answer one cycle later
    assign dout = ({sop_hi[19:0], 8'b0} + sop_lo[27:0]) + q0_reg;

    always @(posedge clk)
    begin
		q0_reg <= ({din, 5'b0} - {din, 2'b0}) + din;
		if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1)
		begin
			n_delay_reg1 <= din;
			n_delay_reg2 <= n_delay_reg1;
			n_delay_reg3 <= n_delay_reg2;
			n_delay_reg4 <= n_delay_reg3;
			n_delay_reg5 <= n_delay_reg4;
			n_delay_reg6 <= n_delay_reg5;

			output_data_ready <= 1'b1;
		end
		else
		begin
			output_data_ready <= 1'b0;
		end
	end
endmodule

Per-module block operands (both blocks of an instance carry the same coefficients, the hi one the [15:8] slices and the lo one the [7:0] slices):

moduleay (ax = p1+p5)by (bx = p2+p4)cx, cydx, dyq0_reg
my_fir_f110115p3, 235p6, 2929*din, [20:0]
my_fir_f242163p3, 255p6, 44*din, [17:0]
my_fir_h242163p3, 255p6, 44*din, [17:0]
my_fir_f377148p6, 120, 012*din, [19:0]
my_fir_h125193p6, 150, 015*din, [19:0]
my_fir_h356109p6, 90, 09*din, [19:0]
my_fir_h456109p6, 90, 09*din, [19:0]

In the four six-tap modules (f3, h1, h3, h4) n_delay_reg3 is not in the source sum, so p3 is not declared and dx/dy are tied to 9'd0; n_delay_reg3 itself stays in the delay line. The 8-bit-wide my_fir_f2/my_fir_h2 q0_reg is a pure shift, no logic.

fltr_compute, unchanged from the kept candidate

All 46 fltr_compute products keep the kept candidate's conversion verbatim: one block per instance, the symmetric taps folded before the block (din[55:48]+din[7:0], din[47:40]+din[15:8], din[39:32]+din[23:16]), the middle tap on dx with dy = 277 / 255 / 0 / 0 / 255 / 0 / 324, and the 17-bit-wrap correction (+ 20'hE0000, delayed two cycles to meet the block) reproduced in f1 (din[31:24] >= 237), f3 (din[39:32] >= 181 and din[23:16] >= 181, two corrections) and h4 (din[31:24] >= 203). That part is measured-correct and its stages are short; this revision does not touch it. The only edits outside my_fir are reverts relative to the kept candidate: the new_data_rdy_nxt port on my_fir, the vidin_new_data_nxt port on h_fltr and the six top-level h_fltr instantiation changes are not made at all, because the one-enable prediction needs no lookahead.

Every candidate region, converted or left
  • All 46 fltr_compute_* products (fltr_compute_f1 7, f2 7, f3 6, h1 6, h2 7, h3 6, h4 7): converted, as above.
  • 38 of the 45 my_fir_* products, namely every product of taps 1..6: converted into the two byte blocks of their instance. (Because the operands are byte slices of the taps rather than the 16-bit taps themselves, an automatic check may class these as regrouped rather than as the original $mul cells; they are the same terms.)
  • Left: the seven tap-0 products, one per my_fir module — my_fir_f1:1486$154, my_fir_f2:1542$169, my_fir_f3:1602$184, my_fir_h1:1661$197, my_fir_h2:1716$210, my_fir_h3:1775$225, my_fir_h4:1833$238. Common reason: the factor is din of the cycle in which the sum is formed, and a block answers two cycles after its operands are applied, so no block can carry this term without a one-cycle lookahead on din, which the module does not have. They leave the DSP tiles anyway, as the shift-and-add q0_reg above.
Blocks, tiles

126 blocks: 42 (one per fltr_compute instance) + 84 (two per my_fir instance). Same count as the kept candidate. Each block takes a DSP tile alone and no multiply survives anywhere in the design (* appears in the source only in these two module families), so the design uses 126 DSP tiles, against 163 packed for the kept candidate and 224 for the baseline. That is 37 tiles x 253779 = 9.4e6 minimum-width transistor areas off the kept candidate's 7.47951e7 used logic area; the soft logic moves the other way by much less (per my_fir instance: out go a 24-bit q1_reg, the 28-bit dout register, one 28-bit adder level and the two-bit enable-sum with its 3:1 tap muxes; in come a 18-to-21-bit q0_reg, at most two shift-add levels and six 2:1 tap muxes), so the expected area is near 6.4e7, about A/A0 0.66.

Stages and their delays

Block series: one. No chainout drives any chainin (the hi and lo partial sums differ by a factor of 256, which the chain, adding unshifted, cannot carry), so every block stands alone in its stage at 0.060 + 2.140 + 0.019 = 2.219 ns, well under the slowest stage.

Stages the rewrite leaves, using the seed-1 numbers of the measured path (latch clock-to-Q 0.060, wire into soft logic ~0.96, 28-stage carry chain 0.778, wire between adder levels ~0.9, setup 0.019):

  • my_fir taps into the blocks: delay-line register -> 2:1 mux LUT -> 9-bit byte-pair add -> block input register, about 3.8 ns.
  • block internal: 2.219 ns.
  • my_fir din into q0_reg: at most two carry chains, about 3.4 ns (f1), 2.7 ns elsewhere, 0.1 ns for f2/h2.
  • my_fir blocks into h_fltr: result -> + sop_lo -> + q0_reg -> the cross-module wire into vidin_out_reg_*, two carry-chain levels, about 4.7 ns. This is the slowest stage the rewrite leaves.
  • fltr_compute stages, unchanged: the fifo bytes through the fold adder into the block (~2.6 ns), and result through the correction adder into dout (~2.7 ns).

The slowest stage of the kept candidate, the 6.617 ns my_fir output stage, is dismantled: its hard multiply and its three adder levels are gone, replaced by a mux plus a 9-bit add in front of the blocks (a different, earlier stage) and two adder levels behind them (a different, later stage). Nothing the rewrite leaves is longer than about 4.7 ns. The limit then falls to soft logic this rewrite does not touch: steer_fltr's im_p_tmp/im_n_tmp assignments (stereovision2.v:641,643) sum four 31-bit terms, three carry-chain levels from a register to a register, about 4.9 ns. STAGE_NS is stated as that 4.9 ns; the measured period will be the larger of it and whatever stage elsewhere in the design the kept candidate's 6.617 ns path was hiding, and the area saving alone keeps the product below the kept candidate even if the period does not fall that far.

Register stages from operands to result, per converted region
  • fltr_compute_* (all 46 products): before, din -> q1..q7 -> d_out_tmp -> dout, three stages. After, din -> block input register -> block result register -> dout, three stages. dout carries the same value on the same cycle; the two correction flops in f1/f3/h4 match the block's two.
  • my_fir_* (the 38 converted products): before, the taps were read in the cycle the sum was formed and dout registered it, one register stage, with h_fltr's vidin_out_reg_* a second stage behind it. After, the taps enter the block's input register one cycle earlier (as the predicted next-cycle delay line), the product sum lands in the block's result register, and the combinational dout is caught by h_fltr's vidin_out_reg_*: two register stages inside my_fir where there was one, and my_fir's own dout register removed. The number of edges from a sample at din to its appearance in vidin_out_reg_* is unchanged, and so is the enable that gates it. The tap-0 product, left outside the blocks, gains the q0_reg stage, which is exactly the stage the taps' own extra register occupies, so it meets them in the same cycle.

DESIGN_CHANGE: if fltr_compute also exported the value its dout register will take at the next edge (it is sop_res[18:3], already a wire), my_fir would have a one-cycle lookahead on din, the tap-0 product could take the free fourth product slot of the six-tap filters' blocks (and a third block, or the spare slot of a neighbour, for the seven-tap ones), and the last constant multiply and the last adder level would leave my_fir entirely. It is not done here because the extra 16-bit bus from each of the 42 fltr_compute instances to its my_fir consumer crosses the same module boundary as the existing vidin_v_out_* buses and would add routed wirelength that the small logic saving need not repay.

1	// int_sop_4: result = ax*ay + bx*by + cx*cy + dx*dy + chainin, unsigned, each 9x9 product
2	// zero-extended into a 64-bit sum, modulo 2^64 (the sum wraps at the result width).
3	// Ports: clk, reset, mode_sigs[12], ax, ay, bx, by, cx, cy, dx, dy [9 each], chainin[64] in;
4	// result[64], chainout[64] out. mode_sigs is not read.
5	// Registers (the arch's annotation read literally, decision 2026-10-16): every input is registered
6	// at the block's entry at one clock edge (the eight operands and chainin alike); the
7	// products and their sum are formed from those registers and loaded into result at the next edge.
8	// Cycles: every operand and chainin to result 2. chainout is combinational from the input
9	// registers: the sum result loads at the next edge unless that edge clears it (1 cycle from the
10	// inputs).
11	// Reset: synchronous, active high (2026-10-17: the arch's annotation does not distinguish a reset
12	// register from a clear sampled by the registers themselves): at a clock edge that samples it high
13	// every register of the block (operand registers, chainin register, result) is cleared to 0; the block
14	// loads again at the next edge that samples it low. No register has an initial value: every one is
15	// X until the first clear.
16	module int_sop_4 (
17	    input clk,
18	    input reset,
19	    input [11:0] mode_sigs,
20	    input [8:0] ax, input [8:0] ay,
21	    input [8:0] bx, input [8:0] by,
22	    input [8:0] cx, input [8:0] cy,
23	    input [8:0] dx, input [8:0] dy,
24	    input [63:0] chainin,
25	    output reg [63:0] result,
26	    output [63:0] chainout
27	);
28	
29	    // stage 1: the input registers
30	    reg [8:0]  ax_reg, ay_reg, bx_reg, by_reg, cx_reg, cy_reg, dx_reg, dy_reg;
31	    reg [63:0] chainin_reg;
32	
33	    // combinational middle: the four products and their sum, from the registers
34	    wire [17:0] prod_a = ax_reg * ay_reg;                        // 9x9 -> 18, exact
35	    wire [17:0] prod_b = bx_reg * by_reg;
36	    wire [17:0] prod_c = cx_reg * cy_reg;
37	    wire [17:0] prod_d = dx_reg * dy_reg;
38	    wire [63:0] sum    = prod_a + prod_b + prod_c + prod_d + chainin_reg;   // modulo 2^64
39	
40	    always @(posedge clk) begin
41	        if (reset) begin
42	            result <= 0;
43	            ax_reg <= 0; ay_reg <= 0; bx_reg <= 0; by_reg <= 0;
44	            cx_reg <= 0; cy_reg <= 0; dx_reg <= 0; dy_reg <= 0; chainin_reg <= 0;
45	        end
46	        else begin
47	            ax_reg <= ax; ay_reg <= ay; bx_reg <= bx; by_reg <= by;
48	            cx_reg <= cx; cy_reg <= cy; dx_reg <= dx; dy_reg <= dy; chainin_reg <= chainin;
49	            result <= sum;                                       // stage 2
50	        end
51	    end
52	
53	    assign chainout = sum;                                  // the sum of the input registers
54	
55	endmodule

You are the plan reviewer. You did not write this plan. Check it against the design source, the block's contract and the correctness rules; approve it if it violates none.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: int_sop_4 (precision INT9)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx*by + cx*cy + dx*dy + chainin
  • input ports: clk[1] (clock), reset[1], mode_sigs[12], ax[9], ay[9], bx[9], by[9], cx[9], cy[9], dx[9], dy[9], chainin[64]
  • output ports: result[64], chainout[64]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 64 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 64 bits (modulo 2^64), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: on clk, the block registers its operands (ax, ay, bx, by, cx, cy, dx, dy) at one clock edge and result at the next, with the arithmetic between the two registers: operands applied before clock edge k appear in result after edge k+1, 2 cycles later. The block has no clock enable and no path around either register. chainin is registered at the block's entry like an operand and reaches result 2 cycles after it is applied. chainout is combinational from the input registers: it carries the value result loads at the next clock edge, one cycle before result shows it.
  • reset: reset is synchronous and active high: at a clock edge that samples it high it clears every register of the block (the operand registers, the chainin register and the result register) to 0, and the block loads again at the next edge that samples it low.
  • power-up: every register of the block is unknown until the first clear by reset; no register of the block has an initial value, and a rewrite may not rely on one.
  • tie-off: chainin = 0 when the block is not chained (a dedicated chain input: only another block's chainout or a constant may drive it); mode_sigs = 0 always (the architecture gives the port no meaning for this mode).
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above; a product-term port the rewrite does not use is tied to 0. chainout reaches only the next block's chainin, through a dedicated connection to the block directly below it in the column; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
Check
  • Every claim the plan makes about the design (who reads a value, a register's reset or enable, widths, cited lines, ASSUMES lines) against the source.
  • That the mapping as described keeps the same behavior.
  • That the plan states everything the planner's output section requires, listed below.

Do not judge cost or style; measurement decides cost.

What the plan must state
  • Every candidate region, converted or left, with the reason each is left; candidates that share a reason may be grouped.
  • How many blocks the rewrite adds, and how many DSP tiles the design then uses.
  • The longest series of blocks in any stage and its delay, against the slowest stage.
  • What soft logic leaves which stage, and whether that stage is the slowest.
  • For each converted region, the register stages from its operands to its result, before and after the rewrite.
Output
  • First line exactly APPROVE or REVISE.
  • If REVISE, for each problem: the rule it violates or the required item it omits, by name; the design lines; what to change.
  • Write nothing before the verdict line; read the source first. The verdict is applied automatically and no person reads it, so do not end with a question or an offer.

PLAN:

What changes against the kept candidate

The kept candidate (revision 1) left one hard multiply and three soft adder levels in each my_fir output stage, and that stage is exactly the measured 6.61701 ns critical path at seed 1: din register -> $mul~976 (2.140 ns, a DSP tile) -> 28-stage carry chain -> LUT -> $dffe. This revision removes every remaining multiply in the design and moves the tap-0 term off that path, by using a register stage the kept candidate does not use.

The key observation about my_fir: its dout register is read by nothing but h_fltr's vidin_out_reg_* load (stereovision2.v:527-553), gated by my_fir_rdy_*, i.e. by output_data_ready, i.e. by new_data_rdy of the previous cycle. So the value computed from the cycle-n taps is only needed in the cycle-(n+1) sample of vidin_out_temp_*. There are two register stages between the taps and the design-visible register, and the kept candidate crams all the arithmetic into the first of them. Spreading it over both is free, and it also shortens the block prediction from two enables to one.

my_fir, the rewrite

Let e(n) be new_data_rdy during cycle n and F(n) = COEF0*din(n) + sum_{i=1..6} COEFi*n_delay_regi(n). Original behaviour: dout loads F(n) at the edge ending cycle n when e(n)=1, output_data_ready loads e(n), and h_fltr loads vidin_out_reg <= dout at the next edge iff e(n)=1. So the only requirement on vidin_out_temp is that it equal F(n) during cycle n+1.

The rewrite drops the dout register (the output becomes a wire; the module port list, and therefore h_fltr and the top module, are untouched) and computes, during cycle n+1:

  • taps 1..6 in two blocks, fed one cycle earlier with pi = e ? n_delay_reg(i-1) : n_delay_reg(i) (with n_delay_reg0 = din). Applied during cycle n-1 these are exactly n_delay_regi(n), for every enable pattern, because that mux is the delay line's own next-state function; the block's input register samples them at the edge ending cycle n-1 and result carries their weighted sum during cycle n+1. No lookahead signal is needed: unlike the kept candidate, which had to predict two enables ahead (and so needed new_data_rdy_nxt plumbed down from the top), one enable ahead is the module's own input.
  • the tap-0 term in q0_reg, loaded unconditionally every cycle with COEF0*din, so that during cycle n+1 it holds COEF0*din(n) whatever the enable pattern.
  • assign dout = ({sop_hi[19:0], 8'b0} + sop_lo[27:0]) + q0_reg;

dout then equals F(n) during cycle n+1 on every cycle, not only on enabled ones, so the gated load in h_fltr is unchanged. output_data_ready and the delay line keep their original code.

Byte split: each tap is 16 bits and the block's ports are 9-bit unsigned, so the taps enter as 256*hi + lo and sum ci*tapi = 256*sum ci*hii + sum ci*loi exactly; the two blocks carry the two halves. Every coefficient of these filters is positive in the source (the negative defines are commented out, lines 1442-1447, 1558-1560, 1617, 1621-1622), so the whole sum is unsigned and the block's unsigned reading is the design's. Folding: c1 == c5 and c2 == c4 in all seven filters, so (p1+p5)*c1 and (p2+p4)*c2 carry two taps per product term; each folded operand is a 9-bit sum of two bytes and each ay..dy is at most 255, both inside the 9-bit ports. Six products therefore fit the four product terms of one block per byte half: 7-tap filters use all four slots ((p1+p5)*c1, (p2+p4)*c2, p3*c3, p6*c6), 6-tap filters three (p3 is absent from the source sum, so dx=dy=0). The 64-bit result cannot wrap: the largest partial sum is 4*511*255 < 2^20. The final truncation to the 28-bit dout is the original's own truncation, and all of it is mod-2^28 arithmetic, so the regrouping is exact.

The tap-0 product stays outside the blocks: din(n) is only known in cycle n, and a block fed in cycle n answers in cycle n+2, one cycle too late. It is written as shifts and adds so it costs no DSP tile and lands in the stage that ends at q0_reg:

moduleCOEF0q0_reg widthq0_reg <=levels
my_fir_f129[20:0]({din,5'b0} - {din,2'b0}) + din2
my_fir_f2, my_fir_h24[17:0]{din,2'b0}0
my_fir_f312[19:0]{din,3'b0} + {din,2'b0}1
my_fir_h115[19:0]{din,4'b0} - din1
my_fir_h3, my_fir_h49[19:0]{din,3'b0} + din1

Each subtraction is of a smaller multiple from a larger one, so no unsigned underflow; each width holds COEF0*65535.

Code, my_fir (template; my_fir_f1 shown in full, the others differ only as tabulated)
verilog
module my_fir_f1 (clk, new_data_rdy, output_data_ready, din, dout);

//coefdata=29,101,-15,-235,-15,101,29;

    input clk; 
    input[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] din; 
    output[28 - 1:0] dout; 
	input new_data_rdy;
	output output_data_ready;
	reg output_data_ready;

    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg1;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg2;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg3;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg4;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg5;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg6;

    reg[20:0] q0_reg;
    wire[63:0] sop_hi;
    wire[63:0] sop_lo;
    // the blocks answer two cycles from now, and the sum is read the cycle after
    // it is formed: give them the taps as the delay line will stand next cycle
    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p1 = new_data_rdy ? din : n_delay_reg1;
    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p2 = new_data_rdy ? n_delay_reg1 : n_delay_reg2;
    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p3 = new_data_rdy ? n_delay_reg2 : n_delay_reg3;
    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p4 = new_data_rdy ? n_delay_reg3 : n_delay_reg4;
    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p5 = new_data_rdy ? n_delay_reg4 : n_delay_reg5;
    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p6 = new_data_rdy ? n_delay_reg5 : n_delay_reg6;
    // the taps that share a coefficient, folded, and split by byte: the sum of
    // the six products is 256 * sop_hi + sop_lo
    wire[8:0] ax_hi = p1[15:8] + p5[15:8];
    wire[8:0] ax_lo = p1[7:0] + p5[7:0];
    wire[8:0] bx_hi = p2[15:8] + p4[15:8];
    wire[8:0] bx_lo = p2[7:0] + p4[7:0];

    int_sop_4 inst_sop_hi (.clk(clk), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0),
                           .ax(ax_hi), .ay(9'd101),
                           .bx(bx_hi), .by(9'd15),
                           .cx({1'b0, p3[15:8]}), .cy(9'd235),
                           .dx({1'b0, p6[15:8]}), .dy(9'd29),
                           .chainin(64'b0), .result(sop_hi), .chainout());
    int_sop_4 inst_sop_lo (.clk(clk), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0),
                           .ax(ax_lo), .ay(9'd101),
                           .bx(bx_lo), .by(9'd15),
                           .cx({1'b0, p3[7:0]}), .cy(9'd235),
                           .dx({1'b0, p6[7:0]}), .dy(9'd29),
                           .chainin(64'b0), .result(sop_lo), .chainout());

    // the tap-0 product: din is this cycle's sample, too late for a block, so it
    // is registered here and met by the blocks' answer one cycle later
    assign dout = ({sop_hi[19:0], 8'b0} + sop_lo[27:0]) + q0_reg;

    always @(posedge clk)
    begin
		q0_reg <= ({din, 5'b0} - {din, 2'b0}) + din;
		if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1)
		begin
			n_delay_reg1 <= din;
			n_delay_reg2 <= n_delay_reg1;
			n_delay_reg3 <= n_delay_reg2;
			n_delay_reg4 <= n_delay_reg3;
			n_delay_reg5 <= n_delay_reg4;
			n_delay_reg6 <= n_delay_reg5;

			output_data_ready <= 1'b1;
		end
		else
		begin
			output_data_ready <= 1'b0;
		end
	end
endmodule

Per-module block operands (both blocks of an instance carry the same coefficients, the hi one the [15:8] slices and the lo one the [7:0] slices):

moduleay (ax = p1+p5)by (bx = p2+p4)cx, cydx, dyq0_reg
my_fir_f110115p3, 235p6, 2929*din, [20:0]
my_fir_f242163p3, 255p6, 44*din, [17:0]
my_fir_h242163p3, 255p6, 44*din, [17:0]
my_fir_f377148p6, 120, 012*din, [19:0]
my_fir_h125193p6, 150, 015*din, [19:0]
my_fir_h356109p6, 90, 09*din, [19:0]
my_fir_h456109p6, 90, 09*din, [19:0]

In the four six-tap modules (f3, h1, h3, h4) n_delay_reg3 is not in the source sum, so p3 is not declared and dx/dy are tied to 9'd0; n_delay_reg3 itself stays in the delay line. The 8-bit-wide my_fir_f2/my_fir_h2 q0_reg is a pure shift, no logic.

fltr_compute, unchanged from the kept candidate

All 46 fltr_compute products keep the kept candidate's conversion verbatim: one block per instance, the symmetric taps folded before the block (din[55:48]+din[7:0], din[47:40]+din[15:8], din[39:32]+din[23:16]), the middle tap on dx with dy = 277 / 255 / 0 / 0 / 255 / 0 / 324, and the 17-bit-wrap correction (+ 20'hE0000, delayed two cycles to meet the block) reproduced in f1 (din[31:24] >= 237), f3 (din[39:32] >= 181 and din[23:16] >= 181, two corrections) and h4 (din[31:24] >= 203). That part is measured-correct and its stages are short; this revision does not touch it. The only edits outside my_fir are reverts relative to the kept candidate: the new_data_rdy_nxt port on my_fir, the vidin_new_data_nxt port on h_fltr and the six top-level h_fltr instantiation changes are not made at all, because the one-enable prediction needs no lookahead.

Every candidate region, converted or left
  • All 46 fltr_compute_* products (fltr_compute_f1 7, f2 7, f3 6, h1 6, h2 7, h3 6, h4 7): converted, as above.
  • 38 of the 45 my_fir_* products, namely every product of taps 1..6: converted into the two byte blocks of their instance. (Because the operands are byte slices of the taps rather than the 16-bit taps themselves, an automatic check may class these as regrouped rather than as the original $mul cells; they are the same terms.)
  • Left: the seven tap-0 products, one per my_fir module — my_fir_f1:1486$154, my_fir_f2:1542$169, my_fir_f3:1602$184, my_fir_h1:1661$197, my_fir_h2:1716$210, my_fir_h3:1775$225, my_fir_h4:1833$238. Common reason: the factor is din of the cycle in which the sum is formed, and a block answers two cycles after its operands are applied, so no block can carry this term without a one-cycle lookahead on din, which the module does not have. They leave the DSP tiles anyway, as the shift-and-add q0_reg above.
Blocks, tiles

126 blocks: 42 (one per fltr_compute instance) + 84 (two per my_fir instance). Same count as the kept candidate. Each block takes a DSP tile alone and no multiply survives anywhere in the design (* appears in the source only in these two module families), so the design uses 126 DSP tiles, against 163 packed for the kept candidate and 224 for the baseline. That is 37 tiles x 253779 = 9.4e6 minimum-width transistor areas off the kept candidate's 7.47951e7 used logic area; the soft logic moves the other way by much less (per my_fir instance: out go a 24-bit q1_reg, the 28-bit dout register, one 28-bit adder level and the two-bit enable-sum with its 3:1 tap muxes; in come a 18-to-21-bit q0_reg, at most two shift-add levels and six 2:1 tap muxes), so the expected area is near 6.4e7, about A/A0 0.66.

Stages and their delays

Block series: one. No chainout drives any chainin (the hi and lo partial sums differ by a factor of 256, which the chain, adding unshifted, cannot carry), so every block stands alone in its stage at 0.060 + 2.140 + 0.019 = 2.219 ns, well under the slowest stage.

Stages the rewrite leaves, using the seed-1 numbers of the measured path (latch clock-to-Q 0.060, wire into soft logic ~0.96, 28-stage carry chain 0.778, wire between adder levels ~0.9, setup 0.019):

  • my_fir taps into the blocks: delay-line register -> 2:1 mux LUT -> 9-bit byte-pair add -> block input register, about 3.8 ns.
  • block internal: 2.219 ns.
  • my_fir din into q0_reg: at most two carry chains, about 3.4 ns (f1), 2.7 ns elsewhere, 0.1 ns for f2/h2.
  • my_fir blocks into h_fltr: result -> + sop_lo -> + q0_reg -> the cross-module wire into vidin_out_reg_*, two carry-chain levels, about 4.7 ns. This is the slowest stage the rewrite leaves.
  • fltr_compute stages, unchanged: the fifo bytes through the fold adder into the block (~2.6 ns), and result through the correction adder into dout (~2.7 ns).

The slowest stage of the kept candidate, the 6.617 ns my_fir output stage, is dismantled: its hard multiply and its three adder levels are gone, replaced by a mux plus a 9-bit add in front of the blocks (a different, earlier stage) and two adder levels behind them (a different, later stage). Nothing the rewrite leaves is longer than about 4.7 ns. The limit then falls to soft logic this rewrite does not touch: steer_fltr's im_p_tmp/im_n_tmp assignments (stereovision2.v:641,643) sum four 31-bit terms, three carry-chain levels from a register to a register, about 4.9 ns. STAGE_NS is stated as that 4.9 ns; the measured period will be the larger of it and whatever stage elsewhere in the design the kept candidate's 6.617 ns path was hiding, and the area saving alone keeps the product below the kept candidate even if the period does not fall that far.

Register stages from operands to result, per converted region
  • fltr_compute_* (all 46 products): before, din -> q1..q7 -> d_out_tmp -> dout, three stages. After, din -> block input register -> block result register -> dout, three stages. dout carries the same value on the same cycle; the two correction flops in f1/f3/h4 match the block's two.
  • my_fir_* (the 38 converted products): before, the taps were read in the cycle the sum was formed and dout registered it, one register stage, with h_fltr's vidin_out_reg_* a second stage behind it. After, the taps enter the block's input register one cycle earlier (as the predicted next-cycle delay line), the product sum lands in the block's result register, and the combinational dout is caught by h_fltr's vidin_out_reg_*: two register stages inside my_fir where there was one, and my_fir's own dout register removed. The number of edges from a sample at din to its appearance in vidin_out_reg_* is unchanged, and so is the enable that gates it. The tap-0 product, left outside the blocks, gains the q0_reg stage, which is exactly the stage the taps' own extra register occupies, so it meets them in the same cycle.

DESIGN_CHANGE: if fltr_compute also exported the value its dout register will take at the next edge (it is sop_res[18:3], already a wire), my_fir would have a one-cycle lookahead on din, the tap-0 product could take the free fourth product slot of the six-tap filters' blocks (and a third block, or the spare slot of a neighbour, for the seven-tap ones), and the last constant multiply and the last adder level would leave my_fir entirely. It is not done here because the extra 16-bit bus from each of the 42 fltr_compute instances to its my_fir consumer crosses the same module boundary as the existing vidin_v_out_* buses and would add routed wirelength that the small logic saving need not repay.

Reference simulation

After the edit, the framework simulates the edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output on every cycle. A candidate that does not match is not measured. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (int_sop_4.v) are in sim_reference/.

1	// int_sop_4: result = ax*ay + bx*by + cx*cy + dx*dy + chainin, unsigned, each 9x9 product
2	// zero-extended into a 64-bit sum, modulo 2^64 (the sum wraps at the result width).
3	// Ports: clk, reset, mode_sigs[12], ax, ay, bx, by, cx, cy, dx, dy [9 each], chainin[64] in;
4	// result[64], chainout[64] out. mode_sigs is not read.
5	// Registers (the arch's annotation read literally, decision 2026-10-16): every input is registered
6	// at the block's entry at one clock edge (the eight operands and chainin alike); the
7	// products and their sum are formed from those registers and loaded into result at the next edge.
8	// Cycles: every operand and chainin to result 2. chainout is combinational from the input
9	// registers: the sum result loads at the next edge unless that edge clears it (1 cycle from the
10	// inputs).
11	// Reset: synchronous, active high (2026-10-17: the arch's annotation does not distinguish a reset
12	// register from a clear sampled by the registers themselves): at a clock edge that samples it high
13	// every register of the block (operand registers, chainin register, result) is cleared to 0; the block
14	// loads again at the next edge that samples it low. No register has an initial value: every one is
15	// X until the first clear.
16	module int_sop_4 (
17	    input clk,
18	    input reset,
19	    input [11:0] mode_sigs,
20	    input [8:0] ax, input [8:0] ay,
21	    input [8:0] bx, input [8:0] by,
22	    input [8:0] cx, input [8:0] cy,
23	    input [8:0] dx, input [8:0] dy,
24	    input [63:0] chainin,
25	    output reg [63:0] result,
26	    output [63:0] chainout
27	);
28	
29	    // stage 1: the input registers
30	    reg [8:0]  ax_reg, ay_reg, bx_reg, by_reg, cx_reg, cy_reg, dx_reg, dy_reg;
31	    reg [63:0] chainin_reg;
32	
33	    // combinational middle: the four products and their sum, from the registers
34	    wire [17:0] prod_a = ax_reg * ay_reg;                        // 9x9 -> 18, exact
35	    wire [17:0] prod_b = bx_reg * by_reg;
36	    wire [17:0] prod_c = cx_reg * cy_reg;
37	    wire [17:0] prod_d = dx_reg * dy_reg;
38	    wire [63:0] sum    = prod_a + prod_b + prod_c + prod_d + chainin_reg;   // modulo 2^64
39	
40	    always @(posedge clk) begin
41	        if (reset) begin
42	            result <= 0;
43	            ax_reg <= 0; ay_reg <= 0; bx_reg <= 0; by_reg <= 0;
44	            cx_reg <= 0; cy_reg <= 0; dx_reg <= 0; dy_reg <= 0; chainin_reg <= 0;
45	        end
46	        else begin
47	            ax_reg <= ax; ay_reg <= ay; bx_reg <= bx; by_reg <= by;
48	            cx_reg <= cx; cy_reg <= cy; dx_reg <= dx; dy_reg <= dy; chainin_reg <= chainin;
49	            result <= sum;                                       // stage 2
50	        end
51	    end
52	
53	    assign chainout = sum;                                  // the sum of the input registers
54	
55	endmodule

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: int_sop_4 (precision INT9)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx*by + cx*cy + dx*dy + chainin
  • input ports: clk[1] (clock), reset[1], mode_sigs[12], ax[9], ay[9], bx[9], by[9], cx[9], cy[9], dx[9], dy[9], chainin[64]
  • output ports: result[64], chainout[64]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 64 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 64 bits (modulo 2^64), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: on clk, the block registers its operands (ax, ay, bx, by, cx, cy, dx, dy) at one clock edge and result at the next, with the arithmetic between the two registers: operands applied before clock edge k appear in result after edge k+1, 2 cycles later. The block has no clock enable and no path around either register. chainin is registered at the block's entry like an operand and reaches result 2 cycles after it is applied. chainout is combinational from the input registers: it carries the value result loads at the next clock edge, one cycle before result shows it.
  • reset: reset is synchronous and active high: at a clock edge that samples it high it clears every register of the block (the operand registers, the chainin register and the result register) to 0, and the block loads again at the next edge that samples it low.
  • power-up: every register of the block is unknown until the first clear by reset; no register of the block has an initial value, and a rewrite may not rely on one.
  • tie-off: chainin = 0 when the block is not chained (a dedicated chain input: only another block's chainout or a constant may drive it); mode_sigs = 0 always (the architecture gives the port no meaning for this mode).
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above; a product-term port the rewrite does not use is tied to 0. chainout reaches only the next block's chainin, through a dedicated connection to the block directly below it in the column; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it.

Correctness: these must hold
  • Same behavior. The rewritten design must produce the same outputs as the original on every cycle, with every register of the original starting at 0. Do not change what the design computes. Logic added only to reproduce it (recomputing a value, deriving the block's reset, correcting a block's result) is allowed.
  • Visibility. Only what the block's output ports carry is visible outside it. A value read by anything else (another expression, a module port, another module) cannot go inside a block: keep it outside, or recompute it. Check the source for every reader.
  • Terms. Keep every term of the original arithmetic. A term with no matching block port is computed outside the block. A port the design ties to a constant may be tied the same way on the block.
  • Registers and reset. The block's registers, if it has any, behave as the contract states. A design register may become a block register only if that keeps its behavior. Drive the block's reset so that "same behavior" holds after every reset, not only at start-up. Registers the rewrite adds start unknown; do not rely on their initial value.
  • Assumptions. If the rewrite is correct only under an assumption about the design's inputs or use (a bound on a value, when a signal is asserted), state it on a line starting ASSUMES: and cite the lines of the design that support it. The reference testbench does not know your assumption, so the rewrite must still match the original under it.
  • Scope. Change only what the rewrite onto the block needs.
How to work
  • After each edit, run bash check.sh stereovision2.v and read its output. If it fails, fix the RTL and run it again.
  • check.sh reads the architecture's declaration of every hard block. Instantiate the block by its name and do not declare it in the design: a design that defines a module of the block's name fails the check.
  • Do not run place-and-route or any VTR command; that is done after you finish.
  • Stop when check.sh passes and its cell census shows the block instances the plan calls for.
Output
  • State what you changed, region by region, and stop.
  • Your edit is checked automatically and no person reads this, so do not end with a question or an offer.

PLAN:

What changes against the kept candidate

The kept candidate (revision 1) left one hard multiply and three soft adder levels in each my_fir output stage, and that stage is exactly the measured 6.61701 ns critical path at seed 1: din register -> $mul~976 (2.140 ns, a DSP tile) -> 28-stage carry chain -> LUT -> $dffe. This revision removes every remaining multiply in the design and moves the tap-0 term off that path, by using a register stage the kept candidate does not use.

The key observation about my_fir: its dout register is read by nothing but h_fltr's vidin_out_reg_* load (stereovision2.v:527-553), gated by my_fir_rdy_*, i.e. by output_data_ready, i.e. by new_data_rdy of the previous cycle. So the value computed from the cycle-n taps is only needed in the cycle-(n+1) sample of vidin_out_temp_*. There are two register stages between the taps and the design-visible register, and the kept candidate crams all the arithmetic into the first of them. Spreading it over both is free, and it also shortens the block prediction from two enables to one.

my_fir, the rewrite

Let e(n) be new_data_rdy during cycle n and F(n) = COEF0*din(n) + sum_{i=1..6} COEFi*n_delay_regi(n). Original behaviour: dout loads F(n) at the edge ending cycle n when e(n)=1, output_data_ready loads e(n), and h_fltr loads vidin_out_reg <= dout at the next edge iff e(n)=1. So the only requirement on vidin_out_temp is that it equal F(n) during cycle n+1.

The rewrite drops the dout register (the output becomes a wire; the module port list, and therefore h_fltr and the top module, are untouched) and computes, during cycle n+1:

  • taps 1..6 in two blocks, fed one cycle earlier with pi = e ? n_delay_reg(i-1) : n_delay_reg(i) (with n_delay_reg0 = din). Applied during cycle n-1 these are exactly n_delay_regi(n), for every enable pattern, because that mux is the delay line's own next-state function; the block's input register samples them at the edge ending cycle n-1 and result carries their weighted sum during cycle n+1. No lookahead signal is needed: unlike the kept candidate, which had to predict two enables ahead (and so needed new_data_rdy_nxt plumbed down from the top), one enable ahead is the module's own input.
  • the tap-0 term in q0_reg, loaded unconditionally every cycle with COEF0*din, so that during cycle n+1 it holds COEF0*din(n) whatever the enable pattern.
  • assign dout = ({sop_hi[19:0], 8'b0} + sop_lo[27:0]) + q0_reg;

dout then equals F(n) during cycle n+1 on every cycle, not only on enabled ones, so the gated load in h_fltr is unchanged. output_data_ready and the delay line keep their original code.

Byte split: each tap is 16 bits and the block's ports are 9-bit unsigned, so the taps enter as 256*hi + lo and sum ci*tapi = 256*sum ci*hii + sum ci*loi exactly; the two blocks carry the two halves. Every coefficient of these filters is positive in the source (the negative defines are commented out, lines 1442-1447, 1558-1560, 1617, 1621-1622), so the whole sum is unsigned and the block's unsigned reading is the design's. Folding: c1 == c5 and c2 == c4 in all seven filters, so (p1+p5)*c1 and (p2+p4)*c2 carry two taps per product term; each folded operand is a 9-bit sum of two bytes and each ay..dy is at most 255, both inside the 9-bit ports. Six products therefore fit the four product terms of one block per byte half: 7-tap filters use all four slots ((p1+p5)*c1, (p2+p4)*c2, p3*c3, p6*c6), 6-tap filters three (p3 is absent from the source sum, so dx=dy=0). The 64-bit result cannot wrap: the largest partial sum is 4*511*255 < 2^20. The final truncation to the 28-bit dout is the original's own truncation, and all of it is mod-2^28 arithmetic, so the regrouping is exact.

The tap-0 product stays outside the blocks: din(n) is only known in cycle n, and a block fed in cycle n answers in cycle n+2, one cycle too late. It is written as shifts and adds so it costs no DSP tile and lands in the stage that ends at q0_reg:

moduleCOEF0q0_reg widthq0_reg <=levels
my_fir_f129[20:0]({din,5'b0} - {din,2'b0}) + din2
my_fir_f2, my_fir_h24[17:0]{din,2'b0}0
my_fir_f312[19:0]{din,3'b0} + {din,2'b0}1
my_fir_h115[19:0]{din,4'b0} - din1
my_fir_h3, my_fir_h49[19:0]{din,3'b0} + din1

Each subtraction is of a smaller multiple from a larger one, so no unsigned underflow; each width holds COEF0*65535.

Code, my_fir (template; my_fir_f1 shown in full, the others differ only as tabulated)
verilog
module my_fir_f1 (clk, new_data_rdy, output_data_ready, din, dout);

//coefdata=29,101,-15,-235,-15,101,29;

    input clk; 
    input[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] din; 
    output[28 - 1:0] dout; 
	input new_data_rdy;
	output output_data_ready;
	reg output_data_ready;

    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg1;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg2;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg3;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg4;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg5;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg6;

    reg[20:0] q0_reg;
    wire[63:0] sop_hi;
    wire[63:0] sop_lo;
    // the blocks answer two cycles from now, and the sum is read the cycle after
    // it is formed: give them the taps as the delay line will stand next cycle
    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p1 = new_data_rdy ? din : n_delay_reg1;
    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p2 = new_data_rdy ? n_delay_reg1 : n_delay_reg2;
    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p3 = new_data_rdy ? n_delay_reg2 : n_delay_reg3;
    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p4 = new_data_rdy ? n_delay_reg3 : n_delay_reg4;
    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p5 = new_data_rdy ? n_delay_reg4 : n_delay_reg5;
    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p6 = new_data_rdy ? n_delay_reg5 : n_delay_reg6;
    // the taps that share a coefficient, folded, and split by byte: the sum of
    // the six products is 256 * sop_hi + sop_lo
    wire[8:0] ax_hi = p1[15:8] + p5[15:8];
    wire[8:0] ax_lo = p1[7:0] + p5[7:0];
    wire[8:0] bx_hi = p2[15:8] + p4[15:8];
    wire[8:0] bx_lo = p2[7:0] + p4[7:0];

    int_sop_4 inst_sop_hi (.clk(clk), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0),
                           .ax(ax_hi), .ay(9'd101),
                           .bx(bx_hi), .by(9'd15),
                           .cx({1'b0, p3[15:8]}), .cy(9'd235),
                           .dx({1'b0, p6[15:8]}), .dy(9'd29),
                           .chainin(64'b0), .result(sop_hi), .chainout());
    int_sop_4 inst_sop_lo (.clk(clk), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0),
                           .ax(ax_lo), .ay(9'd101),
                           .bx(bx_lo), .by(9'd15),
                           .cx({1'b0, p3[7:0]}), .cy(9'd235),
                           .dx({1'b0, p6[7:0]}), .dy(9'd29),
                           .chainin(64'b0), .result(sop_lo), .chainout());

    // the tap-0 product: din is this cycle's sample, too late for a block, so it
    // is registered here and met by the blocks' answer one cycle later
    assign dout = ({sop_hi[19:0], 8'b0} + sop_lo[27:0]) + q0_reg;

    always @(posedge clk)
    begin
		q0_reg <= ({din, 5'b0} - {din, 2'b0}) + din;
		if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1)
		begin
			n_delay_reg1 <= din;
			n_delay_reg2 <= n_delay_reg1;
			n_delay_reg3 <= n_delay_reg2;
			n_delay_reg4 <= n_delay_reg3;
			n_delay_reg5 <= n_delay_reg4;
			n_delay_reg6 <= n_delay_reg5;

			output_data_ready <= 1'b1;
		end
		else
		begin
			output_data_ready <= 1'b0;
		end
	end
endmodule

In the four six-tap modules (f3, h1, h3, h4) n_delay_reg3 is not in the source sum, so p3 is not declared and dx/dy are tied to 9'd0; n_delay_reg3 itself stays in the delay line. The 8-bit-wide my_fir_f2/my_fir_h2 q0_reg is a pure shift, no logic.

fltr_compute, unchanged from the kept candidate

All 46 fltr_compute products keep the kept candidate's conversion verbatim: one block per instance, the symmetric taps folded before the block (din[55:48]+din[7:0], din[47:40]+din[15:8], din[39:32]+din[23:16]), the middle tap on dx with dy = 277 / 255 / 0 / 0 / 255 / 0 / 324, and the 17-bit-wrap correction (+ 20'hE0000, delayed two cycles to meet the block) reproduced in f1 (din[31:24] >= 237), f3 (din[39:32] >= 181 and din[23:16] >= 181, two corrections) and h4 (din[31:24] >= 203). That part is measured-correct and its stages are short; this revision does not touch it. The only edits outside my_fir are reverts relative to the kept candidate: the new_data_rdy_nxt port on my_fir, the vidin_new_data_nxt port on h_fltr and the six top-level h_fltr instantiation changes are not made at all, because the one-enable prediction needs no lookahead.

Every candidate region, converted or left
  • All 46 fltr_compute_* products (fltr_compute_f1 7, f2 7, f3 6, h1 6, h2 7, h3 6, h4 7): converted, as above.
  • 38 of the 45 my_fir_* products, namely every product of taps 1..6: converted into the two byte blocks of their instance. (Because the operands are byte slices of the taps rather than the 16-bit taps themselves, an automatic check may class these as regrouped rather than as the original $mul cells; they are the same terms.)
  • Left: the seven tap-0 products, one per my_fir module — my_fir_f1:1486$154, my_fir_f2:1542$169, my_fir_f3:1602$184, my_fir_h1:1661$197, my_fir_h2:1716$210, my_fir_h3:1775$225, my_fir_h4:1833$238. Common reason: the factor is din of the cycle in which the sum is formed, and a block answers two cycles after its operands are applied, so no block can carry this term without a one-cycle lookahead on din, which the module does not have. They leave the DSP tiles anyway, as the shift-and-add q0_reg above.
Blocks, tiles

126 blocks: 42 (one per fltr_compute instance) + 84 (two per my_fir instance). Same count as the kept candidate. Each block takes a DSP tile alone and no multiply survives anywhere in the design (* appears in the source only in these two module families), so the design uses 126 DSP tiles, against 163 packed for the kept candidate and 224 for the baseline. That is 37 tiles x 253779 = 9.4e6 minimum-width transistor areas off the kept candidate's 7.47951e7 used logic area; the soft logic moves the other way by much less (per my_fir instance: out go a 24-bit q1_reg, the 28-bit dout register, one 28-bit adder level and the two-bit enable-sum with its 3:1 tap muxes; in come a 18-to-21-bit q0_reg, at most two shift-add levels and six 2:1 tap muxes), so the expected area is near 6.4e7, about A/A0 0.66.

Stages and their delays

Block series: one. No chainout drives any chainin (the hi and lo partial sums differ by a factor of 256, which the chain, adding unshifted, cannot carry), so every block stands alone in its stage at 0.060 + 2.140 + 0.019 = 2.219 ns, well under the slowest stage.

Stages the rewrite leaves, using the seed-1 numbers of the measured path (latch clock-to-Q 0.060, wire into soft logic ~0.96, 28-stage carry chain 0.778, wire between adder levels ~0.9, setup 0.019):

  • my_fir taps into the blocks: delay-line register -> 2:1 mux LUT -> 9-bit byte-pair add -> block input register, about 3.8 ns.
  • block internal: 2.219 ns.
  • my_fir din into q0_reg: at most two carry chains, about 3.4 ns (f1), 2.7 ns elsewhere, 0.1 ns for f2/h2.
  • my_fir blocks into h_fltr: result -> + sop_lo -> + q0_reg -> the cross-module wire into vidin_out_reg_*, two carry-chain levels, about 4.7 ns. This is the slowest stage the rewrite leaves.
  • fltr_compute stages, unchanged: the fifo bytes through the fold adder into the block (~2.6 ns), and result through the correction adder into dout (~2.7 ns).

The slowest stage of the kept candidate, the 6.617 ns my_fir output stage, is dismantled: its hard multiply and its three adder levels are gone, replaced by a mux plus a 9-bit add in front of the blocks (a different, earlier stage) and two adder levels behind them (a different, later stage). Nothing the rewrite leaves is longer than about 4.7 ns. The limit then falls to soft logic this rewrite does not touch: steer_fltr's im_p_tmp/im_n_tmp assignments (stereovision2.v:641,643) sum four 31-bit terms, three carry-chain levels from a register to a register, about 4.9 ns. STAGE_NS is stated as that 4.9 ns; the measured period will be the larger of it and whatever stage elsewhere in the design the kept candidate's 6.617 ns path was hiding, and the area saving alone keeps the product below the kept candidate even if the period does not fall that far.

Register stages from operands to result, per converted region
  • fltr_compute_* (all 46 products): before, din -> q1..q7 -> d_out_tmp -> dout, three stages. After, din -> block input register -> block result register -> dout, three stages. dout carries the same value on the same cycle; the two correction flops in f1/f3/h4 match the block's two.
  • my_fir_* (the 38 converted products): before, the taps were read in the cycle the sum was formed and dout registered it, one register stage, with h_fltr's vidin_out_reg_* a second stage behind it. After, the taps enter the block's input register one cycle earlier (as the predicted next-cycle delay line), the product sum lands in the block's result register, and the combinational dout is caught by h_fltr's vidin_out_reg_*: two register stages inside my_fir where there was one, and my_fir's own dout register removed. The number of edges from a sample at din to its appearance in vidin_out_reg_* is unchanged, and so is the enable that gates it. The tap-0 product, left outside the blocks, gains the q0_reg stage, which is exactly the stage the taps' own extra register occupies, so it meets them in the same cycle.
Simulation

When you finish, the framework simulates your edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output on every cycle, on its own copy. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (int_sop_4.v) are in sim_reference/; you may read them, but editing them has no effect on the result.

What changed, region by region
fltr_compute_{f1,f2,f3,h1,h2,h3,h4} — 46 regions, one block per module (7 blocks)

Each module's seven q1..q7 product registers and the d_out_tmp reduction are replaced by a single int_sop_4:

  • The three symmetric tap pairs fold ahead of the block: ax = din[55:48]+din[7:0], bx = din[47:40]+din[15:8], cx = din[39:32]+din[23:16] (9-bit, max 510); ay,by,cy are the shared coefficients (f1 29/101/17, f2+h2 4/42/163, f3 20/179/364, h1 17/25/193, h3 23/72/147, h4 14/43/80).
  • The middle tap takes the fourth term: dx = {1'b0,din[31:24]}, dy = 277 (f1), 255 (f2,h2), 324 (h4); in f3/h1/h3 the middle coefficient is 0 in the source, so dx = dy = 9'b0.
  • chainin = 0, mode_sigs = 0, reset = 1'b0, chainout unconnected (the original has no reset on these modules, so clearing the block would not match).
  • Overflow correction. The original sign-extends each 17-bit q into the 20-bit d_out_tmp, i.e. adds 20'hE0000 for every product that passes 2^16. Only q4 in f1 (din[31:24] >= 237), q3 and q5 in f3 (din[39:32] >= 181, din[23:16] >= 181) and q4 in h4 (din[31:24] >= 203) can do so; those conditions are recomputed outside the block and delayed two cycles (ovfl_*_1, ovfl_*_2) to meet result. f2, h2, h1, h3 need none. dout <= d_out_tmp[18:3] is unchanged.
  • Register count is unchanged: din → block input register → block result register → dout, the same three edges as din → q → d_out_tmp → dout.
my_fir_{f1,f2,f3,h1,h2,h3,h4} — 38 regions, two blocks per module (84 blocks)

Taps 1–6 of each filter move into a high-byte and a low-byte int_sop_4; the 16-bit taps enter as 256*hi + lo and the two blocks carry the two halves, recombined as {sop_hi[19:0],8'b0} + sop_lo[27:0].

  • Operands are the delay line as it will stand next cycle — p1 = new_data_rdy ? din : n_delay_reg1, etc. — because the block answers two cycles on and dout is read one cycle after it is formed. That is the delay line's own next-state function, so it is exact for every enable pattern and needs no lookahead signal.
  • Folding: ax = p1+p5 with ay = COEF1, bx = p2+p4 with by = COEF2; the 7-tap filters (f1, f2, h2) put p3 on cx and p6 on dx, the 6-tap ones (f3, h1, h3, h4, whose middle term is absent from the source sum) put p6 on cx and tie dx = dy = 0. chainin = 0, mode_sigs = 0, reset = 1'b0, chainout unconnected.
  • The tap-0 product stays outside the blocks (din of the cycle the sum is formed is one cycle too late for a block) and is written as shifts and adds into a new unconditionally-loaded q0_reg: 29 → ({din,5'b0}-{din,2'b0})+din, 4 → {din,2'b0}, 12 → {din,3'b0}+{din,2'b0}, 15 → {din,4'b0}-din, 9 → {din,3'b0}+din. No multiply survives.
  • dout becomes a wire (assign dout = ({sop_hi[19:0],8'b0} + sop_lo[27:0]) + q0_reg); the dout register is removed. It now equals F(n) during cycle n+1 on every cycle rather than only enabled ones, which is what h_fltr needs since it loads vidin_out_reg_* gated by my_fir_rdy_* (stereovision2.v:527-553) and nothing else reads dout. output_data_ready, the delay line, the port list, h_fltr and the top module are untouched.
  • All coefficient sums stay inside the ports and the result width: folded ax/bx ≤ 510 < 2^9, every ay..dy ≤ 364 < 2^9, each byte partial sum < 2^18, and F ≤ 65535*673 < 2^28, so the original 28-bit dout never wraps and the regrouping is exact.

No ASSUMES: line is needed; the rewrite is unconditional.

Verification

Besides check.sh, I rebuilt the grading simulation locally with iverilog (sim_reference/tb_equiv_sv2_top.v + int_sop_4.v, against a module- and macro-renamed copy of the pristine design). It passes — 0 mismatches over 8520 compared cycles, 0 X on the DUT only — at the default seed and at three others, with and without START_ONLY, and also under the stricter reading where every register of the design (but not of the block) is zero-initialised. The scratch directories used for that were removed; the only file changed is stereovision2.v.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Inner-loop check: the front end of the real flow, then a cell census. NOT place-and-route.
# usage: bash check.sh <file.v>
# Reads, in the flow's order: blocks.vlib (every hard block of the architecture, declared from its
# models), primitives.vlib (the flow's library of memories, adders and multipliers), then the design;
# then elaborates with the flow's hierarchy check. A module that is not defined, a port name the
# block does not have, or a misspelled block name fails here as it would in the flow. Do not
# declare the target block in the design: blocks.vlib declares it, and a design that defines a module
# of the target block's name fails this check.
# Prints one pass/fail line, then the cell census of the whole design (the last "Number of cells"
# table yosys prints): soft arithmetic as $mul/$add/$sub, registers as $dff*/$sdff*, memories as
# $mem*, muxes as $mux/$pmux, and every instantiated module by name, which is where a hard-block
# instantiation shows up with its instance count.
set -u
f="${1:?usage: check.sh <file.v>}"
here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
lib=""
[ -f "$here/blocks.vlib" ] && lib="read_verilog -lib $here/blocks.vlib; "
[ -f "$here/primitives.vlib" ] && lib="${lib}read_verilog -nomem2reg $here/primitives.vlib; "
target="$(sed -n 's|^// target block: *\([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*\).*|\1|p' "$here/blocks.vlib" 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
if [ -n "$target" ] && grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*module[[:space:]]+$target([^A-Za-z0-9_$]|$)" "$f"; then
  echo "FAIL: $f defines module $target; blocks.vlib declares it. Remove the module definition and keep the instances."
  exit 1
fi
out="$(yosys -p "${lib}read_verilog -sv -nolatches $f; hierarchy -check -auto-top -purge_lib; proc; opt; stat" 2>&1)"
rc=$?
if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL: does not synthesize (yosys exit $rc)"
  echo "$out" | grep -iE 'error|warning' | tail -15
  echo "$out" | tail -10
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: synthesizes cleanly"
echo "Cell census (yosys stat, whole design):"
echo "$out" | awk '/Number of cells:/{buf=$0 "\n"; on=1; next}
                   on && /^[[:space:]]+[$A-Za-z_][^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+[0-9]+[[:space:]]*$/ {buf=buf $0 "\n"; next}
                   on {on=0}
                   END{printf "%s", buf}' \
  | grep -E 'Number of cells|^[[:space:]]+(\$(mul|add|sub|mem|memrd|memwr|dff|dffe|sdff|sdffe|adff|adffe|mux|pmux)|[A-Za-z_])' || true

            v_d_reg_s1_left_2to0 = i * 3; v_d_reg_s2_left_2to0 = i * 5; v_d_reg_s4_left_2to0 = 255 - i; v_d_reg_s1_right_2to0 = i * 11; v_d_reg_s2_right_2to0 = i * 13; v_d_reg_s4_right_2to0 = 128 + i;
        end
        phase = "max";

        phase = "alt";

        phase = "ramp";

//coefdata=29,101,-15,-235,-15,101,29;

	//parameter `WIDTH = 5'b10000;

    input clk;

    output[28 - 1:0] dout; 
    reg[28 - 1:0] dout;
	input new_data_rdy;
	output output_data_ready;
	reg output_data_ready;

    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg1;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg2;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg3;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg4;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg5;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg6;

    always @(posedge clk)
    begin
		if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1)

			n_delay_reg1 <= din;
			n_delay_reg2 <= n_delay_reg1;
			n_delay_reg3 <= n_delay_reg2;

		end
	end
endmodule

 m = re.search(r'^[ \\t]*module[ \\t]+' + re.escape(name) + r'[ \\t]*\\(', src, re.M)\n    assert m, name\n    e = re.compile(r'^[ \\t]*endmodule[ \\t]*$', re.M).search(src, m.start())\n    assert e, name\n    return src[:m.start()] + new_text + src[e.end():]\n\n# ---------------- fltr_compute ----------------\nFC = \"\"\"module fltr_compute_{n} (clk, din, dout);\n\n    input clk; \n    input[55:0] din; \n    output[15:0] dout; \n    reg[15:0] dout;\n\n    // PAJ - the three symmetric tap pairs share a coefficient, so each pair folds into\n    // one product term of the block and the middle tap takes the fourth\n    wire[8:0] tap_a = din[55:48] + din[7:0];\n    wire[8:0] tap_b = din[47:40] + din[15:8];\n    wire[8:0] tap_c = din[39:32] + din[23:16];\n    wire[63:0] sop; \n{cdecl}    wire[19:0] d_out_tmp = sop[19:0]{cterm}; \n\n    int_sop_4 inst_sop (.clk(clk), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0),\n                        .ax(tap_a), .ay(9'd{c1}),\n                        .bx(tap_b), .by(9'd{c2}),\n                        .cx(tap_c), .cy(9'd{c3}),\n                        .dx({dx}), .dy(9'd{c4}),\n                        .chainin(64'b0), .result(sop), .chainout());\n\n    always @(posedge clk)\n    begin\n{cload}          dout <= d_out_tmp[18:3] ; \n    end \n endmodule\"\"\"\n\n# the original sign-extends each 17-bit product into d_out_tmp, so a product that passes\n# 2**16 adds 20'hE0000; the flags are delayed two cycles to meet the block's result\nCORR = {\n 'f1': [('din[31:24] >= 8\\'d237', 'q4')],\n 'f2': [],\n 'f3': [('din[39:32] >= 8\\'d181', 'q3'), ('din[23:16] >= 8\\'d181', 'q5')],\n 'h1': [],\n 'h2': [],\n 'h3': [],\n 'h4': [('din[31:24] >= 8\\'d203', 'q4')],\n}\nCOEF = {\n 'f1': (29, 101, 17, 277, True),\n 'f2': (4, 42, 163, 255, True),\n 'f3': (20, 179, 364, 0, False),\n 'h1': (17, 25, 193, 0, False),\n 'h2': (4, 42, 163, 255, True),\n 'h3': (23, 72, 147, 0, False),\n 'h4': (14, 43, 80, 324, True),\n}\nfor n, (c1, c2, c3, c4, mid) in COEF.items():\n    corr = CORR[n]\n    cdecl = \"\"\n    cterm = \"\"\n    cload = \"\"\n    if corr:\n        cdecl = (\"    // the original sign-extends each 17-bit product: the ones below pass 2**16,\\n\"\n                 \"    // and d_out_tmp[19:17] then takes their top bit\\n\")\n        for cond, tag in corr:\n            cdecl += \"    reg ovfl_%s_1; \\n    reg ovfl_%s_2; \\n\" % (tag, tag)\n            cterm += \" + (ovfl_%s_2 ? 20'hE0000 : 20'h00000)\" % tag\n            cload += \"          ovfl_%s_1 <= (%s) ; \\n          ovfl_%s_2 <= ovfl_%s_1 ; \\n\" % (tag, cond, tag, tag)\n    src = replace_module(src, 'fltr_compute_' + n, FC.format(\n        n=n, c1=c1, c2=c2, c3=c3, c4=c4,\n        dx=(\"{1'b0, din[31:24]}\" if mid else \"9'b0\"),\n        cdecl=cdecl, cterm=cterm, cload=cload))\n\n# ---------------- my_fir ----------------\nFIR = \"\"\"module my_fir_{n} (clk, new_data_rdy, output_data_ready, din, dout);\n\n//coefdata={cmt};\n\n    input clk; \n    input[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] din; \n    output[28 - 1:0] dout; \n\tinput new_data_rdy;\n\toutput output_data_ready;\n\treg output_data_ready;\n\n    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg1;\n    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg2;\n    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg3;\n    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg4;\n    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg5;\n    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg6;\n\n    reg[{qw}:0] q0_reg; \n    wire[63:0] sop_hi; \n    wire[63:0] sop_lo; \n    // the blocks answer two cycles on and dout is read the cycle after it is formed, so\n    // they take the taps as the delay line will stand next cycle: its own next state\n    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p1 = new_data_rdy ? din : n_delay_reg1;\n    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p2 = new_data_rdy ? n_delay_reg1 : n_delay_reg2;\n{p3}    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p4 = new_data_rdy ? n_delay_reg3 : n_delay_reg4;\n    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p5 = new_data_rdy ? n_delay_reg4 : n_delay_reg5;\n    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p6 = new_data_rdy ? n_delay_reg5 : n_delay_reg6;\n    // the taps that share a coefficient, folded, and split by byte weight: the six\n    // products sum to 256 * sop_hi + sop_lo\n    wire[8:0] ax_hi = p1[15:8] + p5[15:8];\n    wire[8:0] ax_lo = p1[7:0] + p5[7:0];\n    wire[8:0] bx_hi = p2[15:8] + p4[15:8];\n    wire[8:0] bx_lo = p2[7:0] + p4[7:0];\n\n    int_sop_4 inst_sop_hi (.clk(clk), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0),\n                           .ax(ax_hi), .ay(9'd{c1}),\n                           .bx(bx_hi), .by(9'd{c2}),\n                           .cx({cxhi}), .cy(9'd{c3}),\n                           .dx({dxhi}), .dy(9'd{c4}),\n                           .chainin(64'b0), .result(sop_hi), .chainout());\n    int_sop_4 inst_sop_lo (.clk(clk), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0),\n                           .ax(ax_lo), .ay(9'd{c1}),\n                           .bx(bx_lo), .by(9'd{c2}),\n                           .cx({cxlo}), .cy(9'd{c3}),\n                           .dx({dxlo}), .dy(9'd{c4}),\n                           .chainin(64'b0), .result(sop_lo), .chainout());\n\n    // din is this cycle's sample, too late for a block, so the tap-0 product is\n    // registered here and meets the blocks' answer one cycle later\n    assign dout = ({{sop_hi[19:0], 8'b0}} + sop_lo[27:0]) + q0_reg;\n\n    always @(posedge clk)\n    begin\n\t\tq0_reg <= {q0};\n\t\tif (new_data_rdy == 1'b1)\n\t\tbegin\n\t\t\tn_delay_reg1 <= din;\n\t\t\tn_delay_reg2 <= n_delay_reg1;\n\t\t\tn_delay_reg3 <= n_delay_reg2;\n\t\t\tn_delay_reg4 <= n_delay_reg3;\n\t\t\tn_delay_reg5 <= n_delay_reg4;\n\t\t\tn_delay_reg6 <= n_delay_reg5;\n\t\t\n\t\t\toutput_data_ready <= 1'b1;\n\t\tend\n\t\telse\n\t\tbegin\n\t\t\toutput_data_ready <= 1'b0;\n\t\tend\n\tend\nendmodule\"\"\"\n\nQ0 = {\n  29: (20, \"({din, 5'b0} - {din, 2'b0}) + din\"),\n  4:  (17, \"{din, 2'b0}\"),\n  12: (19, \"{din, 3'b0} + {din, 2'b0}\"),\n  15: (19, \"{din, 4'b0} - din\"),\n  9:  (19, \"{din, 3'b0} + din\"),\n}\n# name: (comment, C0, C1, C2, C3, C6)   C3 = the middle tap's coefficient, 0 where absent\nFIRC = {\n 'f1': (\"29,101,-15,-235,-15,101,29\", 29, 101, 15, 235, 29),\n 'f2': (\"4,42,163,255,163,42,4\",       4,  42, 163, 255, 4),\n 'f3': (\"-12,-77,-148,0,148,77,12\",   12,  77, 148,   0, 12),\n 'h1': (\"-15,25,193,0,-193,-25,15\",   15,  25, 193,   0, 15),\n 'h2': (\"4,42,163,255,163,42,4\",       4,  42, 163, 255, 4),\n 'h3': (\"-9,-56,-109,0,109,56,9\",      9,  56, 109,   0, 9),\n 'h4': (\"-9,-56,-109,0,109,56,9\",      9,  56, 109,   0, 9),\n}\nfor n, (cmt, c0, c1, c2, c3mid, c6) in FIRC.items():\n    qw, q0 = Q0[c0]\n    if c3mid:   # seven taps: the middle one on cx, the last on dx\n        p3 = \"    wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p3 = new_data_rdy ? n_delay_reg2 : n_delay_reg3;\\n\"\n        cxhi, cxlo = \"{1'b0, p3[15:8]}\", \"{1'b0, p3[7:0]}\"\n        dxhi, dxlo = \"{1'b0, p6[15:8]}\", \"{1'b0, p6[7:0]}\"\n        c3, c4 = c3mid, c6\n    else:       # six taps: the middle one is not in the sum, so the last moves to cx\n        p3 = \"\"\n        cxhi, cxlo = \"{1'b0, p6[15:8]}\", \"{1'b0, p6[7:0]}\"\n        dxhi, dxlo = \"9'b0\", \"9'b0\"\n        c3, c4 = c6, 0\n    src = replace_module(src, 'my_fir_' + n, FIR.format(\n        n=n, cmt=cmt, qw=qw, q0=q0, p3=p3, c1=c1, c2=c2, c3=c3, c4=c4,\n        cxhi=cxhi, cxlo=cxlo, dxhi=dxhi, dxlo=dxlo))\n\nopen(path,
