muxes are duplicates and could be shared: about 1150 more BLEs over the design. Neither is
part of a rewrite onto the block, so this plan leaves both in place.

Simulation

When you finish, the framework simulates your edited design against the original with the reference testbench, comparing every output on every cycle, on its own copy. The testbench (tb_equiv_sv2_top.v) and the block's behavioural model (int_sop_4.v) are in sim_reference/; you may read them, but editing them has no effect on the result.

What I changed, region by region

fltr_compute_f1/f2/f3/h1/h2/h3/h4 — 46 regions, one block per instance (42 blocks)
Dropped q1..q7 and d_out_tmp; the three symmetric tap pairs fold onto one product term each (ax = din[55:48]+din[7:0], bx = din[47:40]+din[15:8], cx = din[39:32]+din[23:16], each a 9-bit sum) and the centre tap takes dx = {1'b0,din[31:24]}. Coefficients on ay/by/cy/dy: f1 29/101/17/277, f2 and h2 4/42/163/255, f3 20/179/364/0 (dx=0), h1 17/25/193/0 (dx=0), h3 23/72/147/0 (dx=0), h4 14/43/80/324. chainin=0, mode_sigs=0, reset=0, chainout unconnected. The block's two registers stand exactly where q* and d_out_tmp stood, so dout <= d_out_tmp[18:3] keeps its cycle.

The original sign-extended each 17-bit q into 20 bits, so a product that reaches bit 16 subtracts 2¹⁷ from the sum. That happens only in f1 (277*din[31:24], threshold 237), f3 (364* on two taps, threshold 181) and h4 (324*din[31:24], threshold 203); in those three I added a comparator pipelined two stages (ovf_q, ovf_d) and subtract {ovf_d,17'b0} from result[19:0]. f2/h2/h1/h3 can never reach bit 16, so they take result[19:0] directly.

my_fir_f1/f2/f3/h1/h2/h3/h4 — 28 regions, two blocks per instance (84 blocks)
dout is now a wire. Each instance gets the next-state taps p1..p6 (new_data_rdy ? ... : ...) feeding a high-byte block and a low-byte block ({1'b0, p[15:8]} / {1'b0, p[7:0]}), so dout = {sop_hi[19:0],8'b0} + sop_lo[19:0] + late. Taps in the blocks: f1 p1/p5/p3/p6 at 101/101/235/29; f2 and h2 p1/p5/p2/p4 at 42/42/163/163; f3 at 77/77/148/148; h1 at 25/25/193/193; h3 and h4 at 56/56/109/109. The taps that do not fit go into one free-running late register per instance — f1 q0_reg = 29*din and mid_reg = 15*(n_delay_reg2+n_delay_reg4); f2/h2 soft_reg = 255*n_delay_reg3 + 4*(din+n_delay_reg6); f3 12*(din+n_delay_reg6); h1 15*(...); h3/h4 9*(...). The delay line, output_data_ready and the new_data_rdy enable are untouched.

No ASSUMES: line is needed: every coefficient is positive and the full 7-tap sum is at most 65535·525 < 2²⁸, so the 28-bit dout never wraps and the byte split is exact; each block's four products are under 2¹⁸.

Verification beyond check.sh

I rebuilt the grading simulation locally in /tmp/equiv (reconstructed pristine reference, renamed modules and macros, sim_reference/tb_equiv_sv2_top.v + int_sop_4.v under iverilog). It passes with 0 mismatches on 8520 compared cycles both with every design register forced to 0 and with the stock all-X power-up (x on dut only: 0 in both), on four seeds and with -DSTART_ONLY.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Inner-loop check: the front end of the real flow, then a cell census. NOT place-and-route.
# usage: bash check.sh <file.v>
# Reads, in the flow's order: blocks.vlib (every hard block of the architecture, declared from its
# models), primitives.vlib (the flow's library of memories, adders and multipliers), then the design;
# then elaborates with the flow's hierarchy check. A module that is not defined, a port name the
# block does not have, or a misspelled block name fails here as it would in the flow. Do not
# declare the target block in the design: blocks.vlib declares it, and a design that defines a module
# of the target block's name fails this check.
# Prints one pass/fail line, then the cell census of the whole design (the last "Number of cells"
# table yosys prints): soft arithmetic as $mul/$add/$sub, registers as $dff*/$sdff*, memories as
# $mem*, muxes as $mux/$pmux, and every instantiated module by name, which is where a hard-block
# instantiation shows up with its instance count.
set -u
f="${1:?usage: check.sh <file.v>}"
here="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
lib=""
[ -f "$here/blocks.vlib" ] && lib="read_verilog -lib $here/blocks.vlib; "
[ -f "$here/primitives.vlib" ] && lib="${lib}read_verilog -nomem2reg $here/primitives.vlib; "
target="$(sed -n 's|^// target block: *\([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*\).*|\1|p' "$here/blocks.vlib" 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
if [ -n "$target" ] && grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*module[[:space:]]+$target([^A-Za-z0-9_$]|$)" "$f"; then
  echo "FAIL: $f defines module $target; blocks.vlib declares it. Remove the module definition and keep the instances."
  exit 1
fi
out="$(yosys -p "${lib}read_verilog -sv -nolatches $f; hierarchy -check -auto-top -purge_lib; proc; opt; stat" 2>&1)"
rc=$?
if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL: does not synthesize (yosys exit $rc)"
  echo "$out" | grep -iE 'error|warning' | tail -15
  echo "$out" | tail -10
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: synthesizes cleanly"
echo "Cell census (yosys stat, whole design):"
echo "$out" | awk '/Number of cells:/{buf=$0 "\n"; on=1; next}
                   on && /^[[:space:]]+[$A-Za-z_][^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+[0-9]+[[:space:]]*$/ {buf=buf $0 "\n"; next}
                   on {on=0}
                   END{printf "%s", buf}' \
  | grep -E 'Number of cells|^[[:space:]]+(\$(mul|add|sub|mem|memrd|memwr|dff|dffe|sdff|sdffe|adff|adffe|mux|pmux)|[A-Za-z_])' || true

module my_fir_f2 (clk, new_data_rdy, output_data_ready, din, dout);

//coefdata=4,42,163,255,163,42,4;


//	parameter WIDTH = 5'b10000;

    input clk; 
    input[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] din; 
    output[28 - 1:0] dout; 
	input new_data_rdy;
	output output_data_ready;
	reg output_data_ready;

    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg1;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg2;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg3;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg4;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg5;
    reg[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0]n_delay_reg6;


	// the delay line as it will stand next cycle: the block takes its operands one edge
	// before the original loaded the sum, so it has to see the next state of the taps
	wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p1 = new_data_rdy ? din : n_delay_reg1;
	wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p2 = new_data_rdy ? n_delay_reg1 : n_delay_reg2;
	wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p4 = new_data_rdy ? n_delay_reg3 : n_delay_reg4;
	wire[`WIDTH_5B - 1:0] p5 = new_data_rdy ? n_delay_reg4 : n_delay_reg5;

	// one block per byte of the 16-bit taps, the high one weighted by 256 at the output
	wire[63:0] sop_hi;
	wire[63:0] sop_lo;
	// the taps that do not fit the four product terms, registered late
	reg[28 - 1:0] soft_reg;

	int_sop_4 sop_hi_inst (.clk(clk), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0),
		.ax({1'b0, p1[15:8]}), .ay(9'd42), .bx({1'b0, p5[15:8]}), .by(9'd42),
		.cx({1'b0, p2[15:8]}), .cy(9'd163), .dx({1'b0, p4[15:8]}), .dy(9'd163),
		.chainin(64'b0), .result(sop_hi), .chainout());
	int_sop_4 sop_lo_inst (.clk(clk), .reset(1'b0), .mode_sigs(12'b0),
		.ax({1'b0, p1[7:0]}), .ay(9'd42), .bx({1'b0, p5[7:0]}), .by(9'd42),
		.cx({1'b0, p2[7:0]}), .cy(9'd163), .dx({1'b0, p4[7:0]}), .dy(9'd163),
		.chainin(64'b0), .result(sop_lo), .chainout());

	assign dout = ({sop_hi[19:0], 8'b0}) + sop_lo[19:0] + soft_reg;

    always @(posedge clk)
    begin
		soft_reg <= (n_delay_reg3 * `COEF3_c) + ((({1'b0, din}) + ({1'b0, n_delay_reg6})) * `COEF0_c);
		if (new_data_rdy == 1'b1)
		begin
			n_delay_reg1 <= din;
			n_delay_reg2 <= n_delay_reg1;
			n_delay_reg3 <= n_delay_reg2;
			n_delay_reg4 <= n_delay_reg3;
			n_delay_reg5 <= n_delay_reg4;
			n_delay_reg6 <= n_delay_reg5;
		
			output_data_ready <= 1'b1;

		end
		else
		begin
			output_data_ready <= 1'b0;
		end
	end
endmodule

Driving `reset` from the design's own `reset` would be\nactively wrong: stereovision2's top-level `reset` is active low, resets only `video_state`,\n`tm3_sram_adsp`, `horiz` and `vert` (stereovision2.v:203), and the testbench pulses it mid-run\n(`resets_random`, RESET_RATE 64), while the filter pipelines it would clear never reset in the\noriginal.\n\n**How to apply:** `.reset(1'b0)` on every block, and check the sim summary line\n`x on dut only: 0` to confirm the X really flushed. See [[local-equiv-harness]] for the local sim.\n"

Task

You are the acceptance reviewer. You did not plan or write this edit. Check the edit against the approved plan, the block's contract and the correctness rules.

The block
  • primitive to instantiate: int_sop_4 (precision INT9)
  • computes: out = ax*ay + bx*by + cx*cy + dx*dy + chainin
  • input ports: clk[1] (clock), reset[1], mode_sigs[12], ax[9], ay[9], bx[9], by[9], cx[9], cy[9], dx[9], dy[9], chainin[64]
  • output ports: result[64], chainout[64]
  • arithmetic: the block reads each operand port as an unsigned number, and its result is unsigned. An operand narrower than its port is zero-extended to the port width. The result wraps at 64 bits: a value past the result width keeps its low 64 bits (modulo 2^64), with no saturation and no flag.
  • registers: on clk, the block registers its operands (ax, ay, bx, by, cx, cy, dx, dy) at one clock edge and result at the next, with the arithmetic between the two registers: operands applied before clock edge k appear in result after edge k+1, 2 cycles later. The block has no clock enable and no path around either register. chainin is registered at the block's entry like an operand and reaches result 2 cycles after it is applied. chainout is combinational from the input registers: it carries the value result loads at the next clock edge, one cycle before result shows it.
  • reset: reset is synchronous and active high: at a clock edge that samples it high it clears every register of the block (the operand registers, the chainin register and the result register) to 0, and the block loads again at the next edge that samples it low.
  • power-up: every register of the block is unknown until the first clear by reset; no register of the block has an initial value, and a rewrite may not rely on one.
  • tie-off: chainin = 0 when the block is not chained (a dedicated chain input: only another block's chainout or a constant may drive it); mode_sigs = 0 always (the architecture gives the port no meaning for this mode).
  • connections: connect every input port, by the port names above; a product-term port the rewrite does not use is tied to 0. chainout reaches only the next block's chainin, through a dedicated connection to the block directly below it in the column; it has no connection to general routing, so nothing else may read it.

What this revision changes against the kept candidate

The kept candidate's period, 4.71829 ns at seed 1, is one stage in my_fir: delay-line
flip-flop -> the new_data_rdy next-state mux -> the 9-bit folding adder -> a block's bx
pin (0.060 + 2.221 + 0.153 + 0.792 + 0.266 + 1.209 + 0.019). It has three routing hops
because two soft cells stand between the register and the block. The mux cannot be removed:
the block needs its operands one cycle before the original registered the sum, so the operand
is the delay line's next state, which depends on new_data_rdy and on din of that same
cycle and therefore cannot be a register output (the testbench drives vidin_new_data high
on consecutive cycles, so the shift can land on the very edge that would have to be
predicted). The folding adder can be removed: the block has its own four multipliers, so a
symmetric tap pair can take two product terms with the same coefficient on ay/by instead
of one term fed by a soft adder. That costs product terms, so the taps that no longer fit are
moved out of the block into one registered late term per instance - which is free of the mux,
because at the edge where the output is formed the delay registers already hold exactly the
samples that term needs.

This keeps 126 blocks and 126 tiles, removes the four 9-bit folding adders per my_fir
instance, and leaves each my_fir block fed by register -> mux -> block: two hops,
0.060 + 2.221 + 0.153 + 1.209 + 0.019 = 3.66 ns with this design's own measured wire and mux
numbers. The late term is two soft adder levels deep, 0.060 + 1.419 + 1.069 + 1.069 + 0.019 =
3.64 ns; a 2-level soft stage of this shape already exists in the kept candidate (f1's
q0_reg) and is under 4.718 there. STAGE_NS 3.9 is the estimate with some margin for the
fltr_compute folding-adder stage (register -> 9-bit adder -> block, 0.060 + 1.419 + 0.266 +
1.209 + 0.019 = 2.97 ns at the median wire, 3.75 ns if its wires are as long as the ones on
the measured path).

Why the timing is sound (the same argument the kept candidate rests on)

Call the edge at which the m-th shift happens (new_data_rdy sampled high) edge k. Before
edge k the delay line holds the six samples s[m-1..m-6] and din carries s[m]; the original
loads dout <= sum(c_i * s[m-i]) at edge k, and h_fltr captures it at edge k+1 under
my_fir_rdy (stereovision2.v:523-554), which is output_data_ready and is high exactly in
the interval (k, k+1). So dout only has to be right in that interval; it is a wire here and
free-running otherwise, as in the kept candidate.

  • Block terms: the operands are the mux outputs p_i sampled at edge k-1, which are the line
    state after edge k-1 = the state before edge k = s[m-1..m-6]. The block registers them at
    edge k-1 and loads result at edge k, so result carries those products in (k, k+1).
  • Late terms: they are registered at edge k from din (= s[m]) and from the delay registers
    themselves (n_delay_reg_i = s[m-i] before edge k), so they are valid in (k, k+1) too. No
    mux is needed for them, which is what makes this split free.

Unsigned, no wrap: every coefficient is positive and the largest full sum is
65535 * 525 = 3.44e7 < 2^28, so the 28-bit dout never wraps, and
sum = 256 * sum(c_i * tap_i[15:8]) + sum(c_i * tap_i[7:0]) exactly. Each block's four
products are at most 4 * 255 * 255 = 260100 < 2^18, well inside result[19:0].

Converted and left, by module
  • fltr_compute_f1/f2/f3/h1/h2/h3/h4 (46 candidates, 6 instances each): all converted, one
    block per instance, exactly as in the kept candidate. The three symmetric tap pairs fold
    (the folding adder stays here: its stage is 2.97 ns, well under the slowest, and unfolding
    would need seven products and so two blocks per instance, +42 tiles).
  • my_fir_f1 (7 candidates): 1487$155, 1489$159, 1491$163, 1492$165 converted (taps 1, 3, 5,
    6, coefficients 101, 235, 101, 29). Left: 1486$154 (tap 0, din, the sample of the current
    cycle - it is only available one cycle after a block would have to take it, so it can never
    be in a block) and 1488$157, 1490$161 (taps 2 and 4, coefficient 15). Those two are left
    because f1's outer coefficient 29 needs two adder levels on din alone; putting the cheap
    15 pair outside keeps both late registers at two levels, while putting 235 or 29*(din+tap6)
    outside would make the late stage three or four levels and slower than the stage it
    replaces.
  • my_fir_f2, my_fir_h2 (7 each): 1543$170, 1544$172, 1546$176, 1547$178 and 1717$211,
    1718$213, 1720$217, 1721$219 converted (taps 1, 2, 4, 5; 42, 163, 163, 42). Left: tap 0
    (din, as above), tap 3 (255) and tap 6 (4); 255*tap3 is one subtract and 4*(din+tap6) is
    one add and a shift, so the late register is two levels.
  • my_fir_f3, my_fir_h1, my_fir_h3, my_fir_h4 (6 each): the four middle taps converted
    (1603$185/1604$187/1605$189/1606$191, 1662$198/1663$200/1664$202/1665$204,
    1776$226/1777$228/1778$230/1779$232, 1834$239/1835$241/1836$243/1837$245). Left: tap 0
    (din) and tap 6, which share the small outer coefficient (12, 15, 9, 9) and go into one
    two-level late register. These filters have no tap 3 (coefficient 0), so all six remaining
    taps are covered by four block products plus the one late pair.

No candidate is left because it could not be rewritten; the ones left are left because they
are the cheapest terms to compute outside and keeping them outside is what removes the
folding adder from the critical stage.

Blocks, tiles, chains

126 blocks: 42 fltr_compute instances x 1, 42 my_fir instances x 2. Each takes a DSP tile
alone, so the design uses 126 DSP tiles, against 224 in the baseline and 126 in the kept
candidate. No block drives another: chainout is left unconnected everywhere and chainin
is tied to 0. Chaining is impossible in my_fir - a chained block would have to be fed one
edge earlier than the block it drives, which would require the delay line's state two shifts
ahead, i.e. new_data_rdy of a cycle that has not arrived - so the longest series of blocks
in any stage is one, and the longest block-internal stage is 0.060 + 2.140 + 0.019 =
2.219 ns, below the 3.9 ns stage this rewrite leaves.

Soft logic that leaves, and which stage it leaves
  • Leaves the slowest stage: the four 9-bit folding adders in each my_fir instance (168
    adders, 1512 adder bits over the design). They stood between the delay-line mux and the
    block's operand pins; that stage was the slowest at 4.71829 ns and loses one cell and one
    routing hop, becoming register -> mux -> block.
  • Leaves nothing else: the 96 next-state muxes per my_fir instance stay (they are the
    delay line's own enable logic and pack with its flip-flops), and fltr_compute's three
    folding adders stay in a 2.97 ns stage that is not the slowest.
  • Added soft logic, all in stages that are not the slowest after the change: per my_fir
    instance one or two late registers (one 16-bit add and one constant-multiply add, two
    levels, about 3.64 ns) and, for f1 only, one more term in the output sum (the output sum
    stays two levels: block result clock-to-Q 0.060 + 0.96 wire + 1.069 + 1.069 + 0.019 =
    3.18 ns). Net cell count is about even with the kept candidate - the removed folding adders
    pay for the added late arithmetic - so area stays near 5.87e7 and the gain is the period.
Register stages, per converted region, before and after
  • fltr_compute (all 46): before, din -> q1..q7 (edge k) -> d_out_tmp (edge k+1) -> dout
    (edge k+2): the products are registered 1 stage before their sum, 3 stages in all. After,
    din -> block operand registers (edge k) -> block result (edge k+1) -> dout (edge k+2):
    still 3 stages, the block's two registers standing where q and d_out_tmp stood. The
    overflow-correction bits are pipelined 2 stages to meet result in the same interval.
  • my_fir (all 28): before, the taps were read combinationally and dout was registered at
    edge k: 0 register stages between the products and their sum, 1 stage from tap to output.
    After, the taps are read one cycle earlier through the next-state mux and pass the block's
    operand register (edge k-1) and result register (edge k), and dout is a wire: 2 stages
    from the mux, 1 register stage from the delay-line registers to the value h_fltr captures
    at edge k+1, unchanged. The terms left outside keep exactly the original single stage (they
    are registered at edge k from din and the delay registers).

DESIGN_CHANGE: fltr_compute_f2 and fltr_compute_h2 are instantiated with identical
coefficients and the identical din in all three v_fltr modules (stereovision2.v:825 and
828, and the same pair in v_fltr_496x7 and v_fltr_316x7), so vidin_out_f2 and
vidin_out_h2 are equal on every cycle; one of the two instances could be deleted and its
consumer wired to the other. That would drop 6 blocks (126 -> 120 tiles, about 5% of the used
logic area) at no cost in delay. For the same reason my_fir_f1 and my_fir_h1 see the same
din (vidin_in_f2 and vidin_in_h2), so their six-deep 16-bit delay lines and next-state
muxes are duplicates and could be shared: about 1150 more BLEs over the design. Neither is
part of a rewrite onto the block, so this plan leaves both in place.

The DESIGN_CHANGE paragraph said the duplicate f2/h2 and f1/h1 instances stay; they are untouched.

Ports. All 21 instances connect all 14 ports by name (.clk .reset .mode_sigs .ax .ay .bx .by .cx .cy .dx .dy .chainin .result .chainout); chainin = 64'b0, mode_sigs = 12'b0, unused product terms tied to 9'b0, chainout unconnected everywhere, so nothing reads it.

Terms and arithmetic. Every original tap is accounted for: fltr_compute folding is exact because each unfolded product is < 2^16 (no bit‑16 sign extension in the folded pairs); the only products that set bit 16 are f1 q4 (din[31:24]*277, ≥65536 at 237 — 236·277=65372, 237·277=65649), f3 q3/q5 (*364, threshold 181 — 180·364=65520, 181·364=65884) and h4 q4 (*324, threshold 203 — 202·324=65448, 203·324=65772); each is corrected by subtracting ovf·2^17 in the 20‑bit d_out_tmp, which reproduces the original's sign‑extended sum mod 2^20. f2/h2/h1/h3 need no correction, and none is added. Every block sum fits result[19:0] (max 287130 for f3), and each my_fir byte sum ≤ 239700 < 2^20, so 256·sop_hi + sop_lo + soft is the exact filter sum, below 2^28 (max 65535·673).

Registers/timing. fltr_compute: operands register at edge k, result at k+1, dout at k+2 — the same three stages as q→d_out_tmp→dout; ovf_q/ovf_d pipeline the correction to meet result in the same interval. my_fir: p_i sampled at edge k−1 equals the delay-line state after k−1 = the state before edge k, so result in (k,k+1) carries exactly the terms the original loaded at edge k; soft_reg/q0_reg/mid_reg register the remaining taps at edge k from din and n_delay_reg* before edge k. dout becoming a free-running wire is safe: its only reader is stereovision2.v:525-553, gated by my_fir_rdy = output_data_ready, high exactly in (k,k+1).

Reset/power-up. .reset(1'b0) on all 126 blocks; the filters have no reset in the original, so no clear must be reproduced, and the block and added registers (ovf_q, ovf_d, soft_reg, q0_reg, mid_reg) are loaded unconditionally every edge, flushing X in ≤2 cycles with no initial-value dependence. The run's mid-run reset introduces no new X (x on dut only: 0).

3	// Ports: clk, reset, mode_sigs[12], ax, ay, bx, by, cx, cy, dx, dy [9 each], chainin[64] in;
4	// result[64], chainout[64] out. mode_sigs is not read.
5	// Registers (the arch's annotation read literally, decision 2026-10-16): every input is registered
6	// at the block's entry at one clock edge (the eight operands and chainin alike); the
7	// products and their sum are formed from those registers and loaded into result at the next edge.
8	// Cycles: every operand and chainin to result 2. chainout is combinational from the input
9	// registers: the sum result loads at the next edge unless that edge clears it (1 cycle from the
10	// inputs).
11	// Reset: synchronous, active high (2026-10-17: the arch's annotation does not distinguish a reset
12	// register from a clear sampled by the registers themselves): at a clock edge that samples it high
13	// every register of the block (operand registers, chainin register, result) is cleared to 0; the block
14	// loads again at the next edge that samples it low. No register has an initial value: every one is
15	// X until the first clear.
16	module int_sop_4 (
17	    input clk,
18	    input reset,
19	    input [11:0] mode_sigs,
20	    input [8:0] ax, input [8:0] ay,
21	    input [8:0] bx, input [8:0] by,
22	    input [8:0] cx, input [8:0] cy,
23	    input [8:0] dx, input [8:0] dy,
24	    input [63:0] chainin,
25	    output reg [63:0] result,
26	    output [63:0] chainout
27	);
28	
29	    // stage 1: the input registers
30	    reg [8:0]  ax_reg, ay_reg, bx_reg, by_reg, cx_reg, cy_reg, dx_reg, dy_reg;
31	    reg [63:0] chainin_reg;
32	
33	    // combinational middle: the four products and their sum, from the registers
34	    wire [17:0] prod_a = ax_reg * ay_reg;                        // 9x9 -> 18, exact
35	    wire [17:0] prod_b = bx_reg * by_reg;
36	    wire [17:0] prod_c = cx_reg * cy_reg;
37	    wire [17:0] prod_d = dx_reg * dy_reg;
38	    wire [63:0] sum    = prod_a + prod_b + prod_c + prod_d + chainin_reg;   // modulo 2^64
39	
40	    always @(posedge clk) begin
41	        if (reset) begin
42	            result <= 0;
43	            ax_reg <= 0; ay_reg <= 0; bx_reg <= 0; by_reg <= 0;
44	            cx_reg <= 0; cy_reg <= 0; dx_reg <= 0; dy_reg <= 0; chainin_reg <= 0;
45	        end
46	        else begin
47	            ax_reg <= ax; ay_reg <= ay; bx_reg <= bx; by_reg <= by;
48	            cx_reg <= cx; cy_reg <= cy; dx_reg <= dx; dy_reg <= dy; chainin_reg <= chainin;
49	            result <= sum;                                       // stage 2
50	        end
51	    end
52	
53	    assign chainout = sum;                                  // the sum of the input registers
54	
55	endmodule

1	---
2	name: sv2-int-sop-4-rewrite
3	description: "Why int_sop_4's reset is tied to 0 in the stereovision2 rewrite, despite the \"registers unknown until the first clear\" wording"
4	metadata:
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: 76ab6f4c-a94c-4b96-b34a-61d708087003
8	  modified: 2026-10-24T01:59:15.283Z
9	---
10	
11	In the /work hard-block rewrites (stereovision2 onto `int_sop_4`), tie the block's `reset` to 0.
12	
13	**Why:** the contract's "every register of the block is unknown until the first clear by `reset`"
14	reads as if a reset pulse were mandatory, but `sim_reference/int_sop_4.v` loads every operand
15	register and `result` unconditionally on each edge where `reset` is low, so the power-up X flushes
16	out in 2 cycles — well before `tb_equiv_sv2_top.v` starts comparing (8 reset cycles + 80 lead-in,
17	`cmp` is still 0 during the reset phase). Driving `reset` from the design's own `reset` would be
18	actively wrong: stereovision2's top-level `reset` is active low, resets only `video_state`,
19	`tm3_sram_adsp`, `horiz` and `vert` (stereovision2.v:203), and the testbench pulses it mid-run
20	(`resets_random`, RESET_RATE 64), while the filter pipelines it would clear never reset in the
21	original.
22	
23	**How to apply:** `.reset(1'b0)` on every block, and check the sim summary line
24	`x on dut only: 0` to confirm the X really flushed. See [[local-equiv-harness]] for the local sim.

layout koios_small · used area 9.73358e+07 · critical path 11.6069 ns · wirelength 436921 · area x delay x wirelength (delay register to register, 2026-10-20) 4.93619e+14 (read from entry; median per term over the entry's seed runs (its seed_medians; seeds lists them))

The objective is area x delay x wirelength (delay register to register, 2026-10-20): VPR's total used logic block area (I/Os and empty grid tiles excluded) times the critical path times the total routed wirelength. Each term is the median over the loop's seeds; the product is the product of the medians. Beside every product stand the ratios against the baseline, A/A0 (area), D/D0 (critical path), W/W0 (wirelength) and their product, so the normalization can be read off. After each measured rewrite, the planner is given every measurement so far and asked for a revision. A revision is built and checked like the first rewrite, and the lowest product is kept, a later rewrite having to beat it by more than 9.41%. The loop stops when the planner declines to revise, when a revision does not lower the best product by more than 9.41%, when a revision fails its checks, or when 9 revisions have been made.

"A/A0 · D/D0 · W/W0" are the rewrite's medians over the baseline's, whose product is the "vs baseline" change plus one. "vs previous" is against the rewrite measured before this one. "Path 1 ends in" is read from the rewrite's own timing report and netlist: the constant coefficients on the block (or plain multiply) that path 1 passes through, matched against the constants each module of the edited RTL multiplies by; two modules that share a coefficient set are both named, and the hover text gives the element and its constants. Verification comes from verification.yaml in the run dir when one was written; the loop itself does not run the equivalence checks. Its label is proven when the LEC closed, simulation under assumption when the simulation passed without a closed proof and the plan stated a bound it rests on, simulation only when it stated none; the hover text gives the simulation and LEC results and the stated bounds.
